## S21 — This week: every league's matchup, live, with the swing matchups

**User-visible effect.** A **This week** card at the top of the Dashboard's League Command Center (under Sync All /
Optimize All, above the league cards), from the owner's sleeper-weekly-recap skill:
- **Header** (it folds to this line, remembered): "Week 7", your W-L as it stands across every head-to-head Sleeper
  matchup, "N still live", a **Provisional** chip (amber) until every game of the week is final, then **Final**, and
  **Refresh**.
- **Splits:** "Paid 4–2 · Free 5–4" (or, until a league is marked paid, a hint to mark them) and "Redraft 3–2 · Dynasty
  6–4", with "(keeper counts with redraft)" when a keeper league is in it. Guillotine leagues are redraft (owner's note:
  a chopped league is a redraft league of a specific kind, like Best Ball), but have no W-L of their own.
- **Still in play:** the swing matchups, most uncertain first, each with both scores, the margin, "**38% to win**" from
  the Matchup Simulator's math, and the live players on each side ("You: Justin Jefferson WR", "Them: nobody left").
- **Effectively decided: 11 (8 W, 3 L)** on one line ("Done" once every game is final).
- **All leagues:** one line per league: W / L / T, the name ("$" if paid), "vs Opponent" (plus "median: 4th of 12
  (above)" in a league that also plays the median, "Best Ball"), your points–theirs and the margin, right-aligned.
- **Notes:** a guillotine league's place ("Chop Shop · Guillotine (no opponent): 98.4, 7th of 10 alive, 4.2 above the
  lowest · 3 live", or "lowest of 10 alive, 1.2 behind the next team", or "your team has been chopped"); leagues with
  no matchup this week; manual leagues ("2 manual leagues: no Sleeper matchup to show"); and "Couldn't load from
  Sleeper: X. Tap Refresh to try again." for a league whose fetch failed, with every other league still shown.
- Before the week's first kickoff it reads "Week 7 starts Thu 8:15 PM" and lists each opponent without scores.
- **Reorder** on the League Command Center has a **"$ Paid"** switch per Sleeper league; a paid league shows a "$" badge
  on its card and in This week.
- **Roster tab:** under the league name, your record ("5–2"), "Points for 3rd of 12 (812.4)" and "Points against 9th of
  12 (760.1)", as of the last sync (shown after a league's next sync; hidden for manual leagues and before anyone has
  played).

**Owner's decisions (asked before building).**
1. Where: a **Dashboard card that folds**, above the league cards.
2. Paid vs free: a **"Paid league" switch in Reorder mode**, saved on the league; plus the owner's idea of a **"$" badge**
   (shown on the league card and in This week, at every width).
3. Ranking swings: the **Simulator's win chance**, shown as a percent ("I like the interconnectedness of features").
   The skill's rule of thumb still decides what counts as in play; the percent orders them.
4. Refresh: **when the Dashboard opens plus a Refresh button, no timer** (run it before SNF, before MNF, after MNF).
5. Season records: **not on each line; on the Roster tab instead**, next to the league name, with points for and
   against ranks (built here, the owner's long-standing ask).
6. Image export: **not now, but wanted**; the owner also wants an **Export on the Roster tab**. Both noted under "Open
   follow-ups" in docs/TESTING.md.

**What changed, and where.**
- `js/mls/week/scoreboard.js` (new, no app state): the skill's rules. `starterState` (live / done / dead: live until his
  team's game is `post`; bye, no team or Out (`SIM_EXCLUDE_STATUSES`) is dead), `reachOf` (QB 20, RB/WR 15, TE/K/DEF 8,
  less what he has scored), `sideSummary` (Best Ball counts live bench players, the best `starters.length` reaches),
  `classifyMatchup` (done when nobody is live; decided when the trailing side has nobody live, or its reach is short of
  a gap of 25+; otherwise a swing), `medianPlace`, `guillotinePlace`, `summarize`, `swingOrder` (the underdog's chance,
  min(p, 100 − p), highest first; then the smaller gap), and the sync helpers `teamNamesFrom`, `playsMedian`,
  `isGuillotine`, `seasonRecord`, `ordinal`.
- `js/mls/week/thisWeek.js` (new): the card. `refreshThisWeek` fetches `GET /v1/league/<id>/matchups/<week>` for each
  Sleeper league, five at a time, for Sleeper's `week` (`State.currentNflWeek`), after the scoreboard, projections and
  player map; it reuses anything fetched in the last 2 minutes unless forced (Refresh) and fetches a league added since.
  Draws scores first, then adds win chances. Your entry by `league.rosterId`, the opponent by `matchup_id`; points are
  `custom_points` when Sleeper sets it, else `points`. Guillotine: `league.guillotine`, or, for a league synced before
  S21 whose meta didn't load, every roster having its own `matchup_id`.
- `js/mls/sim/winChance.js` (new): the Simulator's inputs gathered as `runMatchupSim` does (actual points once a
  player's game has kicked off, projection plus his history's spread before, Doubtful/Out/IR left out) and run through
  its own `sim/worker.js` instance (so it never answers the Lineup tab's Simulator run), returning each matchup's win
  chance. One difference from the Simulator card: a player whose game has kicked off counts even with no game history
  (the card drops him, losing real points). No change to the math.
- The cache: `State.lineupActualPoints[leagueId]` (the Lineup tab's, `js/mls/lineup/gameInfo.js`) now holds the whole
  matchups response and `finalTeams` (every team final at fetch time) in place of the lineup-only `finalKey`;
  `storeLeagueMatchups` writes it for both the Lineup tab and the card. In memory only, as before.
- `js/mls/leagues/sync.js`: the league object gains `teamNames` ({ roster_id: display name }), `medianMatch`,
  `guillotine`, `record` (from the rosters a sync already fetches) and `paid` (carried over like `rosRankingSetId`).
  Backup/Restore copies `mls_leagues` whole, so `paid` round-trips. A league synced before S21 reads its names and
  flags from Sleeper once per visit (league, users, rosters) until its next sync.
- `js/mls/render/leagueCards.js`: "$ Paid" in Reorder (`toggleLeaguePaid`), the "$" badge on the name, and the card's
  load when the Dashboard is shown (redrawn otherwise). `js/mls/state.js`: loads it once Sleeper's week is known.
- `js/mls/render/roster.js`, `lineup/index.html`: `#rosterRecord`. `#thisWeekCard` in the Command Center.
- `js/mls/badges.js` + `js/mls/legend.js`: `paidBadgeMarkup`, `weekResultMarkup` (W/L/T), `weekStatusMarkup`
  (Provisional/Final), each with a legend line. `css/mls.css`: the card, the badge, the record.
- `js/shared/storage/keys.js`: `mls_this_week_folded` ('1' while folded). `sw.js`: the three new modules in
  `PRECACHE_ASSETS`, `CACHE_NAME` v2.8.100 → v2.8.101. CHANGELOG lines under Lineup Strategist.

**What I found in the owner's leagues (Sleeper API, week 7).** LOOG - Chop Shop is `settings.type` 3; every roster has
its own `matchup_id`; chopped teams stay in the matchups with 0 points and no players (and 0 wins in the rosters). Eight
leagues have `league_average_match` 1. `week` and `leg` agreed (7).

**Measured.** 21 leagues, every one a swing, CPU slowed 4x (local server, so no network latency): from a reload, the
scores were up in about 1.1 s and all 21 win chances 0.1–0.45 s after (the week stats come from IndexedDB after the
first visit). The Dashboard never waits on the Simulator.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/weekScoreboard.test.mjs` (the rules, median, guillotine, Best Ball, splits, order, record).
`tests/mls-this-week.spec.mjs` (both widths): Sunday of week 2 with ESPN's scoreboard stubbed, two Sleeper leagues
(the generator now writes "Second Fixture League", id …021, dynasty, and the mid-Sunday and final matchups): the

whose matchups fail is named and the other still shows; a guillotine league and a median league; one line per league

Strategist's "Something went wrong loading the app" banner (`SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 's'`): that preview was
still serving commit b339938's `js/mls/week/thisWeek.js`. JS and CSS are served from the service worker's cache first
and refreshed in the background (sw.js), and the fix commit kept the same `CACHE_NAME`, so a browser that had cached
the broken file could keep serving it. `CACHE_NAME` v2.8.101 → v2.8.102, so every browser that saw the bad build takes
a fresh copy. Lesson for later cards: bump `CACHE_NAME` again in a fix commit that follows a broken push, even on the
same branch.

### S21, user-hat pass 5 (a replayed Sunday afternoon) and round 12

To see a Sunday afternoon with real leagues, week 6 was replayed with the late-afternoon, Sunday-night and Monday games
set back to "not started" and those players' points removed (a review script, not in the repo).

- **The Simulator during games** (owner: "make the change in the Simulator itself"). A player whose game had kicked
  off counted as his points so far with no spread, as if final. During games that made win chances badly wrong, and
  the round-5 rule (under 0.5% or over 99.5% counts as decided) could take a live matchup out of "Still in play".
  Found when the replay counted the late games as kicked off: every late player froze on 0 and all 19 matchups read
  as decided. Now:
  - `gameShareLeft(status)` (sim/stats.js): the share of a game still to play, from ESPN's quarter and clock (1
    before, 0 final, half at halftime or without a clock, overtime against a full game).
  - `parseEspnScoreboard` stores it per team (`left`); `gameShareLeftFor(team)` (lineup/gameInfo.js) reads it.
  - `getPlayerVarianceProfile`'s new `shareLeft`: points so far plus his usual distribution scaled to the share left
    (spread by its square root); `floorAt` so the worker never draws below what he has scored; Boom/Bust from the
    model around the live mean; `inProgress` and `actualSoFar` for the Simulator card ("(3 so far)").
  - Used by the Simulator card (sim/matchup.js, sim/ui.js) and the Scoreboard's win chances (sim/winChance.js).
  - The "settled by the Simulator" rule waits until nobody on either side is mid-game; a chance that rounds to 0 or
    100 meanwhile reads "<1%" / ">99%".
- **A shorter in-play list, with the chance on the tiles** (owner: combine (a) and (b)): "Still in play" lists the five
  most uncertain, with "Show all N" (in memory, until the week changes); every in-play tile shows its win chance
  next to the margin.
- **"Effectively decided" only beside something still open** (owner agreed): with nothing in play or too early, it
  repeated the record.
- Also from the pass: a tile's foot is two lines, the result and how it stands, then the league's context (median,
  guillotine place), instead of one wrapping line that left a "·" at the end of a line on desktop; the in-play list's
  margin sits by the league's name instead of at the far edge of a wide screen.

**User-visible effect.** Only in dynasty and keeper leagues (`getPowerLeagueKind(league) === 'dynasty'`); redraft
leagues look and work exactly as before.
- **Roster tab, ROS card.** The set drop-down's label reads "Dynasty rankings for this league" (was "Ranking Set for
  this League", which redraft leagues keep). Under its "Used in…" row a new **Season rankings** picker (with an (i)
  tooltip): "None (use your dynasty rankings)" plus every saved ROS set. With a Season set chosen the card header reads
  "Dynasty: <set> · Season: <set>", and "Season rankings in N of M dynasty and keeper leagues · Choose leagues…" opens the
  existing league picker for the Season slot (only dynasty and keeper leagues listed; uncheck to send one back to its
  dynasty set). With the slot empty and a redraft league on a ROS set, the row offers it: "Your redraft leagues use
  <set>. **Use it here**"; after the tap, a dialog asks "Also use "<set>" in the N other dynasty and keeper leagues
  without Season rankings?" (**Use in all N** / **Just this league**). A set's "Used in N of M leagues" line counts Season
  use too: "(k as Season)".
- **Power Rankings.** With a Season set: **Start** (and so the Contender / Retool / Rebuild labels, the Your Team card and
  the Roster tab's power strip) is scored by the Season set; **Ovr** and the QB/RB/WR/TE columns by the dynasty set;
  **Future** by the dynasty set × Sleeper age (or dynasty Market Consensus, unchanged). The Ovr tooltip lists the rooms
  by the dynasty set then. A new note names the sets: "Start (and so the labels) uses your Season rankings (<set>). Ovr
  and the position columns use your dynasty rankings (<set>). Future uses your dynasty rankings (<set>)." A new switch,
  **I'm competing this year** ("Ovr and position rooms use your Season rankings."), shown only with a Season set and your
  own rankings as the source, moves Ovr and the rooms to Season (Future stays dynasty); saved per league. A Contender with
  the switch off whose dynasty set is 14+ days old (when the ROS freshness label turns amber) gets a note: "Your dynasty
  rankings are 18 days old. Competing this year? Turn on I'm competing this year to read your rooms by your Season
  rankings."
- **The same numbers elsewhere:** the All My Leagues search's power ranks and the Trade Analyzer's "Power Rankings after
  the trade" (S14) read each league the same way (its line says "by your dynasty rankings (Start by your Season
  rankings)"). The Trade Analyzer's values ("Your rankings") are unchanged: that's S24.
- **Lineup.** With no Weekly set, the lineup is optimized by the Season set (was the dynasty set), its rank badges and
  rank-change chips follow it, and the Command Center's "not in …" reason names "your Season rankings". The Waiver Wire's
  Starting Lineup check uses the same. A Season change changes the league's rankings stamp, so the lineup re-optimizes
  when next opened.
- **Waiver Wire Assistant.** Rank By gets **Season Rank** in a league with a Season set (hidden elsewhere); rows read
  "Season Pos / Season Overall". The Dashboard's best-available switch (the same setting) gets a **Season** button while
  any league has a Season set: dynasty leagues use their Season set, the others their ROS rankings.
- With no Season set chosen, everything is exactly as before.

**Owner's decisions (asked before building).**
1. Names: **Dynasty** for today's ROS slot in these leagues, **Season** for the new one.
2. No Season set: **as today**, plus an **offer** of the ROS set the redraft leagues use, and after accepting, one
   question to use it in every other dynasty and keeper league without one. (The owner found my first version, an offer
   with a separate "Choose leagues…", more than needed.)
3. Where Season is used in this card: **all three** (Power Rankings' Start and labels, the lineup's fallback, Rank By).
4. **No site-wide toggle**: a default per place (lineups, waivers and Start ask "now"; Future asks "later"); switches only
   where both answers help (S24's Trade Analyzer and Roster rows).
5. Bulk assigning: **in the existing league picker dialog**.
6. Ovr and the position columns (my question; the card named only Start): **dynasty by default**, because dynasty
   rankings are updated about monthly and the long view matters unless you're competing. The owner asked for a
   "Competing / Rebuilding" toggle in dynasty language; I suggested one switch, **"I'm competing this year"**, because a
   two-sided switch would label every team "Rebuilding" until flipped, plus the two-week hint. Built as suggested; the
   owner can change the wording.

**What changed and where.**
- `js/mls/rankings/season.js` (new, pure, in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`): the slot (`seasonRankingSetId`, `hasSeasonSlot`,
  `seasonSetFor`), the resolver `resolveSeasonRankings` (Season set, else the league's ROS rankings as they are),
  `seasonStamp`, `roomsUseSeason` (`powerCompeting`), `setUsage`, `seasonOffer`, `leaguesWithoutSeason`.
- `js/mls/leagues/sync.js`: `getLeagueSeasonRankings(league)`, `activeSeasonRankings()` (looked up on each call, so no ROS
  change can leave it stale; State gains no field), `activePowerRankings()` ({ start, rooms, future }); the rankings
  stamp appends `|season:<id>@<updatedAt>` only when a Season set is chosen (every other league's stamp is unchanged, so
  no needless re-optimizing after the update); a sync carries `seasonRankingSetId` and `powerCompeting` over like
  `rosRankingSetId`. `js/mls/main.js` re-exports the three; modules that `state.js` loads early (`lineup/gameInfo.js`,
  `scout/waivers.js`, the power and trade modules) import them from `main.js`, as with `getLeagueRankings` (importing
  `leagues/sync.js` directly from `gameInfo.js` broke the load order: State used before it was set).
- `js/mls/power/shared.js`: `computePositionalPower(league, rankings, { startRankings, futureRankings })`. `rankings`
  scores Ovr and the rooms, `startRankings` the lineup split (Start, bench), `futureRankings` the age mode's values. Both
  default to `rankings`, which gives identical numbers (unit-tested). `team.startSeparate` marks a split.
- `js/mls/power/rosterCard.js`: the sources, the switch (`setPowerCompeting`), the notes (`seasonSourceText`,
  `competingHint`). `power/allLeagues.js`, `trade/lineupSection.js`: the same split.
- `js/mls/rankings/sets.js`: `populateSeasonPicker`, `onSeasonSetChange`, `openSeasonSetLeagues`, `useSeasonOffer`;
  `renderLeaguePicker` / `assignSetToLeagues` / `openLeaguePickerDialog` take `slot: 'season'`; the header and the
  "Used in" row name Season use; **deleting a set clears every Season slot pointing at it** (the confirm says how many
  leagues go back to their dynasty rankings). Rename needed nothing new: every place looks the set up by id when it draws.
- `js/mls/render/lineup.js`, `js/mls/lineup/gameInfo.js`, `js/mls/scout/waivers.js` (Season Rank as a ROS-shaped basis,
  `scan.season`), `js/mls/scout/topAvailable.js`, `js/mls/scout/bestAvailable.js`, `js/mls/rankings/moveChips.js`
  (`rankMoveChip('season', …)`).
- `lineup/index.html` (the Season row, the switch, the Season Rank option), `css/mls.css` (`.mls-season-row`,
  `.mls-season-offer`; a `[hidden]` rule, since those rows set `display`), `js/mls/main.js` (actions:
  `onSeasonSetChange`, `openSeasonSetLeagues`, `useSeasonOffer`, `setPowerCompeting`).
- `sw.js`: `season.js` in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`; `CACHE_NAME` v2.8.100 → v2.8.101. CHANGELOG line under Lineup Strategist.
- **No new storage key.** Both fields live on the league objects (`mls_leagues`), so Backup / Restore keeps them (spec)
  and Factory Reset clears them with the leagues. No new badge, chip or pill, so no legend line.

**Market source (asked to note, not build).** Power Rankings' Market Consensus option scores every column, Start

- `competingSuggestion(label, record, { starterRank })` in `js/mls/power/directionLabels.js` (pure, beside the labels):
  Contender → competing (losing and points for in the bottom half → retool); Retool → retool (winning and points for
  in the top half → competing; losing and bottom half → rebuilding); Rebuild → rebuilding (winning and top half →
  retool). Winning / losing = above / below .500 with ties as halves; "top half" = points-for rank ≤ teams ÷ 2, "bottom
  half" > (teams + 1) ÷ 2, so the middle team of an odd league is neither. Points against is named only with a losing
  record and a points-against rank in the top third ("with the most / 2nd-most points against"). Under 4 games, a null
  record (before anyone has played, guillotine leagues) or a missing one (synced before S21: "sync this league to add
  your record"), the label alone. In median leagues the record includes the median game, as Sleeper's standings do.

  it never flips the switch. The Guide's step 4 and the CHANGELOG line describe it. It's text, not a badge, so no
  legend line.

### S23, round 10: uploading into In-Season, and League style for keeper leagues (owner: "build both here")

**Owner's questions.** (1) How does someone with only dynasty leagues get an In-Season set? Before this round they
couldn't without a trap: the In-Season picker and the offer need a saved ROS set other than the league's dynasty set,
and making one meant uploading into the dynasty slot. (2) Keeper leagues counted as dynasty everywhere, but many play
like redraft. The owner chose: build both here; keep dynasty as keeper leagues' default; check Sleeper's keeper count;
put a note on the Roster tab saying where to change the style.

**1. Upload or Auto-Fetch into: Dynasty | In-Season.** Round 8's line under the two pickers is now a switch (dynasty and
keeper leagues only), with a caption: "Updates your dynasty set, …" / "Saves a new In-Season set for this league.
Auto-Fetch gets FantasyCalc's redraft values." / "Replaces your In-Season set, …". On In-Season, an upload (through the
usual preview, which says "…, as this league's In-Season rankings" and offers other leagues' In-Season slots) or an
Auto-Fetch saves a new set or replaces the In-Season one and assigns it to the In-Season slot; the dynasty set,
`State.rosRankings` and the flat fallback keys are untouched. Auto-Fetch then asks FantasyCalc for redraft values
(`isDynasty=false`) whatever the shared League Type says, and names the set "FantasyCalc Redraft – <date>". The switch
lives in memory and goes back to Dynasty after each save and on a league switch, so a later upload can't quietly fill
the wrong slot. With no redraft set to offer, the empty In-Season row says "No redraft set to use yet. **Get
FantasyCalc's redraft values**", which does the In-Season Auto-Fetch in one tap; a new In-Season set then gets the
offer's "Also use it in …?" (`offerSeasonToOthers`, shared with the offer). Code: `rosUploadIntoSeason`,
`setRosUploadSlot`, `resolveSeasonTarget`, `saveSeasonSet`, `updateUploadTarget` (`rankings/sets.js`);
`resolveRankingsTarget` / `saveRankingsAsSet` hand off to them; `rankings/uploadPreview.js`, `rankings/rosFetch.js`.

**2. League style (keeper leagues).** Sleeper's `settings.max_keepers`, checked on the owner's 21 leagues: it's 1 in
every league type (redraft, dynasty, guillotine, best ball), so it only means something in keeper leagues (type 1);
the owner's one keeper league keeps 3. A sync now stores it as `league.maxKeepers` (keeper leagues only).
`league.keeperStyle` ('redraft', or absent = dynasty, the default) is set on the Setup tab's Active League Requirements
card ("League style": Plays like dynasty / Plays like redraft, an (i), and "Sleeper: each team keeps up to 3 players.
Leagues that keep this few often play more like redraft." when it's 3 or fewer) and carried over by a sync.
`getPowerLeagueKind` reads it, so everything that asks "is this dynasty?" follows: Power Rankings' labels and Future,
the Trade Analyzer's draft picks and Future, "To make it fair", the market type, and the In-Season slot (hidden, its
set kept but ignored, while redraft). The Roster tab's Power Rankings card has a note for keeper leagues: "Keeper league
(each team keeps up to 3), treated as dynasty here. **Change League style**" (to the Setup tab, scrolled and focused).
No new storage key: both fields are on the league.

## S22 — This week's MVPs and LVPs across your leagues

**User-visible effect.** On the **Scoreboard** tab, under the league tiles (once a game has kicked off), a section
**"MVPs & LVPs"**, folded to one line until you tap it ("4 MVPs · 2 LVPs" and Provisional / Final; open or folded is
remembered). Opened:
- A short line: how many Sleeper leagues count, what Own means, and the Boom / Bust lines in use.
- **MVPs** (Player | Own | Boomed | Pts | Started): "Ja'Marr Chase WR · 100% (2) · 2 of 2 · 20.0–25.0 · 2 of 2". On
  phones Started drops to a second line under the name ("Started 2 of 2") rather than the table scrolling sideways.
- **LVPs** (Player | Own | Started | Pts).
- Five rows each, then "Show all N" (until the week changes).
- A **Partial boom** line when someone boomed in under half the leagues that own him; then one line each, when there is
  something to say: **Started zeros** ("0.0 usually means he didn't play; the app can't check that"), **Dead weight**,
  **Still open** (games not final: could land on either list), **Worst benchings**, players **not in Sleeper's player
  map** (with any Boom-level score called out), and a **Best Ball** note when a listed player sat on a Best Ball bench.
- "Provisional until the week's last game is final", gone once it is.
- **Advanced Settings** on the Dashboard gains **"MVP / LVP Lines"**: Boom at / Bust under for QB, RB, WR and TE (your
  lines as defaults), Save and Reset to Defaults, with a note that they're separate from the Simulator's boom/bust
  chances. Errors show under the form and mark the field (both positive, Boom above Bust); nothing is saved then.
- The Guide's Scoreboard item gains a line for MVPs & LVPs.

**Owner's decisions (asked before building).**
1. Where: **a section of the Scoreboard tab** (S21's view became a tab in its round 6), **folded until opened**.
2. Lines: **editable in Advanced Settings**, the owner's as defaults, with the note about the Simulator; **no K / DEF**.
3. Ownership: **Sleeper leagues only**, so every percent has points behind it. Manual leagues are mentioned in the
   intro line, not counted.
4. Rows before "Show all": **5 and 5**.

**Rules as built** (`js/mls/week/playerRecap.js`, my readings where the card left room):
- Leagues counted (N): every Sleeper league whose matchups loaded this week with your entry holding players. A league
  whose fetch failed, or a chopped guillotine team, isn't in N.
- Points: Sleeper's `players_points` in each league (its own scoring); a rostered player with none counts 0.
- MVP: at or above Boom in at least one league, whatever his game's state (a Boom mid-game stays a Boom). Ranked by
  leagues boomed, then ownership, then his best score. **Partial boom**: boomed in fewer than half the leagues that own
  him (the card's TE: 1 of 6). Partial booms go after every full one (by boom count alone, a 1-of-6 TE would tie a
  1-of-1 player and win on ownership, which the card says should rank low), and get the call-out line.
- LVP: his team's game is `post`, he's under Bust in at least one league, and he isn't an MVP. Ranked by leagues where
  he started and busted, then ownership. Without game states (ESPN didn't load) nobody is final, so no LVPs.
- Started zeros: 0.0 as a starter in a league, game final. Dead weight: owned in at least max(2, 20% of N) leagues,
  benched in all of them, 0.0 everywhere, game final. Still open: game not final, not already an MVP; by ownership.
- Worst benchings: Sleeper's matchups don't say which slot each starter fills (the league object keeps only slot counts),
  so "the starter in that slot" is **your lowest-scoring starter at the bench player's position** in that league: a
  same-position swap is always legal. Counted when the bench player reached Boom and the starter, whose game is final
  (or who was on a bye), scored at least 10 less. Never in Best Ball. Top 3 by the gap.
- Left out: byes (`getByeWeek`), no team, K, DEF (team-code ids are skipped quietly, not "unresolved").

**What changed, and where.**
- `js/mls/week/playerRecap.js` (new, no app state): `buildPlayerRecap`, `DEFAULT_LINES`, `normalizeLines`,
  `validateLines`, `ownText`, `pointsRange`.
- `js/mls/week/recapLines.js` (new): the lines' storage and the Settings form (`getRecapLines`, `applyRecapLinesToUI`,
  `saveRecapLines`, `resetRecapLines`). Called from `init.js` (fill the form) and `main.js` (data-actions).
- `js/mls/week/thisWeek.js`: `recapInput` (each league's own entry from `State.lineupActualPoints`, S21's fetch; no
  second request), `recapHTML` / `recapTable`, `togglePlayerRecap`, `showAllRecap`. Drawn by `renderScoreboard` after
  the tiles once the week has started.
- `lineup/index.html`: the "MVP / LVP Lines" accordion in Advanced Settings; the Guide's line. `css/mls.css`: the section
  (each table is one grid with subgrid rows, so columns fit their numbers; 760px reading width) and the form.
- `js/shared/storage/keys.js`: `mls_recap_lines` (only while different from the defaults; Reset removes it) and
  `mls_player_recap_open` ('1' while open). Both `mls_`, so Backup / Restore and Factory Reset take them.
- `sw.js`: the two modules in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`, `CACHE_NAME` v2.8.111 → v2.8.112. CHANGELOG: two lines under Lineup
  Strategist.
- No new badge: the section reuses S21's Provisional / Final pill (already in the legend).

**Tests.** `tests/unit/playerRecap.test.mjs` (13): ownership, boom count then ownership, the partial-boom TE (1 of 6, a
TE-premium 15.7), LVP order by started busts, bye / no team / K / DEF left out, a 0.0 starter on a final team as a
started zero (and one still to play as still open), still open mid-game, dead weight, worst benchings (Best Ball
skipped, small gaps and unfinished starters skipped), unresolved ids, custom lines, empty input, validation.
`tests/mls-mvp-lvp.spec.mjs` (both widths) with S21's fixtures: folded line and counts, both tables' cells, dead weight
and still open, the open state surviving a reload; a started zero, a starter LVP and a worst benching (Second Fixture

### S22, round 2: the owner's review (real leagues, week 8): Started %, slot order, the share image

The owner looked at the section with their 19 Sleeper leagues (screenshot: 21 MVPs, 97 LVPs) and asked for three things.
I asked three questions first; the owner took my suggestion each time.

1. **MVPs need Started, not just Own** ("Eli Raridon may be owned in 6 leagues, but I didn't start him anywhere. So he
   isn't really an MVP"). Decisions: **an MVP must have boomed in a league where you started him**; in Best Ball any boom
   counts, since its lineup picks itself. MVPs rank by those started booms, then all booms, then ownership. A player who
   boomed only on your bench leaves the table for a line of his own: **"Boomed on your bench: Eli Raridon TE (15.4–17.6
   in 6 leagues). Not MVPs: you didn't start them where they boomed."** **Started reads as a share of the leagues that own
   him**, "67% (4)", in both tables (Own stays the share of all your leagues). Bench boomers aren't LVPs or "still open"
   either. (`startedBoomed`, `startedPct`, `benchBooms`, `startedText` in week/playerRecap.js.)
2. **Each league's slot order, saved at sync** (owner: useful later for the Lineup tab too). `league.starterSlots`:
   Sleeper's `roster_positions` without BN, in order (`leagues/sync.js`); a matchup's `starters` follow it, so
   `starters[i]` filled `starterSlots[i]`. Rebuilt on every sync, so nothing to carry over; Backup / Restore copies it
   with the league. A league synced before this has none until its next sync. Used now by **worst benchings**: the
   benched player is compared with the lowest starter in any slot that takes his position (`SLEEPER_SLOT_POSITIONS`: FLEX,
   SUPER_FLEX, REC_FLEX, WRRB_FLEX), so a WR benched for an RB in the FLEX counts, and the line names the slot ("over
   CeeDee Lamb (FLEX) 8.0"). Without slots, or when they don't match the starters, the same-position rule from round 1.
3. **The Scoreboard image** (the open follow-up from S21), as **a summary, a "TL;DR"** (owner: 21 tiles would be too
   much to share). Decision: **headline plus highlights**, at any number of leagues: "My Lineup Strategist · Week 7
   Recap" and Provisional / Final; the record ("Record 12–7 · 2 still live", or too early to call); the splits; **Still
   in play**: up to 3, most uncertain first, with the win chance and the margin; **Biggest win** and **Worst loss** among
   the matchups already settled (every one once the week is final); the top 3 **MVPs** ("boomed 6 of 6", points) and
   **LVPs** ("started 4 of 4", points); "19 Sleeper leagues · provisional until the last game is final ·
   mydraftstrategist.com". 480px wide, like Export Trade. **Export** sits by Refresh in the Scoreboard's header (an icon on
   phones), only once there are scores. The HTML comes from `js/mls/week/shareImage.js` (pure, unit-tested);
   `scoreboardSummary` and `exportScoreboard` in week/thisWeek.js gather the data and draw it from html2canvas's clone of
   `#thisWeekCard` with proportional digits; the page doesn't change. Saved as `Week_7_Recap_Lineup_Strategist.png`.
   The "Wanted by the owner" line for it in docs/TESTING.md is removed; the Roster tab's Export stays there.

Also: the Guide's line says what Started means, the new MVP rule and Export; CHANGELOG lines updated; `sw.js` precaches
`shareImage.js` (CACHE_NAME stays v2.8.112, this branch's one bump, still above main's).

### S22, round 8: one Boom / Bust verdict per player, on half-PPR points

The owner's question after round 6: one line is easier to reach in full PPR than half PPR (RB/WR/TE), and in 6-point
passing TD leagues for QBs. I offered (A) judge each player once on one scale, (B) move each league's line by its
scoring (rules of thumb), (C) convert each league's points with the player's stat line. The owner asked for A and B in
plain terms (same score for everyone with one line, versus each league's own score with a different estimated line),
then chose **A, on half PPR** ("a more common format, and a good in-between of Standard and Full PPR").

- **The verdict.** `buildPlayerRecap` takes `verdict: { points }`, each player's points on the chosen scale; Boom / Bust
  is decided once from it, so `boomed` / `busted` are all his leagues or none, and `startedBoomed` / `startedBusted` are
  his starts. MVPs: boomed and started somewhere, ranked by starts, then ownership, then the verdict's points; LVPs: busted,
  started, game final, ranked by starts, then ownership, then the lower points. Dead weight is a verdict of 0; a bench
  boom (and so a worst benching) is a verdict boom, the gap still in that league's points. Partial booms no longer arise
  (they only came from scoring differences). A player missing from the stats scored 0 (he hasn't played).
- **The numbers.** Sleeper's week stats (`/stats/nfl/regular/<season>/<week>`, the endpoint the Simulator's history uses)
  carry `pts_half_ppr`, `pts_ppr` and `pts_std` (Sleeper's default 4-point passing TDs). `getLiveWeekStats`
  (js/shared/api/sleeperStats.js) fetches the current week uncached (`getWeekStats` keeps a week for good once stored, fine
  for finished weeks only), with the matchups on every load and Refresh. Owner's example: Eli Raridon was 15.35–17.6 in
  his leagues (TE premium) and 13.1 in half PPR.
- **Settings.** MVP / LVP Lines has "Judge on": Half PPR (default), Full PPR, Standard, saved as `scale` in the same
  `mls_recap_lines` object (no new key); Reset returns to Half PPR.
- **Tables.** MVPs and LVPs share one shape: Player | Own | Half PPR (the verdict's points) | Pts (each league's own
  scoring, the range) | Started; on phones Started moves under the name in both. This is the round-6 "Busted" idea in the
  form A gives it: LaPorta above Metcalf now shows why (Metcalf's 7.6s were his leagues' scoring).
- **Fallback.** If the stats don't load, each league's own points decide as before round 8, the third column reads
  Boomed / Busted counts, and a line says "Week stats didn't load".
- **The (i), the image, the Guide.** The tip explains the scale column and Pts; the image's rows read "started 2 of 2 ·
  25.0" with "Boom / Bust on Half PPR points" in the footer; the Guide's MVPs & LVPs item says how players are judged.
- **Fixtures.** The generator writes `stats-2026-2.json` (half-PPR points set apart from the leagues' own: Lamb 25.0 in
  Second Fixture League is 18.0) and `stats-2026-2-final.json` (Jefferson's 20.5).

**Tests.** Unit (448): the verdict overrides each league's scoring (and without it, each league's own), LVP order by
starts and lower points, a player missing from the stats, no partial booms, a verdict bench boom as a worst benching,
the scale in normalize / validate; the image's "started X of N" and footer. Spec (28): the half-PPR column and numbers,
Lamb not an MVP on his 25.0, Bowers an LVP on 4.0, the bench boom's line, Jefferson after the final, the Full PPR switch
(Allen 25.0 → 26.0), the fallback when the stats fail, both tables' Started on a second line on phones.

## S21 follow-up: the Week Recap lasts through Tuesday (owner's bug report, Tuesday after week 7)

Owner: "MNF finished less than an hour ago, and already Week 7 Recap is gone, and now week 8 projections are showing.
Users should see a Week's Recap at least through Tuesday. Most apps transition to the next week on Wednesday, when
waivers typically run." Sleeper's state endpoint answered `"week": 8, "display_week": 7` at 04:13 UTC Tuesday: `week`
moves on when Monday night's game ends, `display_week` is the week Sleeper's own app shows.

- `State.recapNflWeek` (js/mls/state.js): `display_week` when it's a number from 1 to `week`, else `week`. Only the
  Week Recap (`weekCtx` in js/mls/week/thisWeek.js: the Scoreboard tab, the Dashboard's line, the Lineup strip, S22's
  MVPs and LVPs) reads it. Lineups, projections, kickoffs, locks and the Simulator stay on `currentNflWeek`, so Tuesday
  shows the new week's lineups beside last week's recap.
- When the recap week isn't the current week, the card loads that week the way `?week=` did (its own ESPN scoreboard
  and projections) and keeps its matchups in its own cache (`other.matchups`). Before, the address's week wrote into
  `State.lineupActualPoints`, the Lineup tab's cache for the current week, and with the recap a week behind every
  Tuesday the two tabs would have kept replacing each other's entries.
- Test: `mls-this-week.spec.mjs`, "Tuesday: the recap stays on last week…" (state week 3, display_week 2): Week 2
  Recap, Final, no ?week= notice, week 2's scoreboard asked for, the Lineup tab's cache never holds week 2. It fails
  on main ("Week 3 Recap").
- Checked with the owner's real leagues at 04:30 UTC Tuesday: "Week 7 Recap · Record 7–13 · Final" on the Scoreboard
  and the Dashboard, the Lineup strip on week 7, the app's week 8.
- Open: whether `display_week` changes on Wednesday morning or with waivers (Sleeper doesn't document it); either is
  what the owner asked for.

## S23 follow-up: the Scout tab after a league switch made on it (owner's bug report)

Owner: on the Scout tab, switching from a redraft league to a dynasty one kept Rank By at "Weekly Rank / ROS Rank", with
no Dynasty or In-Season choice, and the reverse kept the dynasty choices, until they went to another tab and back.
"Please check that everything else on the Scout tab changes based on league correctly."

- Cause: S23 made Rank By's choices depend on the league, but `applyWaiverScanSettingsToUI` (js/mls/scout/waivers.js)
  ran only at start-up, on a setting change and when the Scout tab was shown (`onScoutTabShown`). `applyActiveLeague`
  (js/mls/leagues/sync.js) redrew the Top Available list but not the controls. It calls
  `applyWaiverScanSettingsToUI` now, before the results are redrawn (imported through main.js, as sync.js's other
  calls are).
- The check: a probe switched leagues on the Scout tab in each Waiver Wire mode (Top Available, Auto-Find, Check a
  List), both ways, and compared everything visible on the tab (text, each select's value and choices, inputs,
  classes) with what leaving the tab and coming back showed. Rank By (its choices, and the wide-group class) was the
  only difference. Trade Analyzer is already cleared on a switch (`clearLeagueScopedResults`), and the Market Consensus
  settings already follow the league (`applyLeagueDefaultsToMarketSettings`).
- Market Disconnect: a tab switch doesn't redraw it either, so it was checked by hand. Its report stayed up after a
  switch with the old league's "Rostered by" and Free Agent lines and the old league's ROS ranks. A report on screen is

  compares with the league, not the drop-downs, so a drop-down changed by hand doesn't hide it. Shown under the Market

### S24, round 2: "nothing works after restoring a backup" (owner's report), and a chip for players one set leaves out

**The report.** Testing the branch in an Incognito window: restore a backup, re-sync, open the Trade Analyzer and the
Roster tab: no S24 at all. After a Factory Reset, importing the leagues by username and setting the In-Season, dynasty
and Weekly rankings again, everything showed.

**What I found.** I loaded the owner's backup (Oct 27) into this branch three ways: written straight into storage,
through the real Restore (file input and confirm), and Restore followed by a real re-sync against Sleeper (both the
Setup tab's username import and Sync All). In every case each dynasty league with an In-Season set showed both ranks,
the chips, the sort switch and two verdicts (34 rows on Managers of the Round Table and on Draft Scouts of America, at
both widths). The data was intact: 14 dynasty leagues pointing at "ROS Redraft" as In-Season, and their dynasty sets.
My first guess was the league the backup reopens on (League of Ordinary Gentlemen, the one keeper league with no
In-Season set). **The owner corrected me: the issue was in May the Receptions Be With You**, a dynasty league with both
sets. I then reproduced their steps on that league exactly: Restore through the file input, a switch to it from the
header drop-down, the Setup tab's username sync, Sync All, and a reload. At every step it showed 29 rows with both
ranks, the source line, and the Trade Analyzer's two verdicts (`tradeSeasonSet()` set). So with this branch's files and
this backup the feature works; **the cause is not found yet**. What's different in the owner's browser is still open
(see the questions to the owner below). The likeliest cause is old files served after the deploy, since the S23 line
"Ranks by your dynasty rankings (…)" would then still show; not confirmed.

Still worth keeping from this round, since current users can have a dynasty or keeper league without an In-Season set
and see nothing new there:
- **A line where the features would be** (dynasty and keeper leagues with a dynasty set and no In-Season set):
  - Roster tab, above the list: "No In-Season rankings in this league, so these are your dynasty ranks alone. Your
    redraft leagues use **ROS Redraft**: **Use it here** to see this season's ranks beside them." (S23's own offer and
    its "Also use it in…" question; without a redraft set to offer: "Choose In-Season rankings in the card above…").
  - Trade Analyzer, under the verdict: "Choose In-Season rankings for this league on the Roster tab to get a
    this-season verdict beside your dynasty one." On screen only (Export Trade leaves it out).
  - Redraft leagues: nothing. `render/roster.js`, `trade/verdict.js`, `css/mls.css` (`.mls-roster-season-hint`,
    `.mls-trade-season-hint`).
- The service worker serves scripts stale-while-revalidate: a page loaded while an older version was cached runs the
  old scripts once, and the next load gets the new ones (`CACHE_NAME` bumped).

**Answered:** the rows showed one "Ovr | Pos" badge each, main's markup, so the browser ran cached older scripts; on

### S24, round 7: superflex QB prices for a 1QB-looking In-Season set (owner: "automatic, with the note")

**The question.** Round 6 found Power Rankings' Start reads the In-Season set's overall ranks too, so a 1QB set
undervalues QBs there as it did in trades. The owner asked whether Start could go by position. Answer: position rank
alone can't choose a superflex starter or set a value (QB5 and RB5 aren't worth the same), so something has to say
what the Nth QB is worth in this format. I offered (a) every In-Season player priced by position on the dynasty set's
scale, (b) only where the In-Season set's format looks different, (c) leave it. The owner leaned (b): (a) would carry
the dynasty set's long-term pricing (young RBs and WRs over aging QBs and TEs) into "now" in every league, making 1QB
dynasty and 1QB redraft the same. The owner asked about a toggle; I recommended automatic with a note (a toggle is hard
to explain, the format is a fact the app can check, and S23's answer was a default per place). Owner: "Build it that way,
automatic with the note." TE premium left out (a TEP list is hard to tell from a plain one).

**What it does.** In a superflex league (a SFLEX slot or two QB slots) whose In-Season set looks 1QB (fewer than 8 QBs in
its top 50, round 6's check) and whose dynasty set doesn't: each QB keeps his In-Season order among QBs and takes the
overall rank the dynasty set gives that QB spot (In-Season QB3 = the dynasty set's QB3); past the dynasty set's last QB,
its last rank plus the average gap. Other positions, 1QB leagues, redraft leagues and the Long-term side are unchanged.

## S26 — A navigation rail on wider screens (Material 3)

**User-visible effect.** Both apps' tab bar now takes one of three layouts, by window width (Material 3's window
sizes):
- **Phones (under 600px):** the bottom bar as before. Lineup Strategist's phone screens are pixel-identical to main's.
- **Tablets (600 to 839px):** the bottom bar with each icon beside its name, the tabs centred, labels whole.
- **Computers (840px and wider):** a 96px **navigation rail** at the left edge, each tab's icon with its name under it.
  The green marker slides up and down beside the active tab. The **menu button moves from the header to the top of
  the rail**, and opens the **expanded rail** over the page with a dimmed backdrop: every tab by name, then **"More"**
  (the Guide, T-Score, the other app), the feedback form and Ko-fi. It closes when you choose an item, press Escape or
  click outside, and focus goes back to the menu button. The header, every tab, toasts and dialogs sit clear of the rail.
- **Draft Strategist's Setup is now the Dashboard**, the first tab in its bar and rail on every screen (with Lineup
  Strategist's grid icon), so its bar has four tabs: Dashboard, Tracker, Team, Board. Text that said "the Setup tab"
  says "the Dashboard" (empty states' "Go to Dashboard", two Sleeper toasts, the Guide, the shortcuts list). The
  checklist keeps its name, "Setup Progress".

**The owner's answers** (asked with screenshots of today and a mock-up at 1280, 1024, 768 and 375px):
1. **Breakpoints: Material 3's** (rail from 840px, side-by-side items from 600px). The app's 768px breakpoint stays
   where it is: it lays out the page content (cards, tables, slide vs. fade transitions), not the bar, and moving it
   would change tablet layouts across both apps.
2. **The menu goes into the rail** (Material 3: an expanded rail opens from a menu icon at its top), with two states,
   collapsed and expanded. The collapsed rail holds the menu button and the tabs; **the Guide, T-Score and the other app
   show only when it's expanded**, under "More". **Draft Strategist's Setup becomes "Dashboard"** and a tab in the bar and
   the rail, for uniformity (owner: its Setup may be redone like Lineup Strategist's walkthrough with several drafts in one
   place, which would make it more of a dashboard; the name can change later). The owner accepted the side effect: its
   phone bar changes too.
3. **The green sliding marker**, not Material 3's pill (owner likes the animation).
4. **Both apps together**, through the shared CSS in css/base.css.
5. **Widths from Material 3's current rail spec**: 96px collapsed; expanded 280px (in M3's 220–360, and the drawer's
   existing width, which the Ko-fi button needs).
- A. **Modal, not standard, for the expanded rail** (my recommendation, owner said go): it adds places you visit once
  rather than navigate between, the pages are information-dense (M3's case for modal), and a standard rail would reflow
  every page and need a saved setting per app. A standard rail from 1600px is an open follow-up (docs/TESTING.md).
- C. **Phones and tablets keep the header's menu button and drawer as they are.** D. **Ko-fi stays at the foot of the
  expanded rail.**

**How it's built.**
- **One set of tab buttons**, laid out three ways by CSS (css/base.css, "NAVIGATION RAIL AND TABLET BAR", at the end of
  the file, and `body.has-nav-bar` on the two apps' pages so T-Score, which shares base.css, is untouched). `showTab`,
  swipes, number keys, the drawer and the screen-reader announcement don't know which layout shows.
- The `<nav class="nav-bar">` moved **before `<main>`** in both pages, so the rail comes after the header in reading
  order (it's fixed-position, so phones look the same). The rail's menu button is the bar's first child, `hamburger-btn
  nav-rail-menu`, not a `.nav-btn`, so the tab code and the marker never count it; it's hidden below 840px and the
  header's is hidden from 840px. `toggleDrawer` (MLS) and `toggleMenu` (MDS) set `aria-expanded` on both buttons.
- **The expanded rail is the existing drawer**, restyled from 840px: its logo row hides, its close button (a 48px
  collapse icon, `.icon-collapse`, in place of the ✕) sits exactly where the rail's menu button is, and a
  `.menu-section-label` "More" (hidden below 840px, `aria-hidden`) heads the Guide, T-Score and the other app.
- **The marker** (`placeTabMarker`, js/shared/ui/viewTransition.js) measures along whichever way the bar runs (the
  bar's `flex-direction`), setting left/width on the bar or top/height on the rail, and clearing the other pair so the
  stylesheet's 3px thickness applies. Same numbers as before on the bottom bar. The ResizeObserver re-measures when the
  bar turns into the rail. Its transition covers top and height too; Reduce Motion still keeps it still.
- **`aria-current="page"`** on the active tab button (both apps, the drawer's too). Lineup Strategist's drawer now marks
  the current tab however it was reached (it only followed drawer taps and swipes before), since on computers it's the
  expanded rail.
- **Draft Board:** its full-width breakout on desktop used `100vw`, which ran under the rail; it now subtracts
  `--rail-inset` (96px beside the rail, 0 otherwise).
- S16's transitions keep naming the bar (`vt-nav`), so the rail stays still while the page fades.

### S26, round 2: a Material 3 review of the rail, and the owner's answers

The owner asked for a "Material 3 Review" of the rail. m3.material.io renders with JavaScript (a plain fetch got only
the page title), so I read its Navigation rail pages (Overview, Guidelines, Specs, Accessibility) and the Navigation
bar's Specs in headless Chromium, and measured the rail at 1280px. **It met** Material 3 on: window sizes (bar under 600,
rail from 840, never both); the leading edge, fixed while scrolling, never hidden; the menu at the top opening the
expanded rail, whose icon turns into a collapse icon in the same spot; secondary destinations under a section header;
a modal expanded rail for information-dense pages; 96px collapsed (M3 Expressive's; the 80px baseline rail is "no longer
recommended") and 280px expanded (220–360); full-width targets; one-word labels; a heavier icon for the active tab (M3's
rule for icons with no filled version) with a bold label in a contrasting color; inactive labels at about 7.5:1; Tab,
Enter and Space; `aria-current`; the focus trap. **Differences the owner chose** (kept): the green sliding bar instead
of M3's pill; a bar, not a rail, on tablets (the rail page: "in medium windows with few destinations, consider using a
navigation bar instead").

**The owner's answers** to the findings, all built:
1. **Labels at 2x text** (a defect): "Dashboard" and "Scoreboard" were cut at the rail's edge and the rail scrolled
   sideways. M3: the full label stays visible up to 2x, wrapping or hyphenating is fine. On the rail, labels may now
   break onto two lines (`overflow-wrap: anywhere; hyphens: auto`, line height in em so the lines grow with the text),
   and the two long ones carry a soft hyphen (`Dash&shy;board`, `Score&shy;board` in the markup) so they break as "Dash- / board"
   (Linux Chromium has no hyphenation dictionary). Invisible at normal size. The Lineup Strategist announcement strips
   the soft hyphen. The marker's ResizeObserver also watches each item now, since bigger text makes an item taller
   without resizing the rail.
2. **The menu uses the tabs' short names, at every width** (owner: phones too): Lineup Strategist's Active Roster,
   Lineup Optimizer, Scout & Waivers, User Guide and T-Score Methodology are now Roster, Lineup, Scout, Guide, T-Score;
   Draft Strategist's Draft Board, User Guide and T-Score Methodology are Board, Guide, T-Score. The other app's link
   keeps its name. (M3: the collapsed and expanded rails "match visually and can transition into each other".)
3. **Arrow keys** (M3: Tab or the arrows move between items): Up/Down/Left/Right move focus to the next or previous item
   in the bar, the rail and the menu's list, wrapping round; Home and End go to the ends. Focus only; Enter or Space
   selects. Ignored with a modifier (Shift+arrows still cycle leagues).
4. **The expanded rail grows out of the rail** (M3: the two transform into each other): from 840px the drawer no longer
   slides in from off-screen; it's revealed from the rail's width outwards (`clip-path`, 0.3s, none with Reduce
   Motion), and its rows' icons sit exactly where the rail's are (36px in; rows 56px apart from 94px down, matching the
   rail's items, which are now 56px apart from 88px with no gap), so only the labels change.
5. **Sizes, Material 3's** (owner: "do it all", phones included; the navigation bar spec gives a 24dp icon, 4dp from icon
   to label, a 64dp bar): 24px icons in the bar, the rail and the menu (were 22px and 20px); 4px from icon to label; 16px
   label line height; the phone bar 64px tall (was 73px: 3px + 56px items + 4px, plus its 1px border); the tablet bar's
   items 56px; the rail's items 56px; the menu's rows 56px with a 14px label (were 47px and 16px); the "More" header 12px
   above, 8px below.
6. **Back closes the menu** (M3: Back dismisses a modal expanded rail): new `js/shared/ui/navMenu.js` (in
   `PRECACHE_ASSETS`). Opening the menu pushes a history entry (same URL and tab, marked `menu`), so Back takes it off
   and closes the menu, leaving the tab and address alone. Closing it any other way (its button, Escape, the backdrop,
   choosing a tab) calls `history.back()` and swallows that pop; a tab chosen from the menu waits for it
   (`toggleDrawer`/`toggleMenu` now return a promise; Draft Strategist's `showTab` closes an open menu first), so Back
   after choosing a tab returns to the tab before, not to the open menu. The module's popstate listener is registered
   before each app's (imported by `js/mls/nav.js` and `js/mds/ui.js`) and stops the app's from seeing the pops it handles.
   Phones' and tablets' menu too (the same drawer).
- Left as is (owner): the feedback form in the expanded rail. Not taken up: dropping the rail's shadow (M3 uses a
  divider, elevation only over sideways-scrolling content).

`CACHE_NAME` v2.8.133 → v2.8.134. Tests (nav-rail.spec.mjs): arrow keys in the rail, the bar and the menu (wrap, Home,
End, focus only); Back at 1280 and 375px (closes the menu and keeps the tab; Escape leaves no entry; Back after choosing a
tab from the menu returns to the tab before; it fails on the round-1 code, where Back switched tab and left the menu
open); labels whole at 2x text with the marker still by the tab; the sizes at 375, 700 and 1280px; the expanded rail's
clip and its icons at the rail's; the short names at 375 and 1280px. Full check: precache OK, 469 unit tests, 617
Playwright passed; only `visual.spec.mjs` fails here (this container's Chromium).

### S26, round 3: a smoother expanding rail

Owner: the expanding rail "appears a bit stuttered". Headless Chromium can't show it (no GPU: 27 even frames either way,
and traces too small to compare), so the fix follows the three causes in the code:
1. **The reveal animated `clip-path`**, which Chromium redraws on the main thread every frame. It's now two opposite
   transforms: the panel slides in from `translateX(96px - 100%)` while its children start `translateX(280px - 96px)` the
   other way, with the same timing, so they cancel: the edge moves out from the rail, the contents stay put. Transforms
   run on the GPU.
2. **The backdrop appeared all at once**: the whole page dimmed and blurred in the first frame while the panel had
   barely moved. It now fades with the menu (`setBackdrop` in js/shared/ui/navMenu.js toggles `.menu-overlay.open`;
   `@starting-style` fades it in from `display: none`; hiding waits for the fade, `pointer-events: none` meanwhile).
   Both apps, every width (phones' backdrop fades too).
3. **The timing**: Material 3's emphasized curve at 300ms put nearly all the movement in the first frames. Now Material 3's
   motion tokens: open 400ms emphasized decelerate `cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1)`, close 200ms emphasized accelerate
   `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15)`; the backdrop 400ms in, 200ms out. Reduce Motion: no transitions.

A filmstrip (frames at 0, 10, 20, 35, 50 and 100% of the animation, before and after) went to the owner. `CACHE_NAME`
v2.8.134 → v2.8.135. Test (nav-rail.spec.mjs, replacing round 2's clip-path check): closed, the panel's right edge is the
rail's; paused halfway, the edge is between 96 and 280px, the icons are already where the rail's are, the backdrop's
opacity is between 0 and 1, and nothing animates but transforms and opacity; open, the edge is at 280px; closing, the
backdrop goes. Screenshots: none show the menu, so the list in round 2 stands (30).

### S26, round 4: Material 3's item heights

Owner: the items "feel scrunched up at the top"; are their heights Material 3's? They weren't. From Material 3's
measurement image (collapsed rail: 96dp wide, items 68dp apart: a 64dp item, then 4dp; inside an item 6dp, the 32dp
indicator round the 24dp icon, 4dp, the 16dp label, 6dp; expanded rows 56dp) and the navigation bar's spec (the same
6/32/4/16/6 in a 64dp bar), round 2 had 56px items with no gap and 4px from icon to label. Without a pill, the indicator's
4dp round the icon becomes space: 10px above the icon, 8px from icon to label, 6px below the label.
- **Rail**: items 64px (`padding: 10px 4px 6px`, 8px icon to label), 4px apart, the first at 92px (icon at 102px).
- **Phone bar**: 64px with the same 10 / 24 / 8 / 16 / 6 (it had 4px from icon to label and 10px below the label).
- **Tablet bar**: 64px (items 60px, 18px above and below the icon), 4px from icon to label (Material 3's for side by
  side).
- **The active icon no longer lifts 2px** (S16's touch, phones and tablets): Material 3 keeps it in place (its heavier
  stroke and color mark it), and the lift took 2px from the space above it.
- **The expanded rail**: its rows stay Material 3's 56px, so they no longer line up with the rail's 68px spacing. They
  start where the rail's items are (each row `translateY(n x 12px)`, `--rail-row` by `:nth-child`) and close up as the
  menu opens, with the same transform timing, so nothing jumps; the first row's icon is at the rail's first (102px).
- **Fix**: Reduce Motion now stops the menu's movement too. Round 3's rule lost to the `.open` rules' higher specificity.

The rail's color: the owner asked whether its lighter navy (the bottom bar's card navy, `rgba(19, 27, 44, 0.85)`) next
to the header's darker page navy (`rgba(10, 14, 23, 0.85)`) is intentional. It isn't a Material 3 choice: the rail kept the
phone bar's background. Material 3 allows either (the container fill is optional; without it, keep a divider). Options
(today's card navy, or the header's navy for the bar and the rail) went to the owner with screenshots; see round 5.

`CACHE_NAME` v2.8.135 → v2.8.136. Tests (nav-rail.spec.mjs): the sizes test measures 10 above the icon, 8 to the label, 6
below in a 64px phone bar; a 64px tablet bar with 4px icon to label; 64px rail items 68px apart; 56px menu rows 56px apart.

that nothing moves or fades with Reduce Motion. Screenshots: the 30 already listed (every PNG of both apps shows the bar).

## F10 — Replace Set: the buttons in reach, and the red box counts every league using the set

From the owner's 2026-10-31 phone screenshot (replacing "ROS Redraft" from How I Met Your Punter).

**User-visible effect.**
- **Pinned buttons.** The shared dialogs are a column: the title, a middle that scrolls, and the button row, which
  stays at the bottom of the window. With content under it the row gets a line and a soft shadow above it (it goes
  away once the middle is scrolled to its end). Before, the whole card scrolled as one block, so on a phone with many
  leagues Cancel and Replace Set sat below the fold behind the whole "Also use this set in" list. Applies to Lineup
  Strategist's upload preview and league picker, Draft Strategist's upload preview, and the shared confirm and prompt
  dialogs (all three pages). Short dialogs measure identical to main, element by element (title, body, each button),
  at 1280×900 and 390×844.
- **Phones.** The card's height follows `dvh` (`85vh` fallback), so the browser's toolbars can't cover the buttons; the
  overlay keeps clear of the notch and home bar (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`, the pages use `viewport-fit=cover`); and with
  the on-screen keyboard up the overlay is fitted to the visible band (`window.visualViewport`), so the prompt's field
  and its buttons stay above the keyboard (iOS Safari and Chrome on Android shrink only the visual viewport, which no
  CSS unit follows).
- **The red box** for a ROS replace now counts the dynasty and keeper leagues using the set as In-Season rankings,
  which change too: "Used by 2 leagues, and as In-Season rankings in 2 dynasty leagues." It also names dynasty-set use
  apart from redraft use. Auto-Fetch's Replace confirm says the same ("It is used by …"). Weekly sets and the
  In-Season upload path (`seasonUseNote`) are unchanged.
- **The "Also use this set in" list** (and "Choose leagues…" for a ROS set): a dynasty league already reading this set
  as In-Season rankings reads "In-Season already · dynasty: Dynasty SF" instead of "Currently: Dynasty SF". Checking it
  still makes the set its dynasty set (unchanged, as the card asked).

**Owner's decisions (asked before building).**
- Red box wording: the proposal, with "dynasty or keeper" spelled out where a keeper league is in a group. So:
  redraft only "Used by 4 leagues." (as before); plus In-Season "Used by 4 leagues, and as In-Season rankings in 2
  dynasty leagues."; a dynasty set "Used as dynasty rankings in 3 dynasty leagues."; mixed "Used by 1 league, and as
  dynasty rankings in 3 dynasty leagues."; all three "Used by 1 league, as dynasty rankings in 1 dynasty league, and
  as In-Season rankings in 1 keeper league." A group of keeper leagues only says "keeper", a mix "dynasty or keeper"
  (my reading of "where a keeper league is among them"). A keeper league played as redraft counts as redraft.
- The pinned row applies at every width (the same dialog everywhere).

**Where.**
- `css/base.css` (modal chrome): `.preview-modal` / `.mds-modal` become a flex column with `max-height: min(85dvh,
  100%)`; new `.preview-body` / `.mds-modal-body` scroll (negative margins with the same padding back, so focus rings
  at the edge aren't clipped and nothing moves); `.is-scrolled-under` on the button row draws the line (a band of
  padding taken back by a negative margin, `--actions-gap` per row, so the buttons don't move when it toggles); the
  overlay's padding respects the safe area. `.mds-prompt-label`'s top margin is 0.25rem: it used to collapse with the
  title's 0.5rem, and inside the body it can't.
- New `js/shared/ui/modalLayout.js` (`watchModal(overlay)`, in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`): toggles `.is-scrolled-under` (scroll,
  ResizeObserver, MutationObserver) and fits the overlay to the visual viewport while a keyboard covers part of the

  `showConfirm` and `showPrompt`.

## S28 — Week Recap: choose the week, and a Competing / Rebuilding split

**User-visible effect.**
- **The Scoreboard's week is a control.** Arrows around the title, "‹ Week 7 Recap ›" (real buttons labelled "Previous
  week" and "Next week"), step back a week at a time to week 1 and forward again to this week's recap; each end's
  arrow is disabled. An earlier week shows its own matchups, scores, tiles, biggest win / worst loss and MVPs & LVPs,
  reads **Final** (no Still in play, no win chances, "Week 6 is over: every result is final." at the foot), and Export
  Recap saves that week's image (`Week_6_Recap_…png`). A week with no matchups in any league says "No matchups in week N
  in your Sleeper leagues." Screen readers hear the week ("Week 6 Recap, final"), focus stays on the arrow (or moves

## M1 — A Material 3 review of the whole site (research)

**What changed.** No app code, CSS or screenshots. New **docs/improvements/material3-review.md** (not served code, so
`PRECACHE_ASSETS` and `CACHE_NAME` stay) with 13 screenshots in **docs/improvements/material3/**: what already meets
Material 3, then 14 ranked, sized proposals, each with what Material 3 says (linked), what the site does now (a
screenshot), the files, the screenshots it would re-take, app by app or site-wide, and overlaps with open cards.

**How.** All 82 m3.material.io pages needed (Guidelines, Specs and Accessibility of 22 components, plus type, color,
elevation, shape, motion, states, layout and contrast) read in headless Chromium the way S26 did; the session's network
allowed it. A throwaway Playwright script (not committed) walked every tab of both apps and T-Score at 375, 768 and
1280px with the fixture data, measuring target sizes, keyboard focus rings, font sizes, transitions, corner radii and text
contrast, and opened the toasts, the confirm and prompt dialogs and the upload preview.

**Main findings.** Navigation (S21, S26), dark surfaces, dialog structure (F10, merged in #212) and Reduce Motion already
meet. Off: controls under 48px on every tab (the Lineup row's swap 30x23 and lock 26x21, Taken / Pick 30px tall, 18px "i"
icons); focus rings are the browser's default on most buttons and faint on text fields; hover lifts the button instead of a
state layer; toasts go after 3.5s, bounce in and sit over open dialogs; selection in chips and segmented buttons is shown
by color only; 35 font sizes in the CSS, nine under 11px on screen; ten different transition curves; a few text colors
under 4.5:1 (T-Score's labels, the injury badge, DEF text).

**Overlaps.** S15 splits into proposal 2 (focus) and 6 (contrast); proposal 1's lineup-row part folds into S32, which
should also offer a modal bottom sheet for the row's extras on phones; proposal 8 (motion tokens) pairs with S18; F10's
pinned buttons are done.

**The owner's picks** (after reading the ranked list): "Do 1+2+3 together, 4+8, 5+12 as suggested. For the rest,
combine where it best makes sense, either because they're related, or because approximate size means they can go in
one session easily enough." All 14 proposals become cards; the next runbook update adds them:

- **M2 = 1 + 2 + 3: touch, focus and feedback** (~25k tok, site-wide, 0 to 4 screenshots). 48px targets, one green
  focus ring (2px on text fields), state layers for hover and press. Replaces S15's focus half. The Lineup row's swap and
  lock spacing goes to S32.
- **M3 = 4 + 8: messages and motion** (~16k tok, site-wide, 0 screenshots). Toasts as snackbars, plus Material 3's
  motion tokens for every transition. Run before S18 so S18 uses the tokens, or in the same stretch, but not alongside it:
  both edit css/base.css's transitions.
- **M4 = 5 + 12: selection controls** (~16k tok, 16 to 18 screenshots). Checks on selected chips and segments (40px
  segments), and switches at Material 3's size with a check. Both apps' Guide legends where a chip's look changes.
- **M5 = 7 + 13: dialogs and form errors** (~20k tok, 0 screenshots). Grouped because both are about telling you what's
  happening where you are: dialog headlines that name the action, a full-screen upload preview on phones, and errors
  under the field in both apps' Sleeper forms.
- **M6 = 6 + 10: contrast, and T-Score's tabs** (~18k tok, ~20 screenshots). Grouped because the contrast failures are
  mostly T-Score's labels and both re-take T-Score's 12 PNGs, so they're re-taken once. Takes S15's contrast half, so
  with M2, **S15 is fully covered and can come off the runbook**.
- **M7 = 9 for T-Score and Draft Strategist: the type scale** (~25k tok, 28 screenshots). The tokens go into
  css/base.css here; T-Score's stylesheet is small, so the two pages fit one session. Checks every tab at 2x text.
- **M8 = 9 for Lineup Strategist** (~20k tok, 14 screenshots). Standalone: the biggest stylesheet (299 of the site's 434 font-size rules) and
  it waits for S32, which redoes the phone rows' text. Uses M7's tokens, so after M7.
- **M9 = 11 + 14: button emphasis and corners** (~20k tok, most screenshots). Grouped because both re-style buttons
  across every screen and both change the identity a little, so the card shows mock-ups and **asks the owner first**
  (which colored buttons lose their fill; 6 to 8px corners). Last, after the type cards, so screenshots are re-taken once
  more at most.

"Before spring" step, one at a time; M8 and M9 with the spring and summer work), each needing M1's branch merged since

### M1, round 2: the rest of Material 3

The owner asked for a second pass "from a different lens": beyond the tangible fixes in round 1, where else could the
rest of Material 3 improve the site's look and feel without changing its identity. Research only.

**What changed.** New **docs/improvements/material3-review-2.md** (linked from the first review) with five more
screenshots in docs/improvements/material3/ (the Dashboard, Lineup, Tracker, Scout and T-Score Top-50 at 1280px). Read
in headless Chromium: the Expressive announcement, the components round 1 skipped (button groups, split button,
toolbars, loading indicator, search, side sheets, FABs, app bars, carousel, navigation drawer) and the Expressive
changes to cards, lists, badges and progress; color roles (surface containers), elevation, shape, motion specs (springs
and their web curves), icons, editorial type; canonical layouts, scaffold, the writing style guide.

**Findings.**
- **Three corrections to written cards**: M3 should use Expressive's web spring curves (spatial ones overshoot a little
  on purpose; round 1 quoted the baseline easing page, which Material 3 now says is no longer maintained), so the
  toast's "no bounce" becomes a smaller, quicker bounce if the owner agrees; M4 should use Expressive's connected button
  group (which replaces segmented buttons: the selected one changes shape and color) and make the site's three looks for
  that control one; M2 can offer Expressive's pressed shape morph (corners tighten) beside the state layer.
- **Nine new proposals (15 to 23)**: the badge legend in a side or bottom sheet instead of a trip to the Guide (and a
  shared sheet S32 can reuse); badges on the navigation (lineups that need you, on the clock); progress and loading
  indicators; two panes on wide screens (the Tracker with your team beside it, and others); surface tones instead of
  boxes in boxes; one or two hero moments; sentence case (fold into M7 and M8); a button group and split button for the
  Lineup card (fold into M9); search bars.
- Looked at and not proposed: FABs, toolbars, carousel, pickers, the abstract shape library, Material Symbols, flexible
  app bars, dynamic color.

**The owner's picks:** "Yes to changing M2, M3, and M4. I want 15-23; group multiple together where it makes sense, and
fold into existing cards if it makes sense at all. Please also feel free to re-order the priority based on estimated
positive impact the change would have. Also, I'm OK making changes mid-season; this season is kind of a Beta
development phase more-so than a fully released product." So:

- **Corrections, all accepted:** M2 offers Expressive's pressed shape morph (corners tighten about 2px) beside the state
  layer; M3 uses Expressive's web curves (spatial ones overshoot a little; the toast's entrance is the owner's call: a
  small bounce or none); M4 becomes Expressive's connected button group, one look for every segmented control on the
  three pages (Lineup Strategist's segments, T-Score's WR / RB pills), with the check optional.
- **Folded into existing cards:** 17 (progress and loading indicators) into **M3** (both are about how the app shows
  it's working, and the loading shape uses M3's motion tokens; M3 grows to ~24k); 23 (search bars) into **M5** (text
  fields; ~26k); 21 (sentence case) into **M7** and **M8**, which re-take the same screenshots anyway (~30k and ~26k);
  22 (button group and Share split button) into **M9**, whose corners (14) moved to M14.
- **New cards:** **M10** navigation badges and hero moments (16 + 20: both rest on "a lineup needs you" and "you're on
  the clock"; ~20k); **M11** the badge legend in a sheet (15; builds the shared sheet, so **S32 now needs M11**; ~12k);
  **M12** two panes on wide screens for Lineup Strategist and **M13** for Draft Strategist (18, one per app; ~20k and
  ~16k); **M14** surface tones and corners (19 + 14: both change every container and the identity a little, so one
  card with mock-ups first; ~25k; M9 now follows it).
- **Order, by expected impact** (owner: changes mid-season are fine, this season is a beta): weeks 10–11 add **M2**
  (felt on every tap) and **M11**; weeks 12–13 add **M10** beside S30, with S32 after M11; the playoffs start with
  **M3**, then S18 on its motion tokens; January **M5** and **M12** beside S25; February–March **M4**, **M6**, **M7**
  one at a time; spring and summer **M13** before draft season, then **M8**, **M14** and **M9**. Runbook updated the
  same day (version 33): those cards, S28 marked merged (#213), S32's need on M11.

## N1 — Research: what notifications would take on this site

**What changed.** `docs/improvements/notifications.md` (new): what each of the three alerts takes with the site open
and with it closed (web push on Cloudflare), a table of alert × open/closed with card counts and risks, the
permission UX, privacy and upkeep, and cited sources. No app file changed: no served code, no `sw.js`, no CSS, so
`CACHE_NAME` is untouched and nothing goes in `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Main findings.**
- Android Chrome only supports `registration.showNotification()` (the constructor throws), so the shared module always
  goes through the service worker; a tap needs a `notificationclick` listener in `sw.js`, which has none today.
- Chrome slows a hidden tab's chained timers to once a minute after 10 s to 5 min hidden and silent, so Draft
  Strategist's 3 s live sync can notice a pick up to ~60 s late. Firefox (budget) and Safari (1 s alignment) are
  milder; Safari needs a real test. Phones pause background pages, so open-site alerts are a computer feature.
- iPhone/iPad: no notifications in a Safari tab; web push only after Add to Home Screen (iOS 16.4+; the manifest is
  already `standalone`).
- Closed-site alerts need a Worker with a Cron Trigger (Pages Functions have no cron), D1 or KV, VAPID keys and a
  Web-Crypto push library. Cron runs once a minute at most; the free plan gives 10 ms CPU per run and 5 cron triggers.
- A server can compute "on the clock" from Sleeper's small draft endpoints. Injury status lives only in Sleeper's
  15 MB player file (once a day, too big for 10 ms CPU), so a closed-site starter alert would miss late scratches.
  Rankings and the recommended lineup are browser-only, so no rankings alert can run closed.
- "Rankings updated" has nothing to alert on: rankings change only when you upload or tap the ROS fetch button, and
  the app already marks Weekly rankings older than 6 days in amber.

**Owner's decision (2026-11-01).** Asked: only while open (recommended), also while closed, or a mix by trigger.
**Answer: C, a mix by trigger.** Starter alerts while the site is open only; "on the clock" while open first, then
also by web push when the site is closed. **N3: dropped**; N2's starter alert gets one line naming leagues whose
Weekly rankings are stale (`getFreshness(…, 6)`, the league cards' rule).

**The N cards after N1** (the runbook's prompts are older: where they differ, this entry wins):
- **N2 — Shared notification module and the Lineup Strategist starter alert (site open).** As the runbook's card,
  plus: always `registration.showNotification()`; add `notificationclick` to `sw.js` (focus or open the right page; a
  middle-number `CACHE_NAME` bump); toast and title-flash fallbacks; the stale-Weekly-rankings line. Its asks stay
  (Sleeper lineup or recommended, minutes before kickoff, Questionable), plus one: refresh injury statuses once before
  each kickoff window (the 15 MB file, at most ~3 times on a Sunday) or use the last sync. Help text: works while
  `/lineup/` is open on a computer.
- **N3 — dropped.** Tick it done in the runbook with this note.
- **N4 — Draft Strategist on the clock (site open).** As the runbook's card, plus: test whether a timer in a dedicated
  Web Worker escapes Chrome's once-a-minute throttle (keep the 3 s timing either way); say how much clock is left from
  the draft's `settings.pick_timer` and the last pick's time; help text says a hidden tab may notice a pick up to a
  minute late. Needs N2.
- **N5 (new) — Web push setup.** Needs N4. A Worker in its own folder (e.g. `workers/notify/`, `wrangler.toml`, the
  repo's first deployed-with-wrangler code), D1 for subscriptions (push endpoint and keys, Sleeper user ID, draft
  IDs, toggles, sent markers), subscribe/unsubscribe Pages Functions beside `functions/api/ffc/`, a Web-Crypto push
  library, the VAPID private key as a Worker secret. **Asks you:** to create the Cloudflare resources and keys (the
  session writes the steps, doesn't create them), free plan or $5/month. First re-check Cloudflare's limits on the
  live pages (this session could only see them through search results).
- **N6 (new) — Push in `sw.js` and Draft Strategist's Settings.** Needs N5. A `push` listener; an "Also alert me when
  Draft Strategist is closed" toggle that subscribes (iPhone: explains Add to Home Screen); a privacy note in the Guide
  (what's stored and how to delete it); Factory Reset and turning the toggle off unsubscribe; storage keys via
  `keys.js`.
- **N7 (new) — The draft poller.** Needs N6. The Worker's cron (once a minute) checks only subscribed drafts that are
  live, alerts N picks ahead and on the clock once each, removes expired subscriptions (404/410), and stops when the
  draft completes. Tests with a stubbed Sleeper, push service and clock.
- Not planned: a closed-site starter alert (injury data too stale); revisit only if a better injury source turns up.

**Left over.** Device tests the research couldn't settle: Safari's hidden-tab timing, and whether a Worker timer
escapes Chrome's throttle (N4 checks it). The runbook page was updated the same day (version 35): N2 and N4
rewritten as above, N3 marked covered by N2, N5–N7 added, and the order and Notifications track adjusted.
