  1 still in play" and "Root for 7 · Against 7 · Both 2".
- **Who to root for**: every starter in this week's Sleeper matchups, from the matchups the Scoreboard already loads.
  - On top, the players in 2 or more of your matchups, in three groups: **Root for** (green, thumbs up), **Against you**
    (red, thumbs down) and **Both sides** (amber, crossing arrows). They sit side by side from 900px and stack on phones.
    Each row has headshot, position badge (D/ST for defenses), name, an "in 3" chip, team and opponent, kickoff time /
    Live / Final, and points. Both sides adds a green/red bar and "67% yours (2 of 3)". Five per group, then "Show all N".
  - **Tap a player (or Enter)** to see the leagues on each side ("Yours in", "Against you in"): each league's name ($ if
    paid), his points there, the win chance or "effectively decided" / "final" / "no opponent", and his share of what
    his side has left.
  - Below that, **every starter by kickoff window** ("Sun 1:00 PM · KC @ DEN · under way · 4 yours · 3 against"), with
    your starters beside the ones against you (stacked on phones). Five per side, then Show all. Each window folds.
  - Finished games fold into one line ("6 games final · 8 of your starters, 9 against you"). In a past week every game
    is final, so that line opens and the list shows final points.
  - Guillotine and median-only leagues have no opponent, and a line names them: their starters count for you only.
  - Players who are Out, on IR or on a bye are left off: S11's "lineups need you" box already flags them.
- A muted **credit line under the Scoreboard card**, styled like the Dashboard's version line: "The root-for board was
  inspired by Sleepy, sleepy-football.vercel.app" (linked). The same sentence ends the Guide's new Who to root for line.
- The header's (i) gains one line on the weights. The Guide's Scoreboard item gains the two halves and Who to root for.
  The badge legend gains two lines: the "in N" chips with the three icons, and the share bar.

**Owner's decisions (asked before building; two rounds of sketches at 375 and 1280px, the second at 20-league scale).**
1. **Where:** between the matchups and MVPs & LVPs, with the tab split into **League Scoreboard** and **Player
   Scoreboard**, both foldable ("allowing users control over what they do and don't see").
2. **Layout:** the spotlight over the list by kickoff window. **Each window folds**, every list is **capped with Show
   all** (as MVPs & LVPs are), and **no By Game view**. A key for the folds: agreed. I proposed one key for the halves and
   Who to root for (`mls_scoreboard_folds`) and nothing remembered for the windows, because their times change weekly.
3. **Weighting: combined.** paid × stakes × impact:
   - paid: **1.5** for a "$ Paid" league.
   - stakes: from the Simulator's win chance, 4·p·(1 − p) (0 once decided or done). It's now computed for every open
     matchup, not just Still in play: before kickoff, and while too early to call. Best Ball, guillotine and week 1 count 1.
   - impact: his projected points still to come ÷ his side's.
   - "Percentage rostered" was (a), how many of your leagues he's in. It's the sum itself (each league adds its weight),
     so it isn't a separate factor.
4. **No "close matchups only" switch for now**: a decided matchup already weighs 0. Revisit after seeing it with many
   leagues.
5. **Points:** this week's live points, not an average. The owner corrected my reading of Sleepy: it averages a player's
   score across the leagues you roster him in, not across the season. The number shown is Sleeper's own stat on the
   MVPs & LVPs scale (half PPR by default); each league's own points are in the tap detail.
6. **Credit:** the Guide line plus a line **at the bottom of the page under the card**, like the Dashboard's version
   (owner's idea). Nothing else in the feature names Sleepy, and nobody was contacted.

**Rules as built** (`js/mls/week/rootFor.js`, no app state):
- Root for: yours in 2+ and against in none. Against you: theirs in 2+ and yours in none. Both sides: at least one of
  each. The share score is your leagues' weight ÷ all his leagues' weight, as a percent. When every weight is 0 (games
  over, a past week) it uses the paid weights alone. Players still to play sort first, by weight, then by how many
  leagues.
- Starters only (`starterIdsOf`): Sleeper's starters, or Best Ball's lineup from the points so far (`bestBallLineup`).
  The Scoreboard's own Best Ball scoring now goes through the same function, unchanged in behavior.
- Impact without projections: a player still to play takes the average of the known ones (or an even share), so a
  missing projection doesn't zero him.

## A1 — Real visitor numbers: privacy-friendly analytics

**User-visible effect.** Nothing changes in how the apps work. Each page now counts visits with **Umami Cloud**
(free plan, no cookies), on mydraftstrategist.com only. One new line in each app's Guide, under "Backup, Restore &
Reset" ("Visitor Counts: …"), and a small muted line at the end of T-Score's **The Research** tab, says what's counted
(the page, the site that linked to it, browser, device type, screen size, language and rough location), that nothing
that identifies you is kept, and that leagues, drafts, rankings and the Sleeper username are never sent. Opening any
page with `?nocount=1` stops counting that browser, with a toast saying so; `?nocount=0` counts it again.

**The owner's decisions (2026-11-03).** After the comparison (now in `docs/improvements/analytics.md`, with sources):
**Umami Cloud, free Hobby plan** ("I'd prefer to not pay anything"); Plausible was out on price, Cloudflare Web
Analytics and GoatCounter count visits rather than people, and GA4 needs a cookie banner. 1–4 "as suggested":
(1) the loader committed in the repo, not Cloudflare's one-click injection; (2) count mydraftstrategist.com only, never
`*.pages.dev` or localhost; (3) `?nocount=1` / `?nocount=0` opt-out; (4) no custom events now, left for K1. Website ID
`9cf14075-37fe-4528-bd9c-a596c26c0671` (public by design). The first look at prices came from search snippets because
the session's network blocked the vendors' sites; the owner allowed them and every number was then re-read on the
vendor's own page (GoatCounter's from its page source on GitHub until its site was allowed).

**What changed, where.**
- `js/shared/analytics.js` (new, in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`): the loader. The last `<script type="module">` on all three
  pages, after the app's module. `shouldCount(hostname, optedOut)` decides (exported, unit-tested); then it adds
  `<script defer src="https://cloud.umami.is/script.js">` with `data-website-id`, `data-domains`
  (`mydraftstrategist.com,www.mydraftstrategist.com`), `data-exclude-hash` (tab switches are `pushState` to `#tab`; without
  it every tab switch would count as a page view against the plan's 100K events a month) and `data-exclude-search`
  (keeps `?week=6` and the like out of the recorded address). Settings are in the loader, no inline snippet.
- `js/shared/storage/keys.js`: `KEYS.shared.analyticsOptOut` = `shared_analytics_optout` (`'1'` = opted out). In the

**Bot Fight Mode (on since 2026-11-02): what it could affect, and a check for the owner.** Cloudflare's page
(read 2026-11-03): it challenges "traffic matching patterns of known bots", "may challenge API or mobile app traffic",
**cannot be bypassed with WAF custom rules or Page Rules** (no exceptions on the Free plan; exceptions need Super Bot
Fight Mode, a paid plan), and it turns on "JavaScript Detections", which injects a small script under
`/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/` into HTML pages (harmless here: the site has no Content-Security-Policy). Requests in
question, all made by a real browser, so normally not challenged, but a challenge on a `fetch()` can't be answered and
shows as a failed request:
- **FFC proxy** (`/api/ffc/<format>`, `functions/api/ffc/`): Draft Strategist's Quick-Start and Fetch Market Value
  call it with `fetch()`. A challenge here would read as "Fantasy Football Calculator unavailable". Its own call out to
  FFC is server-to-server and isn't affected.
- **The service worker**: its install (`cache.addAll` of ~150 files) and its update check (`/sw.js`) are browser
  requests. A challenged file fails the whole precache silently, so offline would stop working for new installs.
- **Installed-app launches**: the first request is a normal page navigation; a challenge there would show
  Cloudflare's interstitial inside the app window.
- Not affected: Sleeper, FantasyCalc, Google Sheets, Ko-fi and Umami are other domains (Cloudflare's setting covers
  only mydraftstrategist.com).

**Two-minute check, after this deploys, on your phone and your computer:**
1. Opt out on each device: open `https://mydraftstrategist.com/?nocount=1` in the browser you installed from, or tap
   **Don't count this device** in a Guide. On an iPhone or iPad, do it **inside the installed app** too (Guide, the link):
   Home Screen apps don't share Safari's storage.
2. Open `/`, `/lineup/` and `/t-score/`. Each should load normally, with no "Checking your browser" page.
3. Lineup Strategist: Sync All Leagues. Draft Strategist: Dashboard, Quick-Start or Fetch Market Value with a Fantasy
   Football Calculator format: players or ADP should load.
4. Offline: once everything has loaded, turn on airplane mode (or DevTools, Network, Offline) and reload each page.
   Each should still open. On the installed app, close it and open it again offline.
5. In Umami (cloud.umami.is), the site should show visits from other people within a day, and none from you after
   step 1. (To check it's live before opting out, open a private window first: it shows up under Realtime.)
6. In Cloudflare, Security, Analytics, Events: anything labelled "Bot Fight Mode" on `/api/ffc/`, `/sw.js` or `/js/`
   paths means real users are being challenged.
If any step fails: turn Bot Fight Mode off (Security, Settings, filter "Bot traffic", Bot fight mode, off). The Free
plan has no way to exempt a path. The rest of the site's protection (DDoS, the WAF's free managed rules) stays on.

installed app shares storage with the browser (and profile) it was installed from. On an iPhone or iPad, no: a Home

link, with 'count this device again' too. Good to allow people to opt out if they want."

  straight away on the live site. The `href` is the fallback if the module never runs. Styled in `css/base.css` like

- `tests/analytics.spec.mjs`: the link on each page toggles both ways without navigating, survives a reload in its

  (only saves the choice). 24 tests, both widths, pass; 485 unit tests pass.

### A1 follow-up: the error banner over a working app (owner's bug report, 2026-11-03)

After PR #217 deployed, the owner's phone showed boot.js's fatal banner ("Something went wrong loading the app",
technical details "Failed to load: https://mydraftstrategist.com/js/shared/analytics.js") over a Lineup Strategist
Dashboard that had loaded and worked. `js/boot.js` treats any same-origin `<script>` that fails to load as fatal (the
case it was written for is one of the app's modules 404ing); the visitor counter's loader is the first same-origin
script the app can do without.

**Cause, as far as a session can tell.** Something stopped that one request on the phone. Candidates: a tracker
blocker matching the file name (none of EasyPrivacy, uBlock's privacy list, AdGuard's spyware sections or Brave's
first-party list has a rule that matches `/js/shared/analytics.js`, checked 2026-11-03, but other blockers and apps
use other lists); a dropped request (every other file came from the service worker's cache, so the new file was the
only network fetch, and `sw.js`'s stale-while-revalidate has no cached copy to fall back to for a file it hasn't
precached yet); or a Bot Fight Mode challenge on it (Cloudflare, Security, Events would show one). The fix covers all
three.

**Fix (test first).** New in `tests/analytics.spec.mjs`: with `analytics.js` aborted as a blocker would, each page
must load with no banner and no console.error (failed on main on all three pages: "fatal boot banner is showing"), and
a real app file that fails (`js/mls/main.js`) must still raise the banner naming it. Then:
- The loader's tag on all three pages carries `data-optional`; `js/boot.js` logs a console.warn for a same-origin
  script with that attribute instead of showing the banner. Only that tag has it.
- `CACHE_NAME` v2.8.148 → v2.8.149. A line under both apps' Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md`.

If the counter is blocked on a device, that device simply isn't counted (and its Guide link falls back to opening
`?nocount=1`, which does nothing without the loader; harmless, since nothing is counted there anyway).

Noted, not changed: `sw.js`'s stale-while-revalidate answers `respondWith(undefined)` when the network fails and
nothing is cached (`.catch(() => cached)` with no cached copy), which turns one dropped request into a hard failure for
that file. Every precached file is safe; only a file added since the last precache is exposed, briefly. A small
separate change if it's ever worth it.

#### The cause, found with the owner (same day)

The owner: Chrome on Android, no blocker, and Reload didn't clear it; every page showed it, in Chrome and in the
installed app. Opening `https://mydraftstrategist.com/js/shared/analytics.js` directly showed **Draft Strategist's home
page** (unstyled) in Chrome and the app, but the real code in an Incognito tab; after force-stopping the app and
clearing its cache, the app showed the code too. So the phone was being handed `index.html` for that one URL, and
keeping it. Two Cloudflare defaults, both in Cloudflare's docs (read 2026-11-03):
- **Pages' SPA mode.** "If your project does not include a top-level `404.html` file, Pages assumes that you are
  deploying a single-page application" and "serves the root (`/`) for any incoming path that does not correspond to a
  static asset", with status 200. This repo has no `404.html`.
- **Browser Cache TTL, 4 hours by default** on every plan: Cloudflare overrides the origin's `Cache-Control` when it's
  lower (Pages sends `max-age=0, must-revalidate`) unless the zone is set to **Respect Existing Headers**.

Most likely sequence: during the deploy the phone asked for the new file from an edge still on the previous
deployment, got `index.html` (200), Chrome kept it for 4 hours, and the service worker's stale-while-revalidate stored
it as the script (status 200 was its only check) and served it on every load; its background refresh went through the
same browser cache and stored the page again. Incognito has neither cache. It wasn't the code (all files pass
`node --check`; main's copy is byte-identical to the tested one) and it wasn't Bot Fight Mode.

**Fix in `sw.js` (test first; v2.9.0, the middle number because the service worker's behavior changes):**
`isHtmlForAsset(request, response)`: a `text/html` response for a path the service worker treats as a static asset
(`.js`, `.css`, images, fonts). `cachePut` never stores one; stale-while-revalidate keeps serving the cached copy
instead of it; after the install's `addAll`, any such entry is deleted so the first load fetches the real file. A
network failure with nothing cached now answers `Response.error()` instead of `respondWith(undefined)` (the same
failure, stated plainly). `tests/sw-html-for-asset.spec.mjs` (service workers allowed; three tests, both widths): a
script and a stylesheet answered with the home page after install stay cached as the real files, and a page served
for the new file during install isn't kept and the real file is cached once it's there. All three failed on the old
`sw.js` (the cache held `<!DOCTYPE html>` for `analytics.js` and `text/html` for `tscore.css`).

**For the owner (not done; dashboard settings or your call):**
- In Cloudflare, Caching, Configuration: set **Browser Cache TTL** to **Respect Existing Headers**. Pages' own headers
  then apply (browsers re-check each file, cheaply, with its ETag), so a deploy is picked up at once and a wrong answer
  can't stick for 4 hours. Recommended.
- ~~Optionally a `404.html`~~: the owner said yes; done, below.
- Anyone else who loaded the site in the minutes of the deploy may see the banner until their 4 hours run out, or
  until this fix deploys (the new service worker serves the cached real file and drops the page).

#### `404.html` (owner: "Proceed with adding a 404.html page")

- `404.html` at the root: "Page not found", a line saying saved data is safe, and links to `/`, `/lineup/` and
  `/t-score/` (Feather icons, the site's buttons, `css/base.css`). Absolute URLs throughout, since Pages serves it at
  whatever address was asked for; no scripts; `noindex`. Not precached: offline, an unknown address still gets the
  app shell from the service worker (`htmlFallback`), as before.
- With it, Pages stops treating the site as a single-page app: an address it doesn't have gets this page with status
  404, and a missing script gets a 404 rather than the home page with 200. Checked first that nothing depended on the
  old behavior: no page has ever been deleted or renamed (git history), the apps use `#hash` for tabs, and
  `tests/serve.mjs` already gave real 404s, so every spec has run that way all along. `/lineup` and `/t-score` without
  the slash are redirected to the folder by Pages, as before.
- `tests/serve.mjs` now answers a 404 with `404.html`'s content (still status 404), like Pages.
  `tests/not-found.spec.mjs`: an unknown address (top level and deep under `/lineup/`) shows the page styled, with
  its logo and the three links, and a link works; a missing `.js` gets a 404. CHANGELOG line under both apps; README
  (Hosting).

#### Owner's decisions on the follow-up (same day)

- Browser Cache TTL set to **Respect Existing Headers** in Cloudflare (done by the owner).
- The error had stopped on main by then (the phone's 4-hour copy had expired). Asked whether the rest is still needed
  with `404.html` in place, the owner chose to **keep everything**: the `data-optional` banner fix (a blocker or a
  dropped request on the optional counter must never show the fatal banner), the service worker's HTML-for-asset
  guard (v2.9.0, mostly redundant once `404.html` exists, kept as a safety net) and `404.html`.

## S31 — Lineup tab: this week's opponent strength from your weekly rankings

**The reproduction first.** On main, a Weekly rankings file with a `Matchup` column (or `SoS`, `Schedule`, `ROS`) in
the single-list layout was read as season SoS by the parser's vertical engine and saved over the Roster tab's season
SoS grid on Save (the SoS card then said "from your Weekly rankings"). `tests/mls-opponent-strength.spec.mjs`'s first
test uploads an SoS file, then saves such a Weekly file, and checks the SoS, its source and the Roster badge are
unchanged: it failed on main (commit c831d1e) and passes now. The owner's own weekly file is the side-by-side layout
(`QB Player … QB Opponent … QB Matchup`), read by the horizontal engine, which never read SoS, so the owner's files
weren't the ones doing it.

**The owner's answers** (from the file "Weekly-Rankings-All-11-3.csv", plus a ROS file for reference):
1. Headers: my suggestion, plus **a position may come before the keyword** ("WR Opponent", "WR Matchup", as in the
   file). Opponent's team: `Opp`, `Opponent`, `Opp Team`, `Opponent Team`, `vs`. Matchup rank: `Matchup`,
   `Matchup Rank`, `Matchup Rk`, `Opp Rank`, `Opp Rk`, `Opponent Rank`, `OPRK`. **A Weekly file never writes season
   SoS** (its SoS / Schedule / ROS columns are ignored); SoS files, ROS rankings files and the manual grid still do.
2. Scale 1 = easiest like SoS, and **one switch**: "My SoS files rank 1 = hardest" flips it too.
3. **A badge in the row's meta line** ("vs KC 28", "@ KC 3"), green to red on the SoS colors, explained on tap;
   **"vs KC" with no rank too** ("include opponent always"); and **yes on the Waiver Wire's Weekly mode** ("that could
   impact a user's decision to pick up the player or not").

**User-visible effect.**
- Lineup tab: each row (starters and bench) with this week's opponent gets a badge at the end of its meta line, after
  the rank: "vs KC 28" (home), "@ KC 28" (away), coloured like the SoS badge (1 green, 32 red), or "vs KC" in plain
  badge colours when the file has no rank for him (the owner's file has none for K and DEF). Tap or hover: "This week:
  at SEA, matchup 15 of 32 for RBs (1 = easiest, 32 = hardest), from your Weekly rankings." On phones and touch
  screens "vs" / "@" is hidden ("KC 28"), as the SoS badge drops "SoS: ".
- Waiver Wire Assistant: the same badge on Top Available rows and Auto-Find cards when Rank By is Weekly (not ROS, not
  Check a List's cards). Top Available still has no SoS badge (S7 round 3).
- Shown only when the league's Weekly set has opponent data and was uploaded this rankings week
  (`isSameRankingsWeek`, Tuesday 10:00 UTC to Tuesday), so last week's matchups never show as this week's.
- "vs" / "@": from the file ("vs KC", "@ KC", "at KC"); for a bare "KC" from ESPN's scoreboard when it names the same
  opponent; else "vs". A row with a Matchup rank but no Opp column takes the opponent from the scoreboard
  (`State.gamesByTeam`, `refreshGameTimes`).

  easiest, 32 = hardest [or: read as 1 = hardest and flipped…]. They show on the Lineup tab, and in the Waiver Wire
  Assistant when Rank By is Weekly, until next week's rankings. Your season SoS isn't changed."
- Fixed: a Weekly file no longer changes season SoS.
- Guide → What the badges mean → Schedule: a new line with three samples (vs KC 3, @ KC 28, vs KC).

**What changed and where.**
- `js/shared/rankings/parse.js`: `parseRankingsFiles(…, { weekly })`. With it, the vertical engine reads no season
  SoS and reads `Opp` / `Matchup` (any of the headers above, optionally after a position); the horizontal engine reads

## M2 — Material 3: 48px touch targets, one focus ring, and press and hover feedback

From M1's review (proposals 1, 2 and 3) and round 2's correction 3. **Also does S15's focus half** (S15's contrast half
is M6).

**The owner's answers** (asked before building, with Playwright screenshots at 375px of a Lineup row, a Tracker card
and the Add/Sync League card, today and after, at rest, with keyboard focus and while pressed, plus the hit areas drawn):
1. **Focus ring: 2px green with a 2px gap**, inset where a parent clips it, and a 2px green outline on text fields
   (the suggestion).
2. **Press feedback: the state layer plus Expressive's pressed shape morph**, the corners tightening 2px while pressed
   (the suggestion; not "state layer only" or "a slight press-in").
3. **Phone primaries and the league arrows keep their look with a bigger hit area** (the suggestion; not 44 → 48px),
   so no screenshot changes.

**What changed and where.**
- **css/base.css, new last section "FOCUS, TOUCH TARGETS AND STATE LAYERS"**, every page (both apps and T-Score):
  - FOCUS: one `:focus-visible` rule, 2px `--primary-green` with a 2px offset; inputs, selects and textareas get it at
    -1px, on their own border. T-Score had none; it gets this one.
  - TOUCH TARGETS: every `button`, `a[href]`, `summary`, `[role=button]` and `[role=tab]` gets `position: relative`
    and an invisible `::after` centred on it whose insets are `min(0px, (100% - 48px) / 2)`: it grows the control to
    48px only in a direction where it's smaller. The toggle switches use `::before` (their `::after` is the handle).
    Both rules are `:where()`, zero specificity, so a component's own position or `::after` wins (an earlier draft had
    the exclusions in a plain `:not()`, whose specificity beat those rules). Left out: `.rankings-card-toggle` (its
    `::after` already covers its card header), the skip link, the Lineup row's swap and lock (the lock's area covered
    the swap: S32), and the two tooltip containers that are `position: static` on purpose (`.mls-lc-status`, the
    Power Rankings table: their area would have stretched over the whole card or table, as their popup does).
  - Split gaps (rules right after it), where neighbours sit closer than 48px: the close buttons on banners grow away
    from what they close (right, not left); the header's menu button stops 4px short of the top-left corner (where the
    screenshots park the mouse) and shares the gap with the league arrow (Lineup) or the logo (Draft, T-Score); Sync
    stops at the screen's edge (it widened the phone page by 1px) and shares 8px with the draft menu; the Tracker card's
    star grows left and its colour dot right; a card header's "i" takes half of its 12px gap to the Badges link; the
    Scoreboard's Refresh doesn't grow toward its "i"; Who to root for's rows (2px apart) take 1px each; "This lineup
    needs you" and its first fix button don't overlap; the matchup strip grows down, not up; Live Sync and Auto-Sync
    (drawn at 85%) keep their own size.
  - STATE LAYERS: a `::before` in `currentColor` on every button, `role=button` and `a.btn`, 8% on hover inside
    `@media (hover: hover)`, 10% on `:active`, fading in 150ms; none on `:disabled` / `aria-disabled`. `.btn`, `.btn-sm`,
    `.mds-btn-sm`, `.mls-btn-sm` and `.btn-header` go from 6px to 4px corners while pressed, on `--press-morph`
    (new in `:root`: 350ms `cubic-bezier(0.42, 1.67, 0.21, 0.90)`, Expressive's fast spatial curve; M3's tokens can
    replace it). Reduce Motion: no fade and no morph animation; the layer and the corners still change.
- **Removed, because the shared rules now do it:** `.btn`'s hover lift and press shrink, `.btn-primary:hover`'s
  brightness filter and glow, the hover backgrounds of `.btn-secondary`, `.btn-danger`, `.btn-warning`, the
  hamburger's tint and 92% press, the bottom bar's 5% tint and 92% press, `.pos-filter`'s 2px hover lift and tint,
  `.btn-header`'s lift and 96% press, Taken's and Pick's (`.btn-draft`, `.btn-mine`) hover lifts, tints, brightness
  and 95% press, `.mls-week-step`'s hover tint and its own `::before` hit area; `transform` and `filter` dropped from
  the small buttons' transitions (`border-radius` added). Focus rules that only repeated the ring: base.css's
  `.toggle-switch`, `.tooltip-icon` and `.tooltip-container[data-tt-self]` outlines, `.btn-bare`, `.pos-filter`,
  `.badge-legend-link`, `a[data-nocount-link]`; mls.css's `button.sos-badge`, `button.opp-rank-badge`,
  `.mls-lc-name-btn`, `.mls-week-step`, `.mls-week-tile-btn`, `button.ir-slot-badge`, `.mls-move-chip`,
  `.mls-week-fold-toggle`, `.mls-week-extreme`, `.mls-gap-chip`, `.mls-root-player`, `.mls-root-window-head`; mds.css's
  `.edit-link`; and every `outline: none` plus faint glow on `.form-input`, `select`, `.scout-textarea`, `.sos-input`
  and the switches. **Kept because they differ for a reason:** `.mls-segmented-btn` (-2px, inside its group),
  `.close-chip` (-4px, inside a chip), the skip link (white on its green), the slider (rings its thumb), and the
  tooltips' "show the popup on focus" rules (which no longer draw a ring of their own).
- **css/mls.css:** `.mls-segmented` lost `overflow: hidden` (it clipped its buttons' areas); the end buttons round their
  own corners (7px inside the 8px border).
- **tests/touch-targets.spec.mjs** (new, phone project only): at 375px with the fixture data, on every tab of both apps
  (empty and seeded) and T-Score, plus the toast, hit-tests a 48x48px square around each visible control (centred, or
  pushed to either side as far as the control still fills it, for split gaps) and fails on a miss unless the control is
  on `ALLOW` with a reason; fails on any control whose own box another control's area covers, allowlisted or not; and
  fails when the page scrolls sideways. `DISCOVER=1` prints every short control and what took each missed point.
- **tests/focus-ring.spec.mjs** (new, desktop project only): tabs through every tab of both apps and T-Score (until
  focus comes round) and fails on any focused control without a solid outline of at least 2px.
- Both fail on main (checked by running them in a worktree of main): Chromium's own 1px `auto` ring on most controls,
  and short controls on every tab.
- `docs/TESTING.md`: a Conventions entry for these rules and specs, and an "owner's decision" follow-up for text
  fields. `CHANGELOG.md`: a line under each app (Draft Strategist's names T-Score too). `sw.js`: `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.2.

**The allowlist, with reasons** (in the spec): links inside a sentence; the Lineup row's swap and lock (S32); **text
fields and selects** (44 to 45px; the header draft menu 32px; they can't take an `::after`, and growing them changes
every form, so it's left for the owner, below); the static tooltip chips and Power Rankings cells; and the split gaps
above: the phone header (menu button 40px wide, Sync 42px), the position chips with the Badges link and its "i" (rows
8px apart on Scout, columns 3px apart in the Roster counts; M4 resizes chips), the Scoreboard's lists and fold toggles
(rows 2 to 6px apart), its "i" and Refresh, the Command Center's Edit / Fold all and the first card's fold button and
name, "This lineup needs you" and its fix button, the Trade Analyzer's Clear above its search, Draft Strategist's Team
tab Undo buttons, the Tracker's star and dot (47px with rounding), and the 85% Live Sync / Auto-Sync switches (their
label beside them toggles them).

**User-visible effect.** Small buttons look the same but take taps in a 48px square (Taken and Pick, the "i" icons,
the toast's ✕, the header buttons, the league arrows, text buttons like Badges, Fold all and Check). Hover shades a
button instead of lifting it; pressing shades it and tightens its corners instead of shrinking it, so a tap on a phone
now shows at once. Keyboard focus is the same green ring with a gap on every control on all three pages (T-Score had
the browser's), and a text field being typed in has a 2px green outline instead of a faint glow. Cards (the Tracker's
player cards, Scout result cards, the guide banner) still lift on hover: they're cards, not buttons.

**Screenshots.** None re-taken. In this container (Chromium 153, so rendering main and the branch the same way and
comparing with pxdiff), three PNGs differ, by 9 to 10 pixels each, all at the left end of a segmented control
(anti-aliasing of the rounded end button instead of the clipped group): desktop `mls-league-setup` (10),
phone `mls-league-setup` (9), phone `mls-league-scout` (9), within the 10-pixel tolerance. Two other side effects were
found this way and fixed rather than accepted: the matchup strip's area reaching upward shifted anti-aliasing across
the Lineup tab (63 to 104 px), and the 85% sync switches' areas blurred their handle (300 px).

**Left over.**
- **For the owner:** text fields and selects stay 44 to 45px (header draft menu 32px). Making them 48px is a visible
  change to every form; it fits M5 (text fields) or M7/M8 (type scale). Recorded under "Open follow-ups".
- The dense spots on the allowlist are a layout question each: the phone header, the Roster's position counts, the
  Scoreboard lists, the Command Center toolbar. S32 takes the Lineup and Roster rows; M4 the chips.
- The spec measures each tab as the fixture leaves it (folds as they open by default) in a redraft league; dialogs, the
  upload preview, opened folds and dynasty-only rows aren't measured. One of those was caught by an existing spec:
  `mls-now-and-later.spec.mjs` (phone) timed out clicking a dynasty Roster row's In-Season | Dyn badge, because the
  "Long-term > now" chip 3px below it reached 15px up over it. They now split the gap (1px each).
- `--press-morph` should move onto M3's motion tokens when M3 lands; the state layer's 150ms fade too.
- S15 is now fully covered once M6 lands (its contrast half).

### M2, round 2: Draft Strategist's header like Lineup Strategist's

**The owner, after reading the summary:** "Update Draft Strategist's header; it'll be better to have it be consistent
with Lineup Strategist anyways." (Its draft menu and Sync were on the allowlist: 118x32 and 30x32 on phones.)

**What changed.**

  PICKER"), renamed `.league-select-wrap` / `.league-select-label` → `.header-picker` / `.header-picker-label`

  to a `.header` that has a picker, so T-Score keeps its logo. The picker's transparent-text rule is

  (js/mds/state.js) keeps the label in step (every switch goes through it) and, with no drafts, leaves a "No Drafts"
  option instead of an empty drop-down.

## Tooling: Playwright 1.56.1 → 1.63.0, the cloud image's Chromium (owner's request, 2026-11-05)

Not a runbook card: the owner asked, after M2, why sessions keep saying the test browser is out of date, and whether it
can be fixed. No app code; `CACHE_NAME` unchanged (tests and docs only).

**Why.** The repo pinned `@playwright/test` 1.56.1 (Chromium 141, revision 1194); CI installs exactly that. The Claude
Code cloud image preinstalls 1.63.0's Chromium 153 (revision 1243) and not 1194, so cloud sessions ran every spec on a
newer browser than CI (`tests/browser.mjs`'s fallback, S23) and could see failures CI didn't, or miss ones it did.
1.63.0 is the release whose Chromium the image has (checked from each release's `browsers.json`: 1.60 → 1223,
1.62 → 1234, **1.63 → 1243**, 1.64 → 1248); the newest, 1.64.1, would put cloud sessions back on the fallback.

**What changed.**
- tests/package.json and the lockfile: `@playwright/test` 1.63.0. `node render-env.mjs` here now finds the pinned
  build (no fallback).
- tests/render-env.mjs: `BASELINE_ENV` 1.63.0 / 1243, and a new `fonts` check. Same browser, the cloud image still
  draws text differently from CI: since 2026-10-03 it has `56-prefer-inter.conf` and `12-unhinted-grayscale.conf` in
  `/etc/fonts/conf.d` (F1, S9). Re-taken here, every PNG came out a different height. With the browser matching, a
  cloud session would otherwise get 42 diffs instead of one message; now it gets one naming those two files, with a
  pointer to "When your machine can't reproduce the baselines".
- tests/browser.mjs keeps its fallback for when the image moves ahead again; comment updated. CLAUDE.md and
  docs/TESTING.md say what's pinned and why screenshots still come from CI.
- **All 42 baselines re-taken from CI's renders** (PR #221, run 42057964808 attempt 2; the procedure in "Upgrading
  Playwright or the CI runner", with CI as the renderer since a cloud session can't be). Checked first: every
  `-expected.png` byte-identical to the committed baseline, and no page changed size. Chromium 153 draws almost
  everything identically to 141. Most differing pixels are one colour level (out of 255) in the translucent, blurred
  header and navigation rail (about 41,500 per desktop PNG, 4,000 to 17,000 per phone PNG). Larger ones, looked at in
  crops, are rendering details only: the edge anti-aliasing of the gradient "TIER" dividers' letters (Tracker), a
  textarea's resize grip, a few glyph edges (Guide, Scout), and on phones the page seen blurred through the
  translucent bottom bar (the strip at y 781-844, which F1's entry already noted draws differently). Nothing moved,
  resized or changed colour.
- CI's first run was cancelled at the job's 30-minute limit, not by this change: the runner's `apt` mirror served the
  font packages at 25 kB/s (16.6 MB in 11 minutes) while the new Chromium downloaded in 7 seconds. Re-run once: 20.3
  minutes, only the screenshots failing, as expected.

**Effect for sessions.** Specs and features run on the same Chromium as CI; screenshot work is unchanged (compare
main and the branch in the container, take baselines from CI).

Strategist's Tracker no longer switches to the Guide tab. The legend opens in a sheet over the tab you're on: from the
right on windows 840px and wider (400px wide, full height), from the bottom below that (half height, scrolling inside;
drag the handle up for nearly full height, tap the handle to switch between half and full, swipe down or tap the scrim
to close). It opens scrolled to the group for the card you came from. Escape, Back, the close button and the scrim close
it, and focus goes back to the link. "Open the Guide" at its foot closes it and opens the Guide at the legend, as the
link did before.

(Lineup and Tracker: Positions and slots; Roster: Ranks and tiers; Scout's Waiver Wire: Changes and trends; the link's

  (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal`, labelled by its title), focus moved to the title and trapped (`focusTrap.js`), Escape,
  the scrim, the close button (48px), Back (the history-entry pattern from `navMenu.js`, S26 round 6, with a capturing

  still clicks the handle.

  corners), and the legend's rows stacked inside it. Motion: Material 3's emphasized decelerate in (400ms) and

  **For M3:** move `.sheet` and `.sheet-scrim`'s transitions onto its tokens.
- `js/mls/legend.js`, `js/mds/legend.js`: `openBadgeLegendSheet(opener, openGuide)`, which opens the sheet with

## K8 — FantasyCalc through a cached Pages Function, and a clear FantasyCalc credit

**Why.** K1's terms check: FantasyCalc's [Terms of Usage](https://fantasycalc.com/terms-of-usage) (effective
2026-10-10) and [API docs](https://fantasycalc.com/api-docs) let sites under 1,000 monthly active users use its values
for free if responses are "cached and reused across users and requests" (each parameter set refreshed at most every
three hours), only `GET /values/current` is called, and "FantasyCalc" is credited with a link near the data. The app
called FantasyCalc from every browser. The owner keeps FantasyCalc while under 1,000 monthly users.

**User-visible effect.** Market values (Trade Finder's Fetch Market Value, the Roster tab's Auto-Fetch ROS Rankings)
come from the site's own cached copy, and the download is ~10 KB instead of ~200 KB. **TE Premium now works**: it
never did, because the app sent `isTEP=true`, which FantasyCalc ignores (checked 2026-11-07: TE ranks identical with
it on or off; FantasyCalc's parameter is `tep=none | te+ | te++`, and `te+` moves Brock Bowers 12th → 9th in redraft).
League sizes FantasyCalc lacks use the nearest one (FantasyCalc offers 8, 10, 12, 14; 16 → 14, 6 → 8). The Trade
Analyzer's line under the verdicts reads "Market values from FantasyCalc, updated today at …" with a link when the
values came from FantasyCalc (a file upload keeps "Market values: Updated …"), and Auto-Fetch ROS Rankings has the
same "Powered by FantasyCalc" mark as Trade Finder.

**The owner's decisions (2026-11-07).** Credit option **A** (the existing line names FantasyCalc, linked; not B, which
added the "Powered by" mark there too), shown with screenshots at 375 and 1280px. **TE Premium stays a switch; on means
`te+`** (not a three-way Off / TE+ / TE++ choice, so the saved setting's shape doesn't change).

**What changed, where.**
- `functions/api/fantasycalc.js` (new Pages Function): `GET /api/fantasycalc?isDynasty=&numQbs=&numTeams=&ppr=&tep=`,
  every parameter required once and checked against FantasyCalc's documented values (anything else 400, so at most
  144 cache entries); one copy per parameter set in `caches.default`, kept a day with the time it was fetched, served
  as is under three hours old, refreshed after; FantasyCalc down → the older copy (`x-fc-stale: 1`), or 502 with
  nothing cached. Rows trimmed to `{ player: { name, position }, overallRank }`. Pages Functions aren't served files,
  so `PRECACHE_ASSETS` is unchanged; `sw.js` already leaves `/api/` alone.
- `js/shared/api/market.js`: `fantasyCalcUrl` (same-origin, the function's parameter order), `fcTeamSize`,
  `FC_TEP_ON = 'te+'`; `fetchMarketConsensusData` keeps its signature and what it returns.
- `js/shared/net.js`: a timeout on `/api/fantasycalc` names FantasyCalc.
- `js/mls/trade/verdict.js` (`marketAgeHTML`) and `css/mls.css`: the credit in the line under the verdicts, from
  `State.marketFormat` (set only by a fetch). `lineup/index.html`: the mark under Auto-Fetch ROS Rankings. `README.md`:
  the function in the project structure. `CHANGELOG.md`: a line under Lineup Strategist. `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.5 → v2.9.6.

### K2: screenshots re-taken from CI (PR #226, run 42424203741)

**The 27 PNGs listed above were re-taken from CI's `-actual.png`.** Each `-expected.png` was checked byte-for-byte
against the committed baseline. `npm run pxdiff` of old against new shows:
- The 15 header-only screens differ only in the header's right end (x ≈ 954–1255, y 12–54; T-Score x 1076–1255).
- The Guides, Dashboards and T-Score's Research tab grow taller by the note, the foot and the line.

The run's only other failure was `badge-legend.spec.mjs`, desktop, "Lineup Strategist: the Waiver Wire Assistant's
link opens the legend…" ("Expected: 0, Received: 153" elements past the screen's edge). It isn't K2's code; it's a race
in M11's test. `openSheet` focuses the title at once but adds `is-open` (which starts the slide-in) two frames later
(`js/shared/ui/sheet.js`). `expectLegendOpen` waited for the focus, then for `getAnimations()`. Read inside those two
frames there's no animation yet, so it measured the side sheet still off-screen. The fix (in this PR): wait for
`.sheet-host.is-open` first.

Checked with `is-open` delayed by 300ms in `sheet.js` on purpose: the old test fails the same way (348 elements), the
new one passes. Main's CI never hit the gap.

### E1 (proposed card, from the owner during K2): easter eggs

The owner, during K2 (2026-11-07): "I love it when sites have easter eggs (e.g., Android's in their version numbers)."
From the ideas offered, the owner picked five. Not built here: K2 stays to its card. **For the runbook:** add this as
card E1 (it isn't on the runbook page yet).

**E1 — Easter eggs: the octopus, the version taps, a hidden code, and two football moments** (~15k tok, Feature,
needs K2; not alongside K4 or S27, which edit the Scoreboard and the Guide's "About this project").

**Goal.** A few hidden surprises that never get in the way. Visible effect, only for whoever finds them: an octopus
that waves from the Guide's "About this project", a message after tapping the version 8 times and another at 18
(Justin Jefferson's number), a football that spirals across the screen after a hidden code, a line when you draft a
kicker or defense in rounds 1–3, and a line on the Scoreboard when a matchup ends within a point.

**Asks you** (before building each part; sketches at 375 and 1280px):
1. The octopus: two or three looks to pick from (our own SVG, Feather-like strokes in the site's green, or a filled
   friendly shape), and the line it says.
2. The words for the 8-tap and 18-tap messages (drafts below).
3. The hidden code on phones, which have no keyboard (for example: a long press on the hero logo, or tapping the
   Dashboard tab's icon in a pattern).
4. The kicker or defense pick: a toast right after your pick, or a calmer line in the Draft Recap once the draft is
   done (a toast mid-draft goes against "never during a draft"; the recap is my pick).

**The eggs.**
- **The octopus** (the mascot; owner's favourite animal). Tapping the "About this project" heading 8 times (eight
  arms; the heading, not the Ko-fi button, so nothing opens Ko-fi) makes a small original SVG octopus rise from the
  box's bottom edge, wave one arm and stay until the tab changes. With Reduce Motion it just appears. Both Guides. It
  can reappear as the "keeper" in the other eggs (in the toasts' icon, or riding the football).
- **The version, 8 taps** (Android's egg; ties to the note's "nothing is locked"): tapping the version at the foot of
  either Dashboard 8 times shows "You've unlocked… nothing. Everything was already unlocked."
- **The version, 18 taps** (Justin Jefferson, WR, Vikings, #18; the owner's favourite player): keep tapping to 18 for
  a Jefferson nod, for example "18. Best route-runner in football." in purple and gold. Text only: his name and number,
  no photo beyond Sleeper's headshots, no team logo.
- **The hidden code.** Typing a code anywhere outside a text field sends a small SVG football spiralling across the
  screen (once; with Reduce Motion a short fade instead). Codes to choose from: the classic ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A,
  "hut hut hike", or "jjettas" (Jefferson's nickname: the football in purple and gold, or with "18" on it). Plus the
  phone trigger from ask 3.
- **Kicker or defense in rounds 1–3** (Draft Strategist): when *your* pick in rounds 1–3 is a K or DEF: "Bold strategy.
  We respect it." Where it shows: ask 4. Once per draft.
- **Within a point** (Lineup Strategist's Scoreboard): when your matchup is Final and the margin is under 1 point, a
  line under it: "Lost by 0.4. That one stings." or "Won by 0.3. Whew." Final weeks only, never while games are live.

**Scope and rules.**
- One shared module, `js/shared/ui/easterEggs.js` (in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`): the tap counter, the key-sequence detector
  (pure functions, unit-tested), the octopus and football SVGs; wired through `data-action` and `delegate()` or a
  document `keydown` listener that ignores inputs, selects, textareas and contenteditable.
- Never during a crunch: no egg shows while a dialog or sheet is open, while Live Sync is on, or in the hour before a
  kickoff with one of your starters (K4's quiet window, if it has merged; else skip the Scoreboard line while live).
- Inline SVG only, no emoji (`noEmoji.test.mjs`); Reduce Motion respected; nothing is announced loudly (toasts are
  polite); no storage key unless the owner wants an egg to show only once (then one key in `keys.js`, e.g.
  `mls_eggs` / `mds_eggs`).
- The screenshot fixtures must not trigger any egg (check the Final fixture's margins in `mls-this-week.spec.mjs`), so
  no baseline changes. No Guide legend line (they're hidden), and the CHANGELOG says only "A few hidden surprises."
- Trademarks: no Star Wars or Batman names, logos, characters or quotes (the owner's other loves; a later card could
  add a "May the Fourth" line on 4 May, or a generic bat silhouette on Halloween, if wanted).
- Tests: unit tests for the sequence detector, the tap counter's reset (taps more than ~2 s apart start over) and the
  margin line's wording; a spec per egg (each trigger shows it once, a near miss doesn't, Reduce Motion, not inside a
  text field, not during Live Sync).

**Avoid.** Anything that blocks a control or needs closing; sounds; ads or links out (beyond what K2 added);
other people's artwork.

**Done.** The five eggs as the owner chose them; unit and spec tests; CHANGELOG line under both apps; `CACHE_NAME`
bumped; screenshots identical; checks pass.

### S30, round 2: lists, tier lines, two chip rows, Fix name (owner's choices, after trying it with a weekly file)

The owner viewed a real weekly sheet (QB / RB / WR / TE / DEF / FLEX / K columns side by side, "Weekly Rankings All
11-8") and asked four things; I proposed how, and they agreed.

1. **Unmatched names.** The banner gets **Show these names** (lists only those rows, in rank order; "Show all players"
   goes back), and the No match chip goes. Owner: allow fixing the name in the app. Each unmatched row has **Fix name**:
   the name becomes a field in the row (not a second dialog over the sheet, whose focus traps would fight), with a line
   that says as you type "Matches a Sleeper player: K, BAL.", "No Sleeper player by that name yet." or "Another player
   in this set already has that name." (refused). Enter or Save name saves, Escape or Cancel goes back. Saving writes
   the name and `cleanName` into the set (stored under the set's existing key), reloads the open league's rankings
   (`hydrateRankingsForLeague`) and redraws the Roster or Lineup tab; other leagues read the set when they're opened.
   A toast says whether it matches now.
2. **Tier lines instead of a Tier column.** A labelled line ("TIER 3", like Draft Strategist's Tracker) before each
   tier's first row, the first tier too. Lines hide with their rows under a search or filter, and all of them hide when
   the rows on screen aren't in tier order. The list's own tiers: the overall tier in All, the position tier in a
   position's list, FLEX tiers in FLEX (the owner's file has none, so no lines there). The Tier column is gone.
3. **Separate lists.** A set where two or more players share a rank (a weekly sheet of side-by-side lists, or one file
   per position) has no All: each chip is its own list, ranked by its own number (FLEX 1–100, QB 1–25, …), opening on
   FLEX when the file has FLEX ranks, else the first position. In FLEX each row's badge shows his position rank. A
   single ranked list (most ROS files) keeps All, and a position chip narrows it in overall order. Search narrows the
   list on screen. Owner: the upload preview may get the same treatment later ("we can circle back").
4. **Chips.** Back to the Roster tab's look (name over count, one equal column each), a little shorter. Two rows: the

## F12 — "N lineups need you" counts a lineup that has a change to set

**The bug** (owner, 2026-11-08: "Saying a lineup doesn't need you when a rankings change is available feels off"). The
Dashboard's strip counted a league as needing you only for a to-do that counts (S11) or an urgent Sleeper change (S12
round 6): `needCount` in `collectLineupNeeds`. A league whose only difference from Sleeper was that your rankings now
prefer another starter ("Set on Sleeper · Start X · Bench Y") was left out: the strip read "2 lineups to set on Sleeper"
as a separate, quieter count, the card's "1 to set" was muted with no amber edge, and with a note beside it (a starter
you locked in, an IR move, an ended lock) both the strip and the Lineup tab's box said "Nothing needs you before
kickoff" above a lineup you still had to set.

**Reproduced on main first** (`tests/mls-lineup-needs.spec.mjs`, "a lineup with a change to set on Sleeper needs you,
worded by kind (F12)": the Fixture League's Sleeper lineup differs, Josh Allen is Doubtful, then locked in). On main the
strip read "1 lineup needs you before kickoff · 1 to set on Sleeper", and after the lock "Nothing needs you before kickoff
· 1 league with notes · 1 to set on Sleeper", with the Lineup tab's box saying "Nothing needs you before kickoff".

**Owner's decisions (asked after reproducing, with the strip, a card and the Lineup tab's box at 375px in four cases:
only a rankings change, only an injured starter, both, and a change plus a kept starter; today against each option).**
- **(a) one count, the kinds after it**: "3 lineups need you · 1 to fix · 2 to set on Sleeper" (not (b), the same with
  fixes in red and sets in amber; not (c), two counts with fixed words).
- **Every change counts**, whatever it gains (no minimum in projected points or tiers): lock a player to keep him.

**User-visible effect.**
- **Strip:** "1 lineup needs you · 1 to set on Sleeper", "2 lineups need you · 2 to fix", "1 lineup needs you · 1 to fix
  · 1 to set on Sleeper" (a league with both is in both kinds). "before kickoff" is gone from the title (a set isn't
  tied to the first kickoff). With nothing that counts but notes: "Nothing needs you before kickoff · 1 league with notes",
  as before. The amber icon whenever a lineup needs you. Show / Show next and the "Set the lineup on Sleeper, then Sync All
  again" line are unchanged.
- **League card:** amber edge and the "Needs you" label for a set-only league too (it was "Set on Sleeper", neutral).
  Counts "1 to fix" (was "1 to do") and "1 to set", both amber (the set was muted since S12 round 5). The Sleeper item
  reads "Set on Sleeper: Start … · Bench …" in every case (was "On Sleeper: …" beside other items, bare when alone).
- **Lineup tab's box:** "This lineup needs you: set it on Sleeper" (amber icon) when the change to set is the only thing
  that counts, with or without notes; it said "Set this lineup on Sleeper" (no amber) or "Nothing needs you before
  kickoff". With a fix it stays "This lineup needs you"; folded, the count adds one for the set.
- **Toasts:** Optimize All "Optimized 2 lineups · 1 needs you · 1 to set on Sleeper" (was "· 1 to set on Sleeper"
  alone); Sync All "Synced 2 leagues · 2 lineups need you · 1 to fix · 1 to set on Sleeper". An injured or bye player
  still starting on Sleeper is a fix ("1 to fix"), not a set, as S12 round 6 made it urgent.
- **Unchanged:** who starts, what counts as a to-do or urgent (S11, S12), what Sync All and Optimize All do, F7 (a change
  involving a player whose game has started is never a change, so never counted), Best Ball (never needs you).

**What changed and where.**
- `js/mls/lineup/issues.js` (pure): **`leagueNeeds({ items, sleeper, bestBall })` → `{ needs, fix, set }`**, the one rule.
  `fix` = counted items + 1 for an urgent Sleeper change; `set` = any other Sleeper change; `needs` = either. Also
  `leagueNeedKeys(leagueId, need)` (the ✕ keys: `fix:<id>`, `set:<id>`) and `needKindsText(fixLeagues, setLeagues)`.
- `js/mls/render/dashboard.js`: `collectLineupNeeds` adds `need` to each `byLeague` entry and returns `needCount`
  (leagues that need you), `fixLeagues`, `setLeagues`. `needKeys` is built from `leagueNeedKeys`, so a league that gains a
  change to set (or a fix) while the strip is hidden brings it back (before, a league's Sleeper key was already there, but
  a set-only league didn't count). `renderLineupNeeds`, `leagueTodoHTML`, Optimize All's and Sync All's summaries read it.
- `js/mls/render/leagueCards.js`: the card's edge and counts from `entry.need`. `js/mls/lineup/gameInfo.js`:
  `getLineupNeedsHTML`'s title, amber and folded count from `leagueNeeds`. `css/mls.css`: `.mls-lc-count-sleeper` amber.
- **For M10 (badges on the navigation):** count from `collectLineupNeeds().needCount` (or `leagueNeeds` per league), the
  same rule as the strip, so the badge and the strip can't disagree.
- No new storage key, file or badge (the counts are text, `badgeLegend.test.mjs` passes). CHANGELOG line under Lineup
  Strategist. `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.9 → v2.9.10.

**Tests.**
- `tests/unit/lineupIssues.test.mjs`, `leagueNeeds`: nothing, a rankings change only, a to-do only, both, a kicked-off
  change ignored (F7, through `sleeperLineupChanges`' frozen check), an urgent Sleeper change as a fix, kept starters and
  notes not counted (a change beside them still is), Best Ball never, the ✕ keys gaining `set:` with a new change, and
  the kinds' wording.
- `tests/mls-lineup-needs.spec.mjs`: the new F12 test (strip, card counts, the Lineup tab's box after a lock, Optimize
  All's toast), and the older tests' wording: the Sleeper-only case now needs you (title, label, amber, toast, the Lineup

- `tests/mls-league-cards.spec.mjs`: the strip's titles, "1 to fix", "Set on Sleeper: …".

## F13 — Locked players still follow kickoff order

**Owner's decisions** (asked after reproducing, with a 375px today/after picture of the Lineup tab, 2026-11-09):
1. Manual locks join the relabel; players whose game has started stay put, including one you locked yourself: **yes**.
2. Only slot placement was meant: no other on-screen change (rows already read in slot order).
3. A manual swap (which locks both players) stays as set until the next re-optimize, which may then relabel two swapped
   starters by kickoff: **agreed**, no special handling.

**The bug, reproduced on main** (`tests/mls-locked-kickoff.spec.mjs`, both widths). Fixture league (QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, TE,
FLEX), Gibbs moved to mds_test so both RB slots fill. CeeDee Lamb (DAL) plays Monday night, everyone else Sunday at 1 pm.
Unlocked, Lamb goes to FLEX. Locked, `fillSlot` puts him in the first slot his position fits (WR1) and
`optimizeFlexKickoffOrder` skipped every `isLocked` starter, so main showed WR Lamb, WR Chase, FLEX Jefferson (1 pm). So a
lock never kept a player's slot; it kept him out of FLEX.

**What changed and where.**
- `js/mls/lineup/kickoffOrder.js`: `optimizeFlexKickoffOrder(starters, kickoffMs, gameStarted = () => false)`. A starter
  is held (his slot out of the pool) only when `player.autoLocked` or `gameStarted(player)`; a manual lock (`isLocked`
  without either) is movable. Who starts never changes (the function only relabels).
- `js/mls/render/lineup.js` (`optimizeLineup`): passes `p => kickoffFreeze(league, p) !== null`, the auto-lock's own rule.
  `optimizeLineup` sets `autoLocked` false for a manual lock (the manual flag wins), so a lock whose game has since
  started needs this second check to stay put. Through `kickoffFreeze`, an auto-lock you overrode (`isAutoLockOverridden`)
  is movable again, and Best Ball holds nobody.
- **Waiver scanner** (`js/mls/scout/waiverScanner.js`): unchanged. Its `fillLineup`/`bestLineup` decide who starts from
  the multiset of slot types; locks there mean "must start", which is still right. It never runs the relabel.
- **Dashboard re-optimize** (`reoptimizeKickedOffLeagues`, `js/mls/render/dashboard.js`): unchanged; it calls
  `optimizeLineup`, so it gets the new rule.
- `sw.js`: `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.10 → v2.9.11. CHANGELOG line under Lineup Strategist.

**User-visible effect.** With FLEX Kickoff Optimization on, a player you locked is placed by kickoff like anyone else
(Lamb above now shows in FLEX, Chase and Jefferson in WR), still starting and still showing LOCKED. A player whose game has
started stays where Sleeper has him. With the toggle off, nothing changes. A manual swap (which locks both players) stays
as you set it until the next re-optimize, which may now relabel two swapped starters by kickoff; on main the fill
already moved locked players to their first fitting slot, so a starter-to-starter swap was never kept slot for slot.

**Tests.**
- `tests/unit/kickoffOrder.test.mjs`: the row helper's lock field now says which lock (`true`/`'auto'` = game started,
  `'manual'` = your lock); the existing lock cases are game-started locks, as they were meant. New "manual locks join
  the relabel (F13)": a manual lock in WR1 who plays latest moves to FLEX; a manual lock in FLEX gives FLEX to a later
  strict-slot starter; auto-locked players stay; a manual lock whose game started (`gameStarted`) stays; a manual lock
  in SFLEX in a superflex league (the later QB takes SFLEX); no locks matches main's function. The three "moves" cases
  fail on main.
- `tests/mls-locked-kickoff.spec.mjs` (new): the lock moves to FLEX (fails on main), and the toggle off keeps the fill.
- `mls-sflex-kickoff`, `mls-weekly-locks`, `mls-lineup-needs` pass.

**Screenshots:** none changed. No screenshot fixture has a locked player. This container can't match CI's baselines

## F11 — Every chevron turns when its section opens

**Goal** (owner, 2026-11-08): "All chevrons need to animate (similar to the chevrons on the Dashboard)." M3 hasn't
merged, so the timing is S16's `--vt-ms` / `--vt-ease` (the Dashboard league cards' own: 275 ms on phones, 375 ms from
768px, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`). When M3 moves every transition onto its motion tokens, the one `.chevron` rule
moves with the view transitions' timings (M3's card keeps S16's durations).

**User-visible effect.** Every fold and unfold in the three pages turns its chevron the same way, at the Dashboard's
speed; with Reduce Motion it switches without moving. Chevrons that turned faster (0.15 s or 0.2 s with another curve)
now turn at the Dashboard's speed; chevrons that jumped (a redrawn box, an inline style) now turn. The folds that showed
the browser's own triangle (▸) show the site's chevron (Feather `chevron-down`, 14px, stroke 2.5, like the "What
changed?" folds; 18px on T-Score's large appendix title) pointing right when closed and down when open, and it turns.
No fold's resting look changed otherwise: the ones that pointed right/down still do, the ones that pointed down/up
(rankings cards, next-lock line, Draft Strategist's cards) still do.

**The shared rule** (css/base.css, CHEVRONS): `<svg class="chevron">` as a direct child of its toggle (a `<summary>`,
or a button with `aria-expanded`). `.chevron` rests at −90° (right) and turns to 0 (down) under
`:is(details[open] > summary, [aria-expanded="true"]) > .chevron`; `.chevron.chevron-flip` rests at 0 and turns to 180°
(up). `transition: transform var(--vt-ms) var(--vt-ease)`, `none` under Reduce Motion. `.chevron-summary` (on a
`<summary>`) drops the browser's marker (`list-style: none`, `::-webkit-details-marker`) and lays the chevron and the
title out in a row (`display: flex; gap: 0.4rem`). The state comes from the toggle's own `[open]` / `aria-expanded`,
which every fold already set (the screen-reader state), rather than from each card's class.

**Redrawn folds** (new `js/shared/ui/chevron.js`, in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`): `turnChevronAcrossRedraw(selector, redraw)`
reads the old chevron's angle, runs the redraw, and plays the turn on the new chevron with the duration and curve the
CSS rule gives it (Web Animations; no turn when the computed duration is 0s, i.e. Reduce Motion). Used by the two folds
that redraw their whole box on every click: the Lineup tab's "This lineup needs you" title (`toggleLineupNeeds`,
renderLineupUI) and Draft Strategist's My Queue (`toggleQueueCollapse`, renderBoard). Folding them in place would have
meant reworking each render; the helper keeps the code paths as they were.

**Inventory** (grep of css/, js/ and the three pages for `chevron`, `<summary>`, Feather chevron polylines and
`rotate(`):

| Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard league cards (`.mls-lc-chevron`, render/leagueCards.js) | turned, `--vt-ms`, own rule in mls.css | shared rule (own rule removed) |
| Scoreboard folds: Still in play, MVPs & LVPs (`.mls-week-chevron`, week/thisWeek.js) | turned, `--vt-ms`, own rule | shared rule (own rule removed; color and flex-shrink kept) |
| Scoreboard kickoff windows (`.mls-root-chevron`, same SVG) | turned (via `.mls-week-chevron`), own −90° rule | shared rule |
| "What changed?" folds, Best Available (Dashboard cards), "Differs from your Sleeper lineup" (`.mls-change-chevron` in `<details class="mls-change-fold">`) | turned in 0.15 s, default ease | shared rule |
| Lineup tab "This lineup needs you" title (`.mls-change-chevron` in a button) | 0.15 s rule, but the box is redrawn on click, so it jumped | shared rule + `turnChevronAcrossRedraw` |
| Lineup tab "Next lock: N players" (`.chevron-icon`, lineup/gameInfo.js) | turned 0.2 s (M2-era curve), down → up | `.chevron.chevron-flip`, in place |
| Roster tab rankings cards: ROS, Weekly (`.chevron-icon`, lineup/index.html) | turned 0.2 s, down → up | `.chevron.chevron-flip`, in place |
| Waiver Wire position groups (`.chevron-icon` in `.rankings-card`, scout/waivers.js) | turned 0.2 s, down → up | `.chevron.chevron-flip`, in place |
| Draft Strategist player cards on phones (`.btn-expand`, tracker.js) | inline `rotate(…)` + `transition: 0.2s` written at render; the toggle (ui.js) flips the class in place, and the inline style beat the class rule, so it never turned until the next redraw | inline style gone; `.chevron.chevron-flip` |
| Draft Strategist My Queue (`.queue-header`, tracker.js) | 0.2 s rule, but renderBoard redraws it, so it jumped | `.chevron.chevron-flip` + `turnChevronAcrossRedraw` |
| Draft Strategist Recap "Show Value Breakdown" (`#recapMathArrow`, index.html / recap.js) | inline `style.transform` set by JS, no transition: jumped | `.chevron.chevron-flip`; the JS lines go |
| Lineup Strategist `<details class="sos-details-accordion">`: Recent Sync Logs, Add Player Manually, MVP / LVP Lines, Backup & Restore, Danger Zone, Edit Manual SoS Grid, Lineup settings, Value settings | browser triangle, swaps in one frame | shared chevron, `.chevron-summary`; Recent Sync Logs' text moved into `<span id="syncLogSummary">` so its count update (render/dashboard.js) keeps the icon |
| Roster tab Auto-Fetch "Settings" (`.mls-autofetch-settings`) | browser triangle | shared chevron |
| Upload preview "Why?" (`.preview-derived-more`) | browser triangle | shared chevron |
| Trade Analyzer "Their team: …" (`.mls-trade-impact-partner`, trade/lineupSection.js) | browser triangle | `FOLD_CHEVRON` + `.chevron-summary`; Export Trade's image still swaps the `<summary>` for a plain title (`textContent`, so no icon) |
| T-Score appendix (`sos-details-accordion`) | browser triangle | shared chevron (18px) |
| T-Score "View WR / RB Model Baseline Variables" | `display: flex` summaries: no marker and no chevron (an info icon) | unchanged: no chevron to turn |
| Not folds: Scoreboard week arrows, tile "go" arrows, the header's league arrows | — | unchanged |

## S33 — Player Scoreboard: kickoff order (Thursday night first), and find a player

**User-visible effect.**
- **Root for, Against you and Both sides list players by kickoff while games are left.** The earliest game that isn't
  final comes first, so Thursday night's players are on top of each box until that game ends, then Sunday's early games,
  and so on; a game with no known kickoff comes after the known ones. A small divider starts each kickoff time
  ("Thu 8:15 PM · Live"), and the rows under it no longer repeat the time or "Live". Inside one kickoff the order is the
  board's own, as before: by weight, then by how many leagues; a "decided" player is last in his kickoff.
- **Finished players fold into "N finished" at the bottom of their box.** Tap it (or Enter) to open them in place,
  dimmed, with "Final" and their points; five, then Show all. Before, the boxes left them out and an empty box pointed
  to the "games final" line further down; an empty box now reads "All 7 have finished." with its own line under it.
  The count in a box's title is still who's left to play.
- **A past week, or a week whose every game is final, is unchanged:** everyone listed by weight, no dividers.
- **Find a player.** A search field above the three boxes ("Find a player in this week's matchups") with the site's
  autocomplete, limited to this week's starters, yours and your opponents'. Each suggestion says where he stands
  ("QB · BUF · Both sides, 2 of 3 yours"; "Yours in 1" for a player in one matchup). Pick one (tap, or Enter when one
  name is left) and his row appears right under the field in his box's color and title, with his leagues open: yours
  in, against you in, his points and the win chance in each. Focus moves to that row. The boxes don't move. Escape (in
  the field or on the row) or the field's ✕ clears and returns to the field. A name nobody matches says 'No starter in
  this week's matchups matches "kelce".' The text and the result survive a Refresh; another week starts empty.
- The intro line, the (i) beside Both sides and the Guide's Who to root for item say "by kickoff".

**Owner's decisions (asked before building; sketches at 375 and 1280px on the real page with sample players: order
1A–1D, find 2 and 2A–2E). Answer: "All your recommendations".**
1. Inside a kickoff window: by weight, then count, as today (not by count alone).
2. Finished games: folded into "N finished" at the bottom of each box (1C), not kept in kickoff order (1D).
3. The kickoff label: a divider between windows, rows without the time (1A), not on each row (1B).
4. A past week, or once every game is final: today's order by weight.
5. Find: the result right under the field, boxes unmoved (2C, my recommendation), rather than the card's suggestion of
   jumping to and highlighting his row (2A) or a filter (2B). Why: a player in one matchup, one behind Show all or one
   whose game is over has no visible row to jump to; on a phone a jump scrolls away from the field.
6. League tiles are not marked (2D): the result already lists his leagues.
7. Nobody matches: a line under the field (2E). The search covers only this week's starters, so that line is how "not
   in any of this week's lineups" reads.
Defaults I stated and the owner accepted: Thursday is no special case (the earliest unfinished game is first, live
games included), and a decided player is last within his kickoff rather than last in the box.

**What changed, and where.**
- `js/mls/week/rootFor.js`: `kickoffOrder(gameOf)`, a pure comparator: finished last, then kickoff (unknown after
  known), then settled, weight, count, id. `buildRootFor`'s own order is untouched (a finished week and the window
  lists still use it).
- `js/mls/week/thisWeek.js`:
  - `rootHTML` sorts each box's players still to play with `kickoffOrder` (kickoff from the week's `times`, i.e.
    `State.gameTimesByTeam`; finished from the row's `over` or the game's `post` state) and draws the finished ones in a
    `.mls-root-finished` fold (`toggleRootFinished`, in place; open boxes kept in `rootView.fin` for the week shown).
  - `rootList` takes `dividers` (an `li.mls-root-kick` where the kickoff changes; "Live" when any player of that
    kickoff in the box is in a live game) and `rootRow` / `rootMeta` take `noTime`.
  - Find: `rootFindUi` builds the field once and `mountRootFind` moves that node into a slot in each redraw, so typing
    and the autocomplete survive the card's `innerHTML` redraws (focus is put back when it was in the field).
    `attachPlayerAutocomplete` gets a `pool` (this week's rows) and a `tag` (`standingText`). `pickRootFind` /
    `clearRootFind`; `foundHTML` draws the result with the same `rootRow` (list key `find`). State in memory
    (`rootView.found`, `findText`); no storage key.
- `js/mls/main.js`: actions `toggleRootFinished`, `clearRootFind`. The field's `input` and `keydown` listeners are added
  in code on the node it builds (delegate() has no table for those events on this page).
- `css/mls.css`: the divider, the finished line, the field and the result (end of the root-for rules).
- `lineup/index.html`: the Guide's Who to root for item. `CHANGELOG.md`: one line under Lineup Strategist.
- `sw.js`: `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.12 → v2.9.13. No file added, so `PRECACHE_ASSETS` is unchanged.
- No new badge, chip or pill (the divider and the finished line are text), so the legend has no new line.

**Tests.**
- `tests/unit/rootFor.test.mjs`: `kickoffOrder` (Thursday unfinished first though it weighs least; Thursday final at the
  bottom, under an unknown kickoff; unknown after known; inside a kickoff by weight, then count, settled last; finished

## S38 — Trade Analyzer: the same draft pick twice, and market values without a trip to Value settings

Two requests from the owner (2026-11-08), before the trade deadlines. Branch `ccr-d061837a-5hnofo`, from main at
48e3cd6 (S33 merged). Needs nothing.

**User-visible effect.**
1. **A draft pick can repeat.** Adding "2027 1st" to a side that already has one adds a second entry, "2027 1st (2)"
   (a third is "(3)"). Each has its own token and Remove, its own row under You Receive / You Give Up, and its own value
   in every verdict, in "To make it fair", in Power Rankings after the trade (two picks move) and in Export Trade's
   image. Removing one of two leaves a plain "2027 1st". In a league with synced picks the row says whether the team
   holds that many: "Yours" twice when you hold two, "Not yours (you hold 2)" on a third, "Rival holds only 1".
   "To make it fair" can now suggest a second pick like one already in the trade, when that team holds another.
   A player still can't be on a side twice.
2. **Analyze Trade brings the market values.** With none loaded for the league's format, or with ones over three hours
   old, Analyze Trade fetches them (the button reads "Fetching market values…" and is disabled meanwhile), so the Market
   Consensus verdict is there on the first tap. A new switch, **Fetch market values automatically**, is under Value
   settings (on by default). A market file uploaded in Trade Finder is never replaced. When the fetch fails, there's no
   error toast: the trade is analyzed by your rankings, and an amber line under the verdicts says "Market values couldn't
   load, so this is by your rankings only. Analyze again to retry." (or, with older values still loaded, "Market values
   couldn't be refreshed: these are the ones loaded earlier.").
3. **Each league has its own market values.** A fetch is for the league's format (redraft or dynasty, 1QB or Superflex,
   PPR, TE premium, and league size) and is kept under it. Switching leagues, or changing a Market Consensus setting,
   brings back the values already fetched for that format, in the Trade Analyzer, Trade Finder and everything else that
   reads Market Consensus. The "Fetched for redraft; this league is dynasty" warning now shows only until that league's
   values are fetched (one Analyze), or with the switch off.

### S38: CI re-takes changed screenshots before the pull request (owner, 2026-11-11: "fix it now")

The owner asked why screenshots always cost two CI runs when the session already knows which PNGs change. A cloud
session can't draw CI's pixels: hiding the image's two extra font rules from Chromium (`FONTCONFIG_PATH`, tried here)
made page heights match CI's baselines, but most PNGs still differed by about 1% of pixels. So the pixels come from CI,
but before the pull request rather than from a failed run: `.github/workflows/update-screenshots.yml` (new) runs
`visual.spec.mjs` with `--update-snapshots=changed` on check.yml's runner and commits the changed PNGs to the branch.
Started by "[update screenshots]" in a commit message (any branch but main that has the file) or from the Actions tab.
Steps in docs/TESTING.md ("Cloud sessions: let CI re-take them before the pull request") and a line in CLAUDE.md.
Tooling and docs only; no `CACHE_NAME` bump.

**The guard (owner, 2026-11-11: "CI will still do its actual job in catching problems?").** As first written the
workflow re-took every PNG that differed, intended or not, and the screenshot check would then pass. Now the PNGs must
be named when it's started (`[update screenshots: desktop/a.png phone/a.png]`, or the dispatch input): any other
changed screenshot fails the job with nothing committed, and its renders are in the `retaken-screenshots` artifact. A
named PNG that didn't change is only noted. `check` itself is unchanged. The first run of the workflow (43044251160,
before the guard) failed at `playwright install`: the runner couldn't resolve Ubuntu's package mirror, nothing of ours.

**The workflow's first good run, and S38's baselines (2026-11-11).** Runs 1, 2 and 3 (and a re-run) failed at
`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` before taking a screenshot: Canonical had an outage from 04:06 MST
(status.canonical.com, Ubuntu's archive and DNS among the components), so the runner couldn't resolve Ubuntu's
package mirrors for Playwright's fonts. Not GitHub's fault (its status page was green; the owner checked both) and not
the workflow's; `check.yml` has the same step and would have failed the same way. Once Canonical's DNS was back, a
re-run of run 43052857777 passed in 80 seconds: the guard accepted the four named PNGs and the workflow committed them
(d53c59a, "Screenshots re-taken on CI (4 PNGs)"), so its token can push to a branch with the repo's settings as they
are. The four, each checked against the one it replaces:

## T1 — T-Score: in-season data from your new Google Sheet

**User-visible effect.** The T-Score page opens on a new **In-Season** tab (first in the tab bar; the preseason tabs
are one tap away, and a `#tab` link still opens its tab). It shows rest-of-season projections for **WR, RB and TE**
(TE is new to the page): ROS rank, Player, Team, ROS PPG, FP/G, Tgt % (target share), **Move** (an up or down arrow
and the places from YTD rank to ROS rank, "–" for none) and a green **Buy** or red **Sell** chip, with WR / RB / TE
pills and a **Buy & Sell only** switch. A line above the table says when the rankings were loaded ("Updated today at
4:00 PM"), the description says which week they were projected after, and **How it's projected** (closed by default)
shows the formula, the Model Weights table (intercept, weights, no-prior adjustment, R², Buy/Sell line per position),
what each term means and the Buy/Sell rule. Under the table, the data credit and licenses (nflverse CC BY 4.0,
ffopportunity CC BY-SA 4.0, the projections shared under CC BY-SA 4.0). The tab fetches the sheet every time the page
opens, draws the copy saved by the last visit first, and offline (or when Google doesn't answer) keeps that copy with
"Couldn't reach the sheet, so these are the last rankings that loaded (…)". A first visit offline says the rankings
couldn't load. A tab missing a column the table needs says so in a plain message ("The WR sheet is missing a column
this table needs: Target share.") and keeps that position's last good rankings if it has them. **Sync with most recent
data** fetches the In-Season sheet too. Draft Strategist is unchanged.

**What changed and where.**
- `js/tscore/inSeasonParse.js` (new, pure): reads each position tab and Model Weights by header name (case, spacing
  and column order don't matter; extra columns are ignored; Move falls back to YTD rank − ROS rank when "Rank move" is
  gone); a missing column throws `InSeasonColumnError` naming each one.
- `js/tscore/inSeason.js` (new): the four published-CSV URLs (`IN_SEASON_URLS`, gid 0 WR, 1 RB, 2 TE, 3 Model
  Weights of "T-Score In-Season (public)"), fetching through `mdsFetch`, the saved copy, drawing, the WR / RB / TE
  pills and the Buy & Sell filter. Fails quietly (no `console.error`): what went wrong is drawn on the tab.
- `js/tscore/main.js`: the default tab is `inSeasonTab` (`DEFAULT_TAB`; was `researchTab`), `initInSeason()` on
  DOMContentLoaded, Refresh also calls `refreshInSeason()`, two `data-action`s. `t-score/index.html`: the tab and its
  nav button; the Refresh button's title. `css/tscore.css`: the tab's styles (`.tscore-move`, `.tscore-chip-buy` /
  `-sell`, the message, the credit; the credit's inline links keep their text size: WCAG's inline exception).
- New key `tscore_inseason_cache` (`KEYS.tscore.inSeasonCache`): `{ wr, rb, te, weights, fetchedAt }`, read only by
  the T-Score page; in neither app's backup, like the other `tscore_` keys. The preseason `tscore_cache` that Draft
  Strategist reads is never written by the In-Season tab.
- `sw.js`: the two modules in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`; `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.19. The service worker still lets the sheet's
  cross-origin requests through; offline works from the saved copy, as the preseason tables do.
- Tests: `tests/tscore-inseason.spec.mjs` (draws the fixture, the filter and positions, the panel, saved copy and
  offline, first visit offline, reordered columns and escaping, missing columns with and without a saved copy, Sync,
  deep links); `tests/unit/tscoreInSeason.test.mjs`; fixtures `tests/fixtures/tscore-inseason/{wr,rb,te,weights}.csv`
  (rows from the public sheet of 2026-11-11, after week 9). `helpers.mjs`: `openApp(page, path, { beforeGoto })`,
  `stubInSeasonSheets`, `inSeasonFixture`, `IN_SEASON_SHEET_RE`; `inSeasonTab` first in `TSCORE_TABS` (so smoke,

  `chevrons` and `support` open `/t-score/#researchTab`; `touch-targets` allows `.tscore-credit a`.

**Owner's decisions (2026-11-11).**
- Option A: an **In-Season** tab beside the preseason ones, first and the default view.
