**Round 2 (owner, 2026-11-11): labels and a write-up.**
- **Labels.** The owner asked for the preseason tabs' labels back. Options: (A) percentiles of ROS PPG, as preseason;
  (B) fixed rank tiers per position; (C) natural breaks. Owner's pick: **A**, open to adjusting the thresholds, with
  **Flex Play** in place of Boom/Bust, worked out by the site. The adjustment: the percentiles are taken over a fixed
  pool per position, **twice the Buy/Sell line** (WR 96, RB 72, TE 36), not over every row in the sheet, whose size
  moves with its games-and-XFP filter (about 136 / 86 / 64 rows after week 9) and would relabel players whose
  projection didn't move. The preseason cutoffs (top 5 / 10 / 20 / 35 / 50%) give WR 1–5 Elite, 6–10 High-End
  Starter, 11–19 Strong Starter, 20–34 Quality Contributor, 35–48 Flex Play; RB 1–4, 5–7, 8–14, 15–25, 26–36; TE 1–2,
  3–4, 5–7, 8–13, 14–18; past the line, Depth Player. So Flex Play ends where Buy and Sell are measured. The lines come
  from Model Weights (defaults 48 / 36 / 18). A `Label` column in the sheet, if ever added, overrides the computed one
  (known names only). The Label column sits after Player, with the preseason badges (`label-*`; Flex Play uses
  `label-boom`'s red). How it's projected gains a Labels line and a Label × WR / RB / TE table of rank ranges. Code:
  `labelCutoffs`, `inSeasonLabel`, `LABEL_BANDS` in `js/tscore/inSeasonParse.js`.
- **Write-up.** "The In-Season Model: Rest-of-Season Points per Game" opens The Research (`#inSeasonModel`), above the
  preseason article and a rule: why a second model (the owner's words, lightly edited and expanded), a What Changed
  table (preseason vs in-season), the three ingredients, how it's fit (2016–2025, refit weekly; week-9 weights and R²
  in prose), reading the In-Season tab, what it doesn't know, and the data credit. The In-Season tab's description
  links to it ("How it differs from the preseason T-Score", `data-action="readInSeasonModel"`). It doesn't mention

**Round 3 (owner, 2026-11-11): labels by points, not rank (pending the sheet).** The owner pointed out that round 2's

rank over the list's size, so A, B and round 2 all ignore the projections themselves. Options given: keep it; A over
every row; or (3) ROS PPG cutoffs per position, set from history at the preseason percentiles, as the preseason T-Score
labelled by score cutoffs (65.5, 57.4, …). Owner's pick: **3**, because a tier's size can then change from week to
week and season to season (the owner's example: an elite group of WRs, then a big drop, "the death of the WR2").
The owner's sheet session computed the cutoffs and added them to Model Weights (rows 7–14): a block headed
`Label cutoffs (ROS PPG),WR,RB,TE`, one row per label down to Flex Play, then `Cutoffs from,2016–2025 projections
after week 9`. In tenths, at the owner's request. They're the 95th / 90th / 80th / 65th / 50th percentiles of this
week's model applied to 2016–2025 players at the same week (2,886 player-seasons, the public sheet's filter); that
session recomputes them weekly with the weights (`ros_model_open.py`, run by hand for now). After week 9: WR 15.9 /
14.3 / 12.2 / 9.9 / 8.2, RB 17.1 / 15.3 / 13.1 / 10.6 / 8.8, TE 12.6 / 11.0 / 9.3 / 7.6 / 6.3.

**Built.** `parseInSeasonWeights` finds the block by its header row wherever it sits (columns by name, `Boom/Bust`
accepted for Flex Play) and keeps a position only with all five numbers; `inSeasonLabelByPoints` labels by ROS PPG ≥
cutoff; `labelFor` takes the sheet's own Label, then points, then the round-2 rank labels (the fallback when the block
is missing). The panel's Labels line and table show the cutoffs ("15.9+", "under 8.2") and "Cutoffs from"; the Label
tooltip, The Research's What Changed row and its Label paragraph say how they're set (with one week-9 observation:
seven Elite WRs, fewer than usual in the WR2 tiers, from the sheet session's report). The fixture's Model Weights
has the block, and WR gains Dontayvion Wicks (8.01, Depth). Specs: labels by points (seven Elite WRs, Watson 15.79
High-End, Wicks Depth, the TE list), the panel's cutoffs, the fallback without the block; unit tests for the block and
the labels. Screenshots: `tscore-inSeasonTab.png` and `tscore-researchTab.png` (desktop, phone) change, compared
before and after in this container; re-taken on CI with this commit.

**From the sheet session's report, for the owner** (not on the site): the 2026 top is unusually strong (top-6 WRs
average 18.99 projected PPG vs 17.95 for 2016–23) and WRs 13–24 are about 0.6 points lower in 2024–26, but there's
no new cliff right below the elite group, and 2022–23 had gaps as wide. Players near a cutoff (Watson 15.79 vs 15.9)
can change label from week to week. That session also found that its training skipped 2015, so 2016 players had no
prior; it offered a fix and a weekly scheduled refresh: both the owner's call, outside this repo.

## W1 — CI: docs-only pull requests pass the required check in seconds

**User-visible effect.** None on the site (no served file changes, so no `CACHE_NAME` bump and no CHANGELOG line).
For the owner: a pull request that changes only docs passes the required `check` in seconds instead of ~20 minutes,
so it can merge right away. Every other pull request, and every push to `main`, runs the full suite as before.

**Owner's decisions (2026-11-12).**
- Docs-only means every changed path is under `docs/` (any file, the review PNGs too), or ends in `.md` and isn't
  under `tests/`, `scripts/` or `.github/`. `llms.txt`, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` are not docs (the site serves
  them). Checked first: no page, spec or unit test reads a `.md` file, and `noEmoji.test.mjs` scans only
  `.js/.mjs/.css/.html`.
- Pushes to `main` always run the full suite; only pull requests get the shortcut.

**Built** (`.github/workflows/check.yml`). Checkout now fetches depth 2, so on a pull request GitHub's merge commit
and both parents are there. A new first step, `changes` ("Docs-only pull request?"), lists
`git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD^1 HEAD` (main's tip against the merge commit: exactly what the pull request
changes) and writes `docs_only=true` only when every path matches the list. It runs everything when it can't tell:
not a pull request, no merge commit, a failed diff, no files listed, or a path git quotes (unusual characters).
`--no-renames` makes a rename count by both paths, so moving an app file into `docs/` still runs the suite. Every
later step has `if: steps.changes.outputs.docs_only != 'true'` (combined with the existing `!cancelled() && …` and
`failure()` conditions). The job keeps the name `check`, so the required status still matches. Plain shell, no
third-party action. The log and the run's summary say which way it went, why (the non-docs files, up to 20), and the
changed files. A header comment in the workflow says never to use `[skip ci]` or `paths-ignore`.
`docs/TESTING.md` ("The checks", CI bullets) documents the rule.

**Checked.** The step's script, run against real merge commits in a scratch repo: docs and `.md` only → true
(including a PNG in `docs/` and a `.md` outside it); an app `.js`, `tests/README.md`, `.github/x.md`, `llms.txt`, a
`js/` → `docs/` rename, a deleted `.js`, a push event, a non-ASCII path and a commit with no second parent → false;
a 3,000-file diff with one `.js` → false with no SIGPIPE under `pipefail` (`sed -n` instead of `head`).
check-precache and `node --test` pass (the full Playwright suite isn't affected and wasn't run: no app file changed).

**Proof runs on CI** (two throwaway draft pull requests into this card's branch, with the owner's OK; both closed).
- Docs-only: #236 changed only `docs/improvements/analytics.md`. [Run 43160610607](https://github.com/btrerise/My-Draft-Strategist/actions/runs/43160610607)
  passed in 8 seconds; its log says "Docs-only pull request: npm, Playwright and the checks are skipped (every changed
  file is docs)", and setup-node, `npm ci`, the Playwright install, render-env, `npm run check` and the artifact upload
  are all marked skipped.
- App file: #237 changed only a comment in `js/shared/names.js`. [Run 43160615884](https://github.com/btrerise/My-Draft-Strategist/actions/runs/43160615884)
  ran everything and passed (`npm run check` 20 min 25 s, the job about 21 minutes).
- Note: GitHub runs a step without its own `shell:` as `bash -e {0}`, without `pipefail`; the script works under both.

**Left over.**
- The throwaway branches `w1-proof-docs` and `w1-proof-app` are still on GitHub: this session's git couldn't delete a
  remote branch. Delete them from the repo's Branches page (Cloudflare Pages also made a preview of each; harmless).
- W1's own pull request changes `.github/`, so it runs the full suite, as it should.

## S29 — Power Rankings: what your last trade did

**User-visible effect.** On the Roster tab of a Sleeper league, a new box sits under the Positional Power Rankings
table (round 2; it was first under the strip): **"Since your trade with Rival on Sep 8"**, who got whom ("You got Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs, Saquon Barkley",
best first by the strip's rankings), then one line per team with only the ranks that moved, right before → right after
the trade ("You: Start 2 → 1 · RB 2 → 1 · WR 1 → 2", green better, red worse; "no rank changes" when none moved).
Columns: Start, Ovr, QB, RB, WR, TE, and Future in dynasty and keeper leagues. With more than one trade this season, a
**Trade** drop-down ("Sep 12: with Rival") picks any of your trades this season (round 3: yours only); it opens on
your newest, and your pick lasts for the visit. A note under it: "Power Rankings right before → right after
this trade, out of N teams, by today's rankings. Moves since then are left out. 1 = strongest." Manual league, no
trades this season, or Sleeper failing: no box, no toast.

**The owner's decisions (Asks you, 2026-11-12).**
1. **Which moves: trades** ("what I mainly care about"). Waiver and free-agent moves are read only to rebuild rosters.
2. **How far back: the whole season, as a log to pick from** (owner asked for a list of all the league's trades rather
   than two weeks, since dynasty rankings change about monthly). Weeks 1 to the current week, every trade in the league.
3. **Where: under the Roster tab's Power Rankings strip** at first; moved under the full table in round 2. Not on the
   Dashboard.
4. **The other team: one line** ("could be interesting to see how much a trade helped/hurt after some time").
5. **Each trade on its own:** "after" is the league right after the trade (every later move undone), "before" the same
   with the trade undone too, both scored with today's rankings. So a trade's numbers are what the Trade Analyzer showed
   for it beforehand (with today's rankings), and two lines don't count the same move twice. The catch: the "after"
   can differ from today's strip when moves came later. The owner asked to check this once built, and confirmed it in
   round 2.

**What changed and where.**
- `js/shared/api/sleeper.js`: `getSleeperTransactions(leagueId, week)` (throws on a non-ok response). S34 can reuse it.
- `js/mls/power/pastTrades.js` (new, pure): `completedMoves` (complete only, deduped, newest first by
  `status_updated`), `undoMove` (each player in a move's adds or drops goes back to the team that dropped him, else off
  every roster; one rule for trades, waiver claims, free-agent adds and drops and commissioner moves), `undoPicks`
  (each traded pick back to `previous_owner_id`, matched by season, round and original team; picks league.picks
  doesn't list are skipped), `leaguesAroundMove`, `tradeEntries`, `defaultTradeId`, `rankChanges`, `makeOwnerOf`
  (roster id → owner as the sync names teams: "You", else `league.teamNames`; a name no roster uses becomes "Unknown
  Team" when that exists, else nobody, so an undone move never adds a team to the rankings).
- `js/mls/power/tradeLine.js` (new): fetches weeks 1..current in parallel (plus the cached player map) for the active
  league only, when the Roster tab is showing, once per visit; a re-sync (new `globalRosterMap`) asks again. Moves after
  the league's `lastSyncedAt` are ignored (today's rosters don't have them yet). Scores with
  `computePositionalPower` and the strip's own source (`resolvePowerRankingsSource`: In-Season and dynasty sets per
  S23, Market Consensus fallback) and future values (picks count in Future, as in S24).
- `js/mls/power/rosterCard.js`: `refreshPowerRankings` calls `renderPastTradeLine` (and hides it with the strip).
- `js/mls/main.js`: the `selectPastTrade` change action. `lineup/index.html`: `#rosterTradeLine` (hidden). `css/mls.css`:
  `.mls-roster-trade*` (reuses `.mls-trade-rank-up/down` for the colors). No new badge or chip, so no legend line.
- `sw.js`: the two new files in `PRECACHE_ASSETS`; `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.19 → v2.9.20. No storage key.
- Fixtures: `league-transactions.json` (no moves, served by default for every league and week),
  `league-transactions-trade.json` (the week-1 trade: your Chase, Jefferson, Lamb for Rival's Bijan, Gibbs, Saquon, plus
  a failed waiver claim) and `league-rosters-traded.json` (rosters after it), from `make-fixtures.mjs`;
  `tests/helpers.mjs` routes `transactions/<week>`.

**Tests.** Unit (`tests/unit/pastTrades.test.mjs`, 16): the undo rule for a trade, a waiver claim with a drop, a
free-agent add alone and a drop alone, a commissioner move, unknown players and teams, picks (back one step, passed on
twice, a draft already held, with a trade's players), failed and duplicate moves, several moves undone newest first with
a player since dropped again, and a scored check that "before" and "after" equal the Trade Analyzer's
(`leagueAfterTrade`) for the same trade. Spec (`tests/mls-past-trade.spec.mjs`, both widths, phone at 375px): the
Trade Analyzer's "after the trade" ranks for the fixture trade, then the trade goes through on Sleeper and the line
shows exactly those changes (and Rival's the other way); two trades (drop-down, newest of yours first, the older one
alone after the later is undone, the pick kept across tab switches); no trades (two requests on opening the Roster tab,
none before it, none again later); Sleeper failing (no box, no toast); a manual league (no box, no request).

**Screenshots.** None change: the box is hidden in every screenshot (no fixture league has a trade). All 44 PNGs,
rendered in this container on main and on the final branch, are pixel-identical (`npm run pxdiff`, 2026-11-12).

**Left over.**
- A trade made after the last sync isn't listed until the league is synced again (its players aren't on today's
  rosters yet). A note saying so would need a comparison with Sleeper's list; not built.
- Trades from last season (a dynasty league's previous season, `previous_league_id`) aren't read; neither are picks
  for drafts already held. Offseason trades in Sleeper's current-season league are (week 1).
- The Guide's Roster tab text doesn't mention the box (a sentence there re-takes `mls-league-guide` at both widths).

### S29, round 6: a trade since the last sync syncs the league by itself (owner)

The owner asked for a trigger: when the box finds a trade of yours completed after the league's last sync, sync the
roster automatically. `renderPastTradeLine` (`tradeLine.js`): once per league per visit, while the Roster tab shows, it
calls `processSleeperData` as the Roster tab's Sync button does (`isRefresh`, the Added / Dropped / Now OUT toast), with
its error toast off. Meanwhile the box shows the new trade's title and "New since your last sync: updating this league
from Sleeper…". The moves just read are kept for the redraw (`keepAfterSync`), so Sleeper isn't asked for them again.
On a failed sync the box falls back to what it showed before (no toast; the sync logs to the console and flags the
league "Last sync failed" on the Dashboard, as any failed sync does).

What else the sync does, the same as the button: it **re-optimizes this league's lineup** (`optimizeLineup(true)`,
manual swaps reset), refreshes the roster, records and the Power Rankings, and clears the Dashboard's stale-sync age.
Only a trade of yours triggers it, not a waiver claim or another team's trade.

Spec: "a trade since the last sync" (the league syncs once, the box shows the trade with the Trade Analyzer's numbers,
the Added toast, the moves aren't read again, no second sync on the next visit to the tab). Also fixed: the "Sleeper
fails" test's toast check used a selector that matched nothing (`.toast-message` now).

Not tested: a failed automatic sync (the sync's own `console.error` fails `expectClean`); the code path falls back to

## N2 — Starter alerts before kickoff (site open), and the shared notification module

**Owner's answers (2026-11-12).**
1. **Which lineup:** the starters set in Sleeper (what scores), not Lineup Strategist's recommendation.
2. **How long before kickoff:** a drop-down in Settings, 15 to 120 minutes in steps of 15, 60 by default. (The help
   text says inactives come out 90 minutes before kickoff, so 75 or less catches them.)
3. **Questionable:** doesn't count (only `SIM_EXCLUDE_STATUSES`: Doubtful, Out, IR, PUP, SUS, NFI, DNR).
4. **Refresh before each window:** yes, "as long as it makes sense with Sleeper's API and how sync is set up". It does:
   Sync All already re-downloads the player file every tap (`forceRefresh`) and each league's roster (which carries
   your Sleeper starters), so the refresh *is* Sync All, run quietly through the same code. About 3 a Sunday (4:05 and
   4:25 share one window), plus Thursday and Monday.
5. **Stale rankings:** kept, as its own switch under the alert ("Also name old Weekly rankings", on by default, only
   used while alerts are on). It rides along in an alert that fires anyway, and on its own at most once a week.
6. **Survive a reload:** yes, a storage key is fine if it's small: `mls_starter_alerts_sent` is
   `{ week, sent: ['leagueId:playerId', …] }`, under 1 KB, started over each NFL week.
7. **Title flash and M10:** keep the title flash (it's in the browser's tab strip, for a hidden tab; M10's badges are on
   the app's own nav bar, seen only while the tab is in view). M10 should count both from the same "needs you" rule:
   noted in `docs/TESTING.md`'s Open follow-ups.

**What changed.**
- `js/shared/ui/notify.js` (new, both apps; N4 reuses it): `notifyPermission()`, `requestNotifyPermission()` (from a
  tap only), `notify({ title, body, tag, url, label })` (always `registration.showNotification()` with `data.url`; with no
  permission or no API: a toast if the tab is in view, else the title flash), `flashTitle()` ("(N) label" / "(N) page
  title" every second, both carrying the count so a hidden tab's once-a-minute timers still show it; put back on
  `visibilitychange`), `notifyNow()` and `notifyAt(ms, fn)` (a timer re-planned at most every 6 hours, for a laptop that
  slept). In `PRECACHE_ASSETS`.
- `sw.js`: a `notificationclick` listener: closes the notification, focuses a window already on `data.url`
  (`/lineup/`; `'/'` matches only Draft Strategist's `/` or `/index.html`), else opens it. `CACHE_NAME` v2.9.19 →
  **v2.10.0** (middle number: the service worker's own behavior changed).
- `js/mls/lineup/starterAlertRules.js` (new, pure): settings, kickoff windows from `State.gameTimesByTeam` (kickoffs
  within 30 minutes of a window's first share it), `dueWindow` / `nextCheck`, `sleeperLineup(league)` (Sleeper's starters
  in `starterSlots` order, slot names mapped to the app's: `SUPER_FLEX` → SFLEX, `REC_FLEX` → WRTE, `WRRB_FLEX` → WRRB),
  `noGameStarters`, `leagueFindings` (what to name, worded by S11's `lineupIssueItems`, so "Ja'Marr Chase is Out: start
  Puka Nacua instead?" reads as on the Lineup tab), `staleLeagues`, `alertMessage`.
- `js/mls/lineup/starterAlert.js` (new): the settings (`mls_starter_alerts`: `{ on, leadMinutes, staleRankings }`),
  the timer (`planStarterAlerts`: the next window's check time; at once if the page opens inside a window's lead time;
  then, after that window kicks off, the next), the check (`runStarterAlertCheck`: quiet Sync All, then S11's
  `getLineupIssues` on each non-Best-Ball league's Sleeper lineup, plus "has no game" and the stale line), and the
  Settings controls. Injured starters are named in their own game's window; a bye, no game or empty slot (no kickoff
  of its own) at the first check that sees it. A player locked in the app is left out (your call, as on the Lineup tab).
- `js/mls/render/dashboard.js`: `syncAllLeagues(btn, { quiet })` returns a promise that settles when the sync is done;
  quiet means no button, no summary toast and the Sync Logs left folded. A Sync All already running is awaited, not
  started twice. The button's behavior is unchanged.
- `lineup/index.html`: the Starter Alerts row under Show Player Headshots in Advanced Settings (a Feather bell,
  `currentColor`), and, while on, the lead-time drop-down, its hint, the stale-rankings switch and a status line
  (blocked, not allowed yet, or no notifications in this browser). `css/mls.css`: their layout.
- `js/shared/storage/keys.js`: `KEYS.mls.starterAlerts`, `KEYS.mls.starterAlertsSent` (both `mls_`, so Backup carries
  them and Factory Reset clears them). `js/mls/main.js` and `init.js`: the three change actions (`data-action`), and
  `initStarterAlerts()` at start-up.

**User-visible effect.** A **Starter Alerts** switch in Lineup Strategist's Advanced Settings, off until you turn it on.
Turned on, the browser asks for notification permission, and while `/lineup/` stays open on a computer (a background
tab is fine) an alert arrives the chosen time before each kickoff window naming starters in your Sleeper lineup who are
Out, Doubtful, on IR or bye, without a game, and empty slots, plus (optionally) leagues with Weekly rankings over 6 days
old. Tapping it brings the Lineup Strategist tab forward. Blocked or unsupported: a toast in view, "(1) Starter alert"
flashing in the browser tab's name while hidden. The Dashboard also gets fresh injury news and Sleeper lineups from the
pre-window Sync All.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/starterAlertRules.test.mjs` (settings, windows, due and next check, the Sleeper lineup, who is
named and once a week, the words), `tests/unit/swNotificationClick.test.mjs` (sw.js in a vm with stubbed `clients`:

## F17 — 2-QB leagues: the two QBs follow kickoff order

**Owner's decisions** (asked after reproducing, with a 375px before/after picture of the Lineup tab, 2026-11-12):
1. **The same top-to-bottom rule as RB and WR**: earliest kickoff in QB1.
2. Where the owner saw it: **League of Ordinary Gentlemen** (Keeper 2QB Half-PPR: QB 2, RB 2, WR 2, TE 1, FLEX 2,
   DEF 1), **week 10**: Jayden Daniels (WAS, Thursday night) in the lower QB slot below Brock Purdy (SF, Sunday 4:25).
   Nothing else looked wrong there (below).

**The bug, reproduced on main.** `optimizeFlexKickoffOrder` (`js/mls/lineup/kickoffOrder.js`) took QBs out of the
relabel unless the lineup had an open SFLEX slot (F1 kept a 2-QB league "as on main"). So a 2-QB league's QB1/QB2 kept
the rank-based fill's order, while RB1/RB2 and WR1/WR2 read earliest kickoff on top. Fixture league with a second QB
slot (QB 2, RB 2, WR 2, TE 1, FLEX 1): Allen (ranked ahead, Sunday night) stayed in QB1 above Hurts (1 pm).

**What changed and where.**
- `js/mls/lineup/kickoffOrder.js`: the QB-removal block is gone, so the QB slots take part like the RB, WR and TE
  slots: earliest kickoff first, ties and unknown kickoffs keep the fill order. Players whose game has started stay
  put; a manual lock moves (F13). The header comment says so.
- `sw.js`: `CACHE_NAME` v2.10.0 → v2.10.1 (after N2 merged; v2.9.21 before). CHANGELOG line under Lineup Strategist.

**User-visible effect.** With FLEX Kickoff Optimization on, a 2-QB league shows the earlier-kickoff QB in the top QB
slot. Who starts doesn't change. Superflex with an open SFLEX slot and 1-QB lineups are unchanged slot for slot. The one
other lineup that changes: two QB slots plus a SFLEX slot whose player has kicked off now orders its QB slots the same
way.

**Sleeper comparison.** `sleeperLineupChanges` compares sets of ids, so swapping QB1 and QB2 is never a change to set
(checked in the spec, with a control that a real difference does show).

**Tests.**
- `tests/unit/kickoffOrder.test.mjs`, new "2-QB leagues (F17)":
  - 2 QB with no SFLEX: Hurts moves to QB1. RB, WR and TE come out the same as main.
  - Ties and no kickoff data keep the fill order.
  - A QB whose game has started stays put. A manual lock moves.
  - 2 QB plus SFLEX, and SFLEX already played: as on main.
  - 500 random 2-QB lineups: main slot for slot, except the QB slots in kickoff order.
  - The old random test against main's function is now 1-QB only.
  - Three of these fail on main.
- `tests/mls-2qb-kickoff.spec.mjs` (new, both widths):
  - The QB order (fails on main).
  - A Sleeper lineup with the QBs the other way round shows no change to set.
  - With the toggle off, the QBs keep the rank order.

committed; week 10 kickoffs from ESPN's scoreboard). Each league's saved lineup was run through main's function and

## F20 — T-Score: the touch-target test that failed now and then (two links in The Research)

Found during F17 (PR #241): `touch-targets.spec.mjs`, "T-Score: every control has a 48px target" (phone), failed about
1 run in 30, on main too, with `a "CC BY 4.0"` losing its bottom edge to `a "ffopportunity"`'s hit area.

**Why it was intermittent (the cause).** The layout never changed; what changed was whether the tab was measured at
all. T-Score switches tabs without a View Transition (`switchTab` in `js/tscore/main.js` only moves the `active`
class), and `.tab-content.active` plays `fadeIn` (css/base.css), cut to 1ms where View Transitions exist, but it still
**starts at opacity 0**. `showTScoreTab` waits only for the class, so `measure` usually ran before the animation's
first frame: `checkVisibility({ checkOpacity: true })` saw opacity 0 and dropped **every control in the tab** (logged:
Research 0 of its 10 controls measured, and the same on Top-50, Values, Avoids, Sleepers and 2024; only In-Season, the
tab the page opens on, was measured). When a frame happened to pass between the class change and the evaluate, the tab
was measured, and the overlap (there every time: a probe found `ffopportunity` at the test point 40 of 40) was
reported. Not `scrollIntoView`, not the In-Season data load, not fonts (they're aborted in tests). Draft Strategist and
Lineup Strategist weren't affected: `showTab` waits for `data-vt-busy`, which outlasts the 1ms fade.

**The spec, now deterministic** (tests/touch-targets.spec.mjs, `check`): before measuring, it waits for every running
animation that ends (`getAnimations()`, finite end time; a spinner is left alone). On main with only this change, the
T-Score test **fails 100 of 100** (`--repeat-each 100`, phone), every time on Research's `CC BY 4.0`. Nothing else in
the three apps' tabs turned up (the other T-Score tabs, now measured for the first time, are clean).

**Owner's decision** (asked with the cause and the list of sentence links on every page): **(a) links inside a
sentence get no 48px area**, on all three pages (not T-Score only; not (b) the spec ignoring the overlap; not (c) more
line height, which would have needed about 48px from line to line instead of 29).

**Pages with the pattern** (every link at 375px, Guide folds opened), all directly in a `<p>` or `<li>`:
- Draft Strategist: the Guide's "Don't count this device".
- Lineup Strategist: the Guide's "Don't count this device" and Sleepy link, the Scoreboard's Sleepy credit.
- T-Score: In-Season's "How it differs from the preseason T-Score" and its credit (nflverse, CC BY 4.0, ffopportunity,
  CC BY-SA 4.0; T1 had already turned those areas off in css/tscore.css); The Research's "The Data" (the same five),
  "random article" and "Don't count this device".
- Only "The Data" had two links on neighbouring lines whose areas met (In-Season's credit would have, without T1's rule).
- Standalone links keep their area, none of them directly in a `p` or `li`: Ko-fi, "Powered by FantasyCalc", "ADP by
  Fantasy Football Calculator", "Read Methodology", the cross-app banners, the header's logo and "Back to Draft", the
  menu's links.

**What changed and where.**
- `css/base.css`, TOUCH TARGETS, right after the shared rule: `:where(p, li) > :where(a[href])::after { inset: 0; }`.
  Zero specificity, so a component's own `::after` still wins. **`inset: 0`, not `content: none`:** removing the
  pseudo-element made Chromium anti-alias the `)` right after the two "CC BY" links differently (85 pixels in each
  Research screenshot); dropping their `position: relative` as well didn't help. An `::after` at the link's own size
  leaves all 44 screenshots pixel-identical.
- `css/tscore.css`: T1's `.tscore-credit a::after { content: none; }` folded into that rule (a comment points to it).
- tests/touch-targets.spec.mjs: the animation wait above. `ALLOW` is unchanged (M16's): the sentence links fall under
  its existing `[data-inline-link]` entry, and a link that isn't in a sentence is still checked for 48px, so a
  standalone link put directly in a `<p>` or `<li>` would show up as short.
- docs/TESTING.md, Conventions, touch targets: the sentence-link rule and the animation wait. CHANGELOG: a line under

## S46 — When you last synced, on the Dashboard

**User-visible effect.** Under **Sync All Leagues** and **Optimize All Lineups** on the Dashboard, a small centered line
with a clock icon says when you last synced your Sleeper leagues: "Last synced 9:42 AM" (today), "Last synced yesterday
8:15 PM", "Last synced Sun 8:15 PM" (within the last 6 days) or "Last synced Nov 9" (with the year when it isn't this
year's), in the device's locale and time zone. Hovering shows the full date and time. It's muted grey normally and
amber when it's old (below). A league whose last sync failed is named after it in red with an alert icon ("Second
League's last sync failed"; two: "Last sync failed: A and B"; three or more: "Last sync failed in 3 leagues", all named
in the hover text). On phones the failed part wraps under the time. With no Sleeper league synced yet (no leagues, or
only manual / Draft Strategist hand-off leagues) there's no line. The Guide's legend line for the amber and red sync
labels now also explains when this line turns amber.

**Owner's choices (2026-11-12, from a sketch at 375 and 1280px; all four were the suggested options).**
1. **Where:** under Sync All and Optimize All, not in the "need you" strip (which hides when nothing needs you).
2. **Which time:** the most recent sync across your Sleeper leagues (manual and hand-off leagues don't count), naming
   any league whose last sync failed.
3. **Amber:** when a kickoff window starts within 3 hours and you haven't synced since 6 AM (local) that day; otherwise
   once the newest sync is over 24 hours old. Kickoffs are the week's game times the app already loads
   (`State.gameTimesByTeam`, grouped into windows by N2's `kickoffWindows`). With no game times (offline, ESPN down)
   only the one-day rule applies.
4. **Format:** today / yesterday / weekday within 6 days / date, as above.

  and its parts (`syncTimeText`, `staleReason`, `failedText`, `isSleeperLeague`), from each league's `lastSyncedAt` and

### U1, round 2: room on phones (owner's question, 2026-11-13)

The owner asked whether "cards in a box" (two layers of padding before any content) costs room on phones, and whether
Material 3 helps. Measured at 375px on the real app: text in a card starts 21px from the edge (333px wide); a Lineup row
28px (319), a Roster row 36px (303), folded sections and toggle rows 38px (299), sub-blocks inside a card (the
Simulator's parts, the Waiver Wire's results) 55px (265). Material 3's compact margin is 16px (343). Material 3: "Don't
force content into cards when spacing, headlines, or dividers would create a simpler visual hierarchy"; "Lists should
extend edge-to-edge in compact windows"; "consider swapping cards for lists" on compact screens; 16dp margins. Two
mock-ups (CSS injected into the real app; organization.md section 7, `organization/room-*.png`): **R1** one box (cards
stay, nothing boxed inside them: rows with dividers, sub-blocks a lighter tone) and **R2** sections on phones (R1 plus,
under 600px, full-width sections with 16px margins and Draft Strategist's player cards as list rows).

**Owner's decision.** **R2, built inside M14** (surface tones and corners), which already asks for mock-ups and re-takes
all 42 PNGs, so one visual card instead of two. M14's scope grows: under 600px `.container` loses its side padding and
`.settings-card` its side borders, corners and shadow (16px padding, an 8px band between sections); inside cards at
every width, rows (`.lineup-slot`, `.roster-item`, waiver results, league cards) become list rows with dividers and
folded sections, toggle rows and sub-blocks a lighter surface tone with no border; meaningful coloured edges stay as a
3px edge; Draft Strategist's `.player-card` becomes a list row under 600px. The exports (Lineup PNG, Export Team,
Export Recap, all html2canvas from the DOM) keep their look at any width. After U1's cards 1 to 3; S32 need not wait
for it.

**Runbook (published 2026-11-13).** Cards named for the runbook: **U4** (Dashboard and Scout tidy; after S45; weeks 12–13),
**A2** (Umami Tab, Tool and Section events; any time; weeks 12–13), **U5** (fold the Simulator, Trade Finder and SoS;
after S20; January), **U6** (jump chips; after U5, before M12; January); **M14** gains R2 (title, goal, ask, scope, done;
~30k tok) and runs after U4 to U6. A new track "Organization (U1)" and a top note. The edits are in
`docs/improvements/organization/runbook-u1-edits.py`, written against runbook version 1794512485-d1fd. This session's

### M17, round 2: the Draft Board runs to the edges again, and T-Score's folds match (owner, 2026-11-13)

The owner asked why T-Score got an exception and whether the Board had an edge-to-edge rule.
- **The Board was a regression of round 1.** css/mds.css's phone bleed (`.draft-board-container`, -0.5rem margins
  matched to `.container`'s old 8px) ran the grid to the screen's edges; ROOM ON PHONES's 16px margins for what isn't a
  card overrode it, so the grid sat inside 16px margins. Now the margin rule leaves the board out, and under 600px
  (css/mds.css, last rule) the board is the screen's full width with 16px of inner padding: it starts at the margin
  and scrolls to the edge. The bleed's -0.5rem would have scrolled the page sideways now that `.container` has no side
  padding. `room-on-phones.spec.mjs` checks it (x 0, 375px wide, 16px padding, the grid scrolls, the page doesn't).
- **T-Score matches (owner's choice).** Round 1 kept T-Score's framed folds with a T-Score-only rule; the owner chose
  one look across the site, so that rule is gone and T-Score's folds are the lighter shade with no border like the two
  apps'. T-Score keeps its 8px phone margins (ROOM ON PHONES needs the nav bar; not asked).
- **Screenshots** (re-taken by CI, below): phone `mds-draft-board` and `mds-empty-board` (the grid from 16px to the
  screen's edge); desktop and phone `tscore-inSeasonTab`, `tscore-researchTab` and `tscore-top50Tab` (2px shorter,
  folds lighter without a border).
- **A timing race, not a change:** CI's first try (run 43489877214) refused because desktop `mls-league-setup.png`
  changed too. After Sync, the button shows "Synced Successfully" (green) for 2.5s (`flashButton`), and `visual.spec`'s

### M17, round 4: Setup Progress is a section on phones; banners and the matchup strip stay framed (owner, 2026-11-13)

From the round 3 mock-up. The owner liked Setup Progress as a section, and asked whether Material 3 covers banners and
whether the strip stays clearly tappable without its frame. Checked on m3.material.io (rendered in Chromium): Material 3
has **no banner component** (its component list has Snackbars, Cards, Lists…; `/components/banners` is a 404; banners
were Material 2's). Snackbars are short updates at the bottom of the screen; a message that stays until you act is a
card in the content. A single-action surface reads as one by its container (a card's "primary action area"); a list
item's trailing icon "can communicate an action" only among other list items. So:
- **Built:** under 600px `.setup-checklist` has no frame, 16px padding and the 8px band (css/base.css, ROOM ON PHONES),
  like a section. It's content you work through, and its text gains about 40px.
- **Kept framed at 16px margins (owner's choice, agreeing):** the guide banner, Scout's Sleeper Sync banner, Draft
  Strategist's banners and the matchup strip. They come and go, and the frame says so; the strip's frame is what makes it
  read as tappable. 16px over 8px: the frame's edge lines up with every section's text (Material 3's compact margin).
- **Screenshots** (local render against round 3's): phone `mds-empty-setup`, `mls-empty-setup`, `mls-league-lineup`,
  `mls-league-roster`, `mls-league-setup`. Specs: room-on-phones, mds-setup, touch-targets pass.

## S36 — The Final Window: what rides on the last game of the week

**User-visible effect.** On the Scoreboard, when every player still to play in your head-to-head matchups is in the
week's last night window (Sunday night, or Monday's one or two games), a new section, **Final Window** (a moon icon),
sits above League Scoreboard and folds like the halves (remembered):
- **Its title line:** the games and kickoff, and how many matchups ride on them ("MIN @ CHI, KC @ DEN · Mon 7:15 PM ·
  3 matchups ride on them").
- **Four tiles** (two across on phones, four from 900px): **At stake** ("2 W · 3 live matchups"), **Expected** ("0.3 W ·
  middle 80%: 0–1 W"), **Best case** ("2 W · 3% of runs") and **Clean sweep** ("3% · all 2 at stake"). While the
  simulation runs they read "working it out"; if it fails, "couldn't run" and a line to tap Refresh.
- **What each matchup needs:** one card per live matchup (one column on phones, two from 900px), most uncertain first,
  settled ones last and dimmed: the league ($ if paid), the margin, "You 100.0 · Rival 102.0", a green/red win-chance
  bar with "26% to win", one line in words ("Down 2.0. **Justin Jefferson** needs 2.0+ more than **Harrison Butker**.",
  "Up 5.2. Hold **James Cook III** + **Jordan Mason** under 5.2 more.", "…: even a zero from X isn't enough",
  "…: anything from X does it"), who's live on each side with position badges, and, when exactly two players decide it
  (and it isn't settled), a table: "If A scores" Quiet: 0.0 / Projection: 8.3 / Big night: 10.0, against "B must score"
  "under 6.3", "2.5+", "anything" or "even a zero isn't enough".
- **Notes** under it: Best Ball leagues and leagues with no opponent are named, not counted; one line on how the runs work.
- A muted credit line under the Scoreboard card ("The Final Window was inspired by FF Historian, ffhistorian.com"),
  under Sleepy's, and the same credit at the end of the Guide's new Final Window item. The badge legend gains the
  win-chance bar.
- Nothing shows before the last window (Sunday afternoon, say), in a past week, or with no live head-to-head matchup.

**Owner's decisions (2026-11-13, asked before building, with sketches at 375 and 1280px).**
1. Name: **Final Window** (my recommendation; it fits Sunday night and two Monday games). Credit: **FF Historian,
   https://ffhistorian.com/**, in the Guide and under the Scoreboard, as S27 credits Sleepy.
2. When: **the last window, Sunday night too**: every live player's game in one night window (same day, US Eastern, at
   5 PM or later), so SNF counts when nobody you care about plays Monday.
3. Math: **one shared simulation** across every live matchup (players shared by matchups move together), with the four
   tiles as sketched.
4. The two-player table **in points**; stat lines stay with S37.

**What changed, and where.**
- `js/mls/week/lastWindow.js` (new, pure): `finalWindow` (the window from live teams, kickoffs and game states),
  `simulateWindow` (10,000 runs; one standard normal per player per run, shared by every league he's in, each league
  scaling it by its own mean and spread of his points still to come, floored at 0; a QB and his own team's WR/TE share
  part of it, the Simulator worker's 0.35, here across leagues), `certainResult`, `shareText`, `needsLine` (names
  escaped), `twoPlayerTable`. "At stake" leaves out matchups that are certain (only one side can still score and it's
  that side's) or settled in the runs (under 0.5% or over 99.5%, the Scoreboard's own rule); the other tiles count the
  matchups at stake.
- `js/mls/week/lastWindowWorker.js` (new): a module worker running `simulateWindow`. Measured: 10,000 runs × 15
  matchups take ~34 ms in Node and 75–100 ms in Chromium with the CPU slowed 4x, so it runs off the main thread (on the
  page as a fallback if the worker can't start). The card suggested the Simulator's worker; that one is a classic
  script, and a module worker importing `lastWindow.js` keeps the math in one place.
- `js/mls/sim/winChance.js`: the history fetch is shared (`historiesFor`), and `remainingProfiles` gives each live
  player's points still to come in each league's scoring (`getPlayerVarianceProfile`, less what he has; mid-game, the
  Simulator's shareLeft rule). Unlike the Simulator, a player with no history still counts (projection with the
  fallback spread), so a matchup is never dropped. `matchupWinChances` is unchanged in behavior.
- `js/mls/week/thisWeek.js`: `finalModel`, `addFinalWindow` (queued after the board's chances, only while the
  Scoreboard is open, rerun when scores, live players or game states change; Refresh reruns it), `finalHTML`; the
  `final` fold in the `mls_scoreboard_folds` key (comment updated in `keys.js`; no new key).
- `js/mls/badges.js` `finalChanceMarkup`, `js/mls/legend.js` (one line), `css/mls.css` (the `mls-fw-*` rules),
  `lineup/index.html` (the Guide item and the credit line), `CHANGELOG.md`, `sw.js` (the two files in PRECACHE_ASSETS,
  CACHE_NAME v2.10.4 → v2.10.5).

**Tests.** `tests/unit/lastWindow.test.mjs` (9): the window (two Monday games as one, SNF alone, an afternoon game
left, unknown kickoff, a final game), a sure win and a sure loss, a settled blowout, a shared player on both sides of
different matchups (every run 1 or 2 wins, never a sweep), two leagues' scoring moving together, the sweep and middle
80% over six coin flips, `shareText`, the needs lines (escaping), the two-player table (two yours, two theirs, one
each, none with one or three). `tests/mls-final-window.spec.mjs` (both widths): Monday night with MIN @ CHI and KC @
DEN left (S27's three fixture leagues, Butker's points set to 0): the section above League Scoreboard, its title, the
tiles, three matchups with their lines, the table, the settled one last without a table, the fold remembered, the
credit, nothing past the card; the worker blocked (the page runs it); Sunday afternoon, no section.
`mls-root-for.spec.mjs`: its credit check picks Sleepy's line by text (there are two now).

**Screenshots.** Rendered main and this branch in this container and compared them (`npm run pxdiff`): four change, by
design; the other 40 match main. The screenshot league isn't in a final window, so the section itself isn't in any.
- `desktop/mls-league-scoreboard.png`, `phone/mls-league-scoreboard.png`: the Final Window's credit line under Sleepy's.
- `desktop/mls-league-guide.png`, `phone/mls-league-guide.png`: the Guide's Final Window item and the legend's
  win-chance bar line.
CI re-takes these four (`update-screenshots.yml`, named in this round's commit message).

**Checks run.** check-precache OK; `node --test`: all pass but `tscoreInSeason.test.mjs`, which needs `npm ci` in tests/
(papaparse), as on main; Playwright: `mls-final-window`, `mls-root-for`, `mls-root-kickoff-find`, `mls-this-week`,
`badge-legend`, `touch-targets`, `tooltips-onscreen` pass (both widths). The full suite hasn't run yet: per rule 7 it
runs once, when the pull request is asked for.

**Left over.**
- In-game players use the Simulator's model (points so far plus the rest of his usual game); real live stats are S37.
- Best Ball is left out with a note, as in the Simulator (the open follow-up on Best Ball there applies).
- S37 (stat lines) builds on this: `remainingProfiles` and `finalHTML`'s matchup cards are where its lines would go.
- S20: `thisWeek.js` now imports `remainingProfiles` from `sim/winChance.js` too; load it through S20's loader with
  `matchupWinChances`.
- The window's "night" is 5 PM Eastern or later; a late-season Saturday afternoon game as the last window wouldn't count.

### S36, round 2: my review as a user, and the owner's "do all six"

   list, Still in play is one line instead: "Still in play: 2, in the Final Window above". Fold the Final Window and the
   list is back (the fold redraws the card); with a swing it doesn't cover, a Best Ball one say, the list shows as before.
2. **No twin tiles.** When the best case is a sweep, the third tile is **Most likely** ("0 W · 73% of runs", the most
   common number of wins) instead of a Best case that repeated Clean sweep. `simulateWindow` returns `likely` and
   `likelyShare`.
3. **The table reads more easily:** "you lose either way" instead of "even a zero isn't enough" in the "must score"
   column, and last names in its headers ("If Jefferson scores | Butker must score"; `shortName`). The sure-loss line
   above the cards keeps "even a zero … isn't enough", as the card asked.
4. **Settled matchups share one line** under the cards ("Settled: Second Fixture League (W, +42.2).") instead of a card
   each with a line like "Butker needs 42.2+ more than Jefferson".

   an (i) beside "What each matchup needs". The Guide says "the usual range (the middle 80% of outcomes)".
The kickoff in my screenshots read "Tue 12:15 AM" only because the test browser runs on UTC; users see their own time.

## F18 — Scoreboard: count Sleeper's auto-subs

**How Sleeper reports auto-subs (checked 2026-11-12).**
- **The setting** is `settings.max_subs` on each league (`GET /v1/league/<id>`): 0 = off, 1–3 = AutoSubs allowed per team
  per week. Two related keys: `sub_start_time_eligibility` (1 = "Require AutoSub To Not Play Before Starter": the sub's
  game must start at the same time as the starter's or later) and `sub_lock_if_starter_active`. In the owner's 21 leagues
  (2026): 17 have `max_subs` 1–3 (LOOG - Chop Shop also has `sub_start_time_eligibility` 1), four have 0 (LRD Cucks,
  2026 Late Round Charity League, Legacy Best Ball, Slow Mock Draft); `sub_lock_if_starter_active` is 0
  everywhere.
- **What it is** ([Sleeper help: How does Player AutoSubs work?](https://support.sleeper.com/en/articles/9731991-how-does-player-autosubs-work),
  read in full on 2026-11-13): "If a starter is inactive, the assigned sub will automatically move into the lineup." The
  commissioner turns it on in General League Settings → Player Auto-Subs and picks how many each team can use per week;
  managers set a sub per starter on the Swap Player screen (mobile app only; shown on web). Both games must not have
  started, and the sub must fit the starter's slot. "As soon as one player in the AutoSub pairing kicks off, both players
  lock." One sub per starter; no injury tag needed. Subs show in Sleeper's team and matchup views (yours and your
  opponent's). The page doesn't say when the swap is written. Sleeper added the start-time option later
  ([SleeperHQ on X](https://x.com/SleeperHQ/status/1824543398432223396)). The Footballguys thread sits behind a
  Cloudflare challenge, so it couldn't be read.
- **The public API** ([docs.sleeper.com](https://docs.sleeper.com/)) has no auto-sub endpoint or field. A matchup entry
  has exactly `roster_id`, `matchup_id`, `points`, `custom_points`, `starters`, `starters_points`, `players`,
  `players_points` (every entry of the owner's 21 leagues, weeks 1–10). Rosters carry no sub assignments either (their
  keys: `starters`, `players`, `reserve`, `taxi`, `settings`, `metadata` with notification switches, `player_map` null).
  So nothing names a swap, and nothing says which bench player is a starter's sub before it happens.
- **`points` is always the sum of `starters_points`**, in the same order as `starters`: 2,196 of 2,196 finished entries
  (weeks 1–9, all 21 leagues, Best Ball included). Sleeper's app counts the sub in the team score, so once Sleeper makes the
  swap, `starters` must already list the sub and `points` include him; the starter he replaced is a bench player.
  Not yet confirmed on a known swap (asked the owner for one).
- **Sleeper's own weekly recap:** not in the public API (confirmed on docs.sleeper.com: users, avatars, leagues,
  rosters, users in a league, matchups, playoff brackets, transactions, traded picks, NFL state, drafts, picks, players,
  trending). The runbook's answer stands.

**What the app does today.** Every Scoreboard view reads Sleeper's `starters` and the tile's score is Sleeper's `points`
(`custom_points` when a commissioner set it), fetched again when older than 2 minutes or on Refresh. No view adds up
starters itself, except Best Ball by design (`bestBallLineup`). So after Sleeper's swap the tiles, record, Still in play,
Root for / Against you and MVPs / LVPs / Started already count the sub. Before the swap (starter ruled out, his game not
started) the starter is left out as Out and the sub is a bench player.

**The owner's check (2026-11-13).** The mismatch the owner saw is gone when he looks again, so Sleeper's matchups catch
up with the swap after a delay. Where a delay can come from:
- Sleeper writing the swap (not documented; the starter has to be inactive, which is only certain at his kickoff).
- Sleeper's CDN: `GET /v1/league/<id>/matchups/<week>` answers with `cache-control: public, s-maxage=60,
  stale-while-revalidate=300`, so a response can be up to about 6 minutes old.
- The app: the Scoreboard re-fetches matchups older than 2 minutes (`FRESH_MS`, thisWeek.js; Refresh forces it). Nothing
  stores matchups across a reload (`State.lineupActualPoints` is in memory), and the service worker doesn't touch
  cross-origin requests.

**Owner's decisions (2026-11-13).** After the research the owner checked again and no longer saw the mismatch, so it was
Sleeper's matchups catching up with the swap, not the app. Of the options offered: **1, a regression test and one shared
rule, no visible change**. Not done:
- The "auto-sub" mark on the sub's row (asked in the card): the API never names a swap, so the app could only mark one it
  had seen happen between two of its own fetches. Dropped.
- Counting the sub as live before the swap (asked in the card): the API doesn't say who anyone's sub is. Dropped.
- Timing Sleeper's swap on a Sunday by fetching the owner's leagues around kickoff (research only): not now; auto-subs
  aren't that common and nothing would be built on it yet.
- A "Sleeper may auto-sub" note on an Out starter: not chosen.

**What changed, and where.** No user-visible change, so no CHANGELOG line, no legend line, no screenshots.
- `js/mls/week/playerRecap.js`: `starterIdsOf` (who counts as a team's starters: Sleeper's `starters`, or Best Ball's
  lineup) moved here from rootFor.js, beside `bestBallLineup`, with a comment on how Sleeper reports auto-subs. The MVPs &
  LVPs (Started, started zeros, LVPs) now use it instead of their own copy of the rule; the same result.
  `js/mls/week/rootFor.js` re-exports it. The card asked for the function beside `summarize` in scoreboard.js; it already
  existed in rootFor.js, and playerRecap.js is the place that avoids a circular import (rootFor.js imports
  `bestBallLineup` from it).
- `js/mls/week/thisWeek.js`: the tiles' and Still in play's sides read their starters with `starterIdsOf` (its own
  `starterIds` copy removed). S36's Final Window is built from those same sides, so it follows too.
- Totals: every tile shows Sleeper's `points` (`custom_points` when a commissioner set one). No view adds up starters
  itself, except Best Ball by design (its lineup is picked after the games).
- `sw.js`: `CACHE_NAME` v2.10.5 → v2.10.6 (above main's after merging S36); no file added.

**Tests.**
- `tests/fixtures/sleeper/make-fixtures.mjs`: `league-autosub.json` (Fixture League with `max_subs` 1),
  `league-matchups-autosub.json` (CeeDee Lamb inactive, Sleeper has put Amon-Ra St. Brown in his FLEX slot: 106.0–110.0)

**Left over.** Nothing for the app. If Sleeper ever adds an auto-sub field to the public API, the mark and the live

## S34 — Waiver claim or free agent: the Dashboard's upgrades say which, and when

**User-visible effect.** In Sleeper leagues, each player on a league card's **Best available**, on **Auto-Find**'s cards
and on **Check a List**'s free agents now carries a small chip after his rank: **FA** (grey outline: a free agent, add
him now, until his game starts) or **W** (amber: on waivers). A tap (or hover) says why and when, in the viewer's time
zone: "Waivers (FAAB) · runs Wed 12 AM: his game has started, so Sleeper locks him until the weekly run.", "Waivers
(FAAB) · clears about Sat 5 PM: dropped lately, …", "Free agent: add him now on Sleeper until his game starts (Sun 10
AM), no claim needed." On **Weekly**, an upgrade who's on waivers and plays before the claim runs is greyed with "too
late for this week", isn't counted in the card's "1 upgrade" (so the card can fold), and the position's next free agent
gets the upgrade check instead; other waiver players whose game is before the run are greyed too. On ROS he's marked W
but still counts (it's about the rest of the season). Manual leagues show no chip. A league synced before this card
has no waiver settings, so no chips until its next sync. The Guide's badge legend has two new lines.

**Owner's decisions (asked before building, with 375px sketches):**
1. **A chip on both** ("FA" and "W"), not my suggestion of W only.
2. **Muted and not counted** ("too late for this week"), my suggestion; and the next free agent at his position is
   checked instead.
3. **Auto-Find and Check a List** get the chip; **not Top Available** (nor the All Leagues search).

### Sleeper's rules, as the app uses them (sources)

Sources: Sleeper's help pages "After Game Waivers / Custom Daily Waivers" (support.sleeper.com/en/articles/3242468),
"Waivers for regular season & playoffs" (…/3978868) and "Why was my waiver time pushed back" (…/4042901), read through
a web search's summary (support.sleeper.com isn't reachable from this cloud session); and the owner's 21 leagues'
settings and their transactions for weeks 7–10 of 2026 (`api.sleeper.app/v1/league/<id>/transactions/<week>`, 10
leagues, ~600 moves), with kickoffs from ESPN's scoreboard.
- **`waiver_type`:** 0 rolling waivers, 1 reverse standings, 2 FAAB (only the FAAB leagues' claims carry a
  `waiver_bid`). The type doesn't change who's on waivers; the chip's tap text names it.
- **Game start:** a player is locked on waivers once his game starts, until the weekly run ("After Game Waivers":
  Sleeper's help says a Thursday player is "locked and on waivers until Tue After Day (or 12:05 a.m. PST on
  Wednesday)"). In the transactions, all 178 free-agent adds of a player with a game that week came before his
  kickoff (one apparent exception was a player who has since changed teams); Sunday adds stop at 10 AM PT, Tuesdays
  have only drops, and Wednesday has the big batch of claims.
- **The weekly run:** the day after `waiver_day_of_week` (2 = Tuesday, Sunday = 0, so Wednesday) at
  `daily_waivers_hour`, **Pacific time**: claims land at Wed 12:07–12:15 AM PT in the hour-0 leagues (daily or not),
  and at Wed 9:02 AM PT in REDRAFT Late Round Board of Directors (hour 9) and 9:05 in Legends of the Pocket Dynasty
  (hour 9). The app computes it in America/Los_Angeles and shows it in the viewer's zone.
- **Dropped players:** on waivers for `waiver_clear_days` days, each on his own clock: claims landed 47 h after the
  drop in 2-day leagues (Penix Wed 6:24 PM → Fri 5:31 PM; Dobbins Thu 5:08 PM → Sat 4:12 PM; Hurst Thu 10:15 AM → Sat
  9:22 AM) and 23 h in 1-day ones (Gainwell Wed 12:15 AM → Wed 11:15 PM). The app uses drop + N days and says "about".
  One exception: in REDRAFT a Tuesday drop cleared at Thursday's 9:02 AM daily run (49 h), so on some days a daily
  league waits for its run hour; that's the next item.
- **`daily_waivers` / `daily_waivers_days`:** daily processing on the days in a 2-bits-a-day mask (5461 = every day
  "1"; 1360, 6140, 10580, 10581, 10583 in other leagues). Sleeper's per-day options are "FA", "Locked" and "Waivers →
  FA". I couldn't decode the mask with confidence from the data (REDRAFT's 1360 matches Sunday-first days shifted by
  one, other leagues don't), so the app **doesn't use it**: it's stored, and only the game-start lock and the drop
  clock decide. Free-agent adds happen in daily leagues all week, so most unrostered players are free agents, as the
  card said.

### What changed, and where
- `js/mls/scout/waiverStatus.js` (new, pure): `waiverSettingsFrom(settings)`, `nextWeeklyRun(waivers, after)`,
  `waiverStatus(player, waivers, drops, kickoffs, now)` → `{ status: 'free' | 'waivers', clearsAt, tooLateThisWeek,
  reason: 'dropped' | 'played', atRun, kickoff, claimType }` (null when the app can't tell), `waiverStatusText`.
  Nothing is "too late" once the week's last game is over (about 4 hours after the last kickoff): the Wednesday run
  is before next week's games.
- `js/mls/scout/recentDrops.js` (new): each Sleeper league's drops from this week's and last week's transactions
  (S29's `getSleeperTransactions`), 4 leagues at a time, cached for the visit and re-read after a league syncs. On
  an error that league gets null: no chips, no toast (a console warning).
- `js/mls/leagues/sync.js`: `league.waivers` from Sleeper's settings, kept from the last sync if a response lacks
  them. It's on the league object, so Backup / Restore carries it (no new storage key).
- `js/mls/scout/bestAvailable.js`: the upgrade check per position walks past waiver players who are too late (Weekly
  only), lists them muted after the real upgrades, and draws the chip on every player. Drops load with the player map,
  projections and kickoffs; kickoffs count only when they're this week's.
- `js/mls/scout/waivers.js`: `waiverChipHTML` (the one helper), and `buildWaiverContext` gives `waiverStatusOf` to
  Auto-Find's cards; `js/mls/scout/engine.js` adds it to Check a List's free agents in a synced league.
- `js/mls/badges.js` `waiverChipMarkup`; `js/mls/main.js` `explainWaiver` (the tip as a toast, like SoS);
  `css/mls.css`; `js/mls/legend.js` two lines; `sw.js` (two new files, `CACHE_NAME` v2.10.8: F18 took v2.10.6 and M17 v2.10.7).

### Round 3: a second review as a user (owner: do 2–4, and check Sleeper's week)

   - **Sleeper's week flips on Wednesday at about 12 AM PT, with the weekly run, not on Tuesday.** Every transaction
     carries the week (`leg`) it was filed in. In the owner's 10 leagues (weeks 7–10, ~900 moves): week 7 ran from
     Wed 10/21 12:14 AM PT to Tue 10/27 11:44 PM PT, week 8 from Wed 10/28 12:13 AM PT to Tue 11/03 11:23 PM PT, week 9
     from Wed 11/04 12:20 AM PT to Wed 11/11 12:11 AM PT, week 10 from Wed 11/11 12:11 AM PT. Sleeper doesn't document
     the state endpoint's rollover (a web search found only "use display_week"); `state/nfl` read week 10 on Fri 11/13.
     So on Tuesday the app's week is the finished one, and its kickoffs are all in the past.
   - Two scheduled checks of `state/nfl` (Tue 11/17 8:30 PM PT and Wed 11/18 1 AM PT) confirm the endpoint flips with
     `leg`; their readings go here.

     locks (the week is over, and the claims are for next week). Left for the owner to place (here or its own card).

4. **No kickoff times, no chips.** If ESPN's scoreboard doesn't load, the app can't tell who has played, and "add

### Round 4: Tuesday's upgrades (owner: make the change in S34)

From the week's last game until Sleeper's week moves on (Wednesday about 12 AM PT, round 3), the Weekly checks treat

  Monday 5:15 PM PT game: from 9:15 PM PT). `waiverStatus` uses it too.

  a kickoff; your own locks still count). Best available passes it on Weekly; Auto-Find's `buildWaiverContext` too,
  and there a played player isn't "Played" or filtered out of Starting Lineup any more.

  explains FA / W and "too late".

  week until Wednesday), so on Tuesday a player on bye next week can still show as an upgrade. The rankings are
  whatever Weekly set the league has (often last week's until you upload the new sheet).

### Round 7: each league's daily waiver schedule (from the owner's Sleeper settings screens)

The owner sent the General Settings screens of LRD Cucks, Fantasy Leftovers and Legends of the Pocket. Against their
`daily_waivers_days` they decode exactly: two bits a day, read from the low end **Sunday, Saturday, Friday, Thursday,
Wednesday, Tuesday, Monday** (not Sunday-first, as round 6 assumed), with

| Code | Sleeper's label | Seen in |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Free Agency | LP Sun, LRD Sun |
| 1 | Waivers (Processing Time = `daily_waivers_hour`) | LP and FL Wed–Sat, LRD Mon–Tue |
| 2 | Locked | LP and FL Mon–Tue |
| 3 | Waivers until the hour, then Free Agents | FL Sun, LRD Wed–Sat |

Every other league's transactions agree in that order: Friday Night Beverages, Gridiron and Legacy Best Ball (10581)
are Locked Monday and Tuesday and Waivers every other day, as the owner said of Gridiron; Managers of the Round Table
(5460) is Free Agency Sunday only; REDRAFT (1360) Free Agency Saturday to Monday, Waivers Tuesday to Friday at 9 AM PT.
Claims also run at 12 AM PT when a Free Agency day starts (REDRAFT's Saturday and LP's Sunday 12 AM claims). Sleeper's
screens show times in the viewer's zone ("1 AM MST" = 12 AM PT). "After games waivers clear" is `waiver_day_of_week`:
None (0), 1 AM Tue (1), 1 AM Wed (2) ...; its time is 12 AM PT, then the day's schedule applies (LP's Wednesday is
Waivers at 9 AM, hence its 9:05 AM claims). `daily_waivers` 0 (weekly waivers): Free Agency every day, a run at the
after-games time.

`waiverStatus` now works from that:
- `dayCode`, `modeAt` ('fa' | 'waivers' | 'locked'), `afterGamesAt`, `nextRunAt` (pure, unit-tested).
- His own hold first (his game: until the after-games time; his drop: the clear days on his own clock; a cut: the
  after-games time), then the day's schedule: Free Agency → FA; Waivers or Locked → W until the next run, with the
  reason in the tap text ("A waiver day in this league: every pickup is a claim." / "Adds are locked today in this
  league."). A hold that ends on a Waivers day clears at that day's run.
- `nextWeeklyRun` (the Tuesday line) counts from the latest after-games time, so on Wednesday at 8 AM in a 9 AM
  league it's that morning's run.
- The Guide's W line and the Command Center's tooltip say "by the league's waiver schedule".
- The fixture league is now a weekly-waiver league (the specs' free-agent cases); a spec sets Friday Night Beverages'
  schedule.

Tests: unit (26): the day codes of the three screens and REDRAFT; LRD's Monday waiver day ("until Tue 12 AM") and

### Round 8: back-testing the rule against the owner's real adds and claims (a fifth review)

I replayed weeks 7–10 of 16 of the owner's leagues (Sleeper transactions, ESPN kickoffs) through `waiverStatus`:
for every free-agent add, would the app have said FA just before it; for every waiver claim, would it have said W
when the claim was placed, with "until" within an hour of when the claim actually ran. About 590 events. (Script kept
out of the repo: it reads the owner's league data.)
- **First run: 17 mismatches.** Fixed from what they showed:
  - **Weekly-waiver leagues lock everyone Monday and Tuesday.** No free-agent add on a Monday or Tuesday in League of
    Ordinary Gentlemen, How I Met Your Punter or Chop Shop (87 on other days); claims placed then, a bye week's defense
    too, ran Wednesday 12 AM. `dayCode` now gives a weekly league Waivers on Monday and Tuesday (claims at the after-games
    time) and Free Agency otherwise.
  - **A drop clears about an hour short of the full days:** 1-day drops were claimed or added 23 h 04 to 23 h 49 later,
    2-day ones 47 h 04 to 47 h 10. So a 12:11 AM drop makes the next day's 12 AM run (Kimani Vidal, Friday Night
    Beverages), which drop + 24 h missed by a day. Now drop + N days − 1 h ("about").
  - **A waiver day's run after his kickoff:** Tyson Bagent, claimed Monday morning in Managers of the Round Table
    (Monday a Waivers day) before a Monday-night game, ran Wednesday, not at Tuesday's 12 AM run: he locked at kickoff.
    Now a player on waivers by the day's schedule whose game starts before the next run clears after the after-games
    time, as a dropped one already did.
- **After: 8 mismatches of ~590 (98.6%).** Two claims placed in the first minutes of a run that still made it (12:01 AM
  into a 12:00 run); three players dropped in week 6, before the data starts (their drop clocks are invisible); one
  player who has since changed teams (the back-test uses today's team); and LRD Cucks' Seth McGowan, added as a free
  agent 6.5 h after a drop in a 1-day league, twice (unexplained; perhaps a player dropped the day he was added goes
  straight back to free agency, not checked).
- Tests: unit (29): a weekly league's Monday (a bye-week defense, claims Wednesday), Bagent's Monday-night lock, Vidal's
  12:11 AM drop; the drop-clock expectations an hour shorter. Spec: the "nobody dropped" case moves to Thursday (the
  tests' clock is a Tuesday, now a waiver day), and Tuesday's player with no game keeps a W. Ran `node --test` (669),
  check-precache and the Best available, waiver, Scout, past-trade, league-card and touch-target specs (77 passed). No
  screenshot changes.

### Left over
- **Seth McGowan's quick re-add** (round 8): if a pattern shows (a player dropped the day he was added skipping
  waivers), add it to the rule.
- **A short gap on a cold Dashboard** (round 5, point 2): if it matters, the count could wait for the chips.
- **Next week's byes on Tuesday** (round 4, above).
- `daily_waivers_days` isn't decoded (above). If a league marks some days "Locked" or "FA", the chip can be wrong on
  those days; a session with the league's settings screen open (or Sleeper's help pages reachable) could map the bits.
- Sleeper's state week may move to the next week before Wednesday's run; then this week's kickoffs are next week's and
  the "game started" lock isn't seen on Tuesday (drops still are). Small: nothing is "too late" then anyway.
- Top Available and the All Leagues search have no chip (owner's choice); `waiverChipHTML` and `ctx.waiverStatusOf`
  are ready if wanted. S35 (FAAB bids) can reuse `recentDrops.js`'s fetch and `league.waivers.budget`.
